Hos. 8.8. that is, of no use, and therefore not regarded; either because broken and cracked, or so tainted and polluted, that it is become altogether unserviceable. See the like. Psal. 31.12. Esay 30.14. Chap. 19.11.

*{wherefore are they cast out?}* Or, *thrown out:* as something, that being past use, and now good for nothing, is thrown away, or thrown out at doors, Mat. 5.13. See verse 26.

*{he and his seed}* Here is a question moved, how it is said, *he and his seed*, when as it may seem he had no issue; and is therefore entered upon record as one childless? verse 30. To which some answer, that he had issue, before he was carried away captive; but that they died in captivity, and so he became childless. So the Jewish commentators here. But against this, some of ours object; that if he had had any issue, mention would have been made of them, where relation is of those that were carried away with him, 2 King. 24.12,14. and they therefore by *his seed*, understand the children that he might have had, had God been pleased to bless him with issue. Others, by *his seed*, understand the whole race of Josiah, which, say they, he surviving Zedekiah, ended in him: but why the race of Josiah should be termed the seed of Jeconiah, is not made to appear. By *his seed* therefore, I conceive to be meant, the seed, or issue, which God foresaw that in captivity he should beget, and accordingly did, Mat. 1.12. said here to be *thrown out*, and *cast into a strange land* in him, because then in his loins; and by means of his deportation, bred and born in the same condition of captivity and exilement with him; as Levi is said to have been *tithed in Abraham*, Heb. 7.9,10. and as this people that lived in Jeremiah's days, are said, to have *gone after* God *in the wilderness;* and to have been *brought* by him *into the land* of Canaan, Chap. 2.2,7.

*{and are cast into a land which they know not.}* The word here used is not the same with the former: and howsoever in notion they come very near the one to the other; in regard whereof also the rabbine makes this member of the sentence no other than in divers terms the same with that before-going; yet there seems some difference here in the use of them: the former relating to the place out of which they were *thrown*, the latter to the place, into which they were *cast;* with an addition of that which contains some aggravation of their misery; that it should be into a strange place, the condition whereof, and their own there, would be the more uncertain, and where no friend, or acquaintance was like to be found. So Chap. 16.13.

**Verse 29.** *{O earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the LORD}* To give the stronger assurance of this dreadful denunciation, and to cause it to make the deeper impression in the minds of those that should hear or read this prediction; and the rather because this self-conceited, self-willed, and incredulous people could hardly be induced to believe that God would herein make his word good; God does by his prophet call with much intension and eagerness to have a solemn record made of it, as intimating that it should be as undoubtedly fulfilled, as if it were already accomplished, and the accomplishment of it entered into some public record; or that being entered upon record, it might remain there unto posterity, whereby the truth of it, upon the issue and event of it, might afterward appear: (see Job 19.23,24. Esai 30.8. Chap. 17.13.) and the *earth* therefore is called upon, as to take notice and bear witness of what, concerning such an instrument to be made, he here requires. vers. 30. But what is meant here by the *earth*, is some doubt made. Where to omit the Jewish doctors' descants upon the repetition of it; some, in regard of a distribution of the land of Israel into three parts; Judah, Galilee, and that beyond Jordan; others, of the land they were to go from, and the land they were to go to, and the land in the way thither. Whereas one of them well observes, that such threefold repetitions are not to note any divers matter, but to make the speech concerning the selfsame thing more emphatical and vigorous: as the like, Chap. 7.4. Ezek. 21.27. Some by the *earth*, understand the inhabitants of the world; the men of the whole earth indefinitely: as, *Let all the earth fear the Lord and let all the Inhabitants of the world stand in awe of him*, Psal. 33.8. others, the inhabitants of the land of Judah only; because they were the people that made doubt of it, and whom it most nearly did concern: so it should rather be rendered *land*, than *earth:* as, *all lands*, or *countries*, (that is, people inhabitants of all lands, or out of countries) *came into Egypt unto Joseph* to buy corn, Gen. 41.59. and so the rabbine last before-mentioned. Howbeit, others again, whom I rather go with, understand *the earth* itself to be spoken to, and called upon, as to hear, take notice, and be a witness of what hereafter ensues: as if he said, Let the earth itself so do, if none else will: the like compellations and contestations of *heaven* and *earth* hereunto, see Deut. 30.19. and 32.1. Esai 1.2. Chap. 2.12. as also of *a stone*, Josh. 24.26,27. and our Savior's speech of *stones*, Luke 19.40.

**Verse 30.** *{Thus saith the LORD, Write ye this man childless,}* Here follows that *word* which the *earth* was called upon to *hear*, vers. 29. not to *write*, but to *hear*, what is required to be written: for the word of *hearing* there, was feminine and singular; the word of *writing* here, is masculine and plural; and is indeed indefinitely here used: *Write ye* that is, *Let* this *be written;* that it may remain upon record to posterity. See on vers. 29. Revel. 14.13. So Esai 3.10. *Say ye to the righteous*, that is, *To the righteous be it said:* and, *Say to Archippus*, for, *To Archippus be it said*, Coloss. 4.17.

*{Write ye this man childless}* So is the word here used, taken, Gen. 15.2. and so is it rendered, Lev. 20.20,21. elsewhere in Scripture, save here, it is not found, the word in the original is deemed to signify, *a bare* and *naked*, or *a solitary* and *desolate* one. See on Chap. 17.6. where a word from the same root, and of the like notion, is found. The ancient Greek here renders it, *a man abdicated*, or *proscribed.* But we need not swerve from the common acception of the word. It sounds as if it were said; Enter this man in the roll, or records of the royal race, a childless man. The question is only, why he should be so termed. Some say, because he neither then had, nor was ever to have any issue; but remained childless to his dying day: as Michal, 2 Sam. 6.23. Howbeit, others rather understand it to be said of him, because none of his issue were to succeed him in the kingdom, and none therefore of his posterity to be entered as upon record in the roll of the royal succession: for that he had issue, seems apparent, by the mention made of his *seed* before, vers. 28. and hereafter again: as also by the genealogical relation, 1 Chr. 3.17,18. where several of his sons are expressly named; of the first whereof, to wit, *Salathiel*, the Evangelist also in as clear and pregnant terms as can be says, *After the Babylonian deportation*, or *after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel*, Mat. 1.12. which is the very same with that which is in the genealogical tables related, *the sons of Jeconiah Assir* (that is, *the prisoner;* implying, that the issue he had was begotten by him, and born to him in the time of his captivity.) *Salathiel his son, and Malciram*, &c. 1 Chr. 3.16. Nor is it unlikely, but that Jeconiah might have children in Babylon during the time of his captivity, (the captive Jews there being not restrained from the benefit of marriage. See Chap. 29.6.) if not before, yet especially, (though then well in years, about fifty and five old) when being by Evil-merodac enlarged, he lived in a freer condition than formerly; enjoying that constant portion by the Chaldee king assigned him in the court of Babylon. See 2 King. 24.27–30. which he held to his dying day. The rabbines indeed, to reconcile this prophetic, and that relation, say, that Jeconiah repented him of his evil courses, when he was in captivity, and that this sentence passed against him, was thereupon reversed. Which, though it be not altogether improbable, but that Jeconiah might do, as Manasses had done before him, and that God, as he restored Manasses then again to his kingdom, 2 Chr. 33.12–15. so he might give Jeconiah favor in the sight of Evil-Merodac, and so incline his heart to enlarge him; according to that, Psal. 106.46. But, because of this supposal, we have no sure ground, we shall not have recourse to any such uncertainty for the clearing of this doubt; neither is there any necessity at all for us so to do: since that God himself expressly here tells, why he would have such a record as is here mentioned to be entered concerning Jeconiah, to wit, not because he should die without issue; but as a man that should be successless in his reign, and with whom the royal dignity, in a manner, should die and expire.

*{a man that shall not prosper in his days}* For he had both a very short, and a very unprosperous reign. See 2 King. 24.8–16. *in his dayes*, for *in his reign:* as Esai 1.1. a defect of the relative, as vers. 6.

*{for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting on the Throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah.}* None of all his children shall ever so thrive, or prosper, as to rise to the royal state, and attain to the kingly government of Judah; for Zedekiah his uncle succeeded him in the kingdom for a few years, 2 King. 24.27. nor did any of his posterity attain to the royal estate, which expired in Zedekiah, Lam. 4.20. See the like of Jehoiakim his father, Chap. 36.30.

## CHAPTER 23

**Verse 1.** *{Woe to the Pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture, saith the LORD.}* This whole sermon or prophecy is mainly spent in menaces denounced: against bad rulers, vers. 1.8. false prophets, vers. 9.32. and profane people, vers. 33.40. The first part of it concerning bad rulers, consists of a threatening of the removal of them, vers. 1,2. and a promise of the restitution of God's people, principally to be accomplished in Christ, vers. 3–8. A learned writer supposes it to be a continuation of the prophet's relation of what had been before delivered by him in the reign of Jeconiah, concerning the abuses and corruptions that reigned among all sorts in his time; but of this his conceit, there is no great probability. See on Chap. 22.1.

*{Woe}* As Esai 5.8. Ezek. 34.2.

*{Pastors}* That is, *Rulers;* whether civil, or ecclesiastical; princes, or priests: for both ruled, Chap. 5.31. and 20.1. Heb. *feeders.* So Chap. 3.15. and 10.21. and 22.22. and 25.34. Ezek. 34.2.

*{that destroy}* See Ezek. 22.27. and 34.3. Zach. 11.4,5.

*{scatter}* By their cruel dealing and oppressions, Ezek. 34.4,21. Chap. 50.6.

*{the sheep of my pasture.}* Or, *my pasture-sheep;* as Psalm 100.3. those whom I take special care for; and had not turned out to graze on some bare common, in the wild waste, but had procured good pasture for, Psal. 23.1,2. Chap. 3.7. Ezek. 34.14.

**Verse 2.** *{Therefore thus saith the LORD God of Israel,}* Whose pasture-sheep the people of Israel are, Ezek. 34.30,31.

*{against the pastors that feed my people}* Or, *concerning* (as Chap. 12.14. and 22.6.) *those Shepherds*, (Heb. *feeders;* as verse 1.) *that rule*, (Heb. *feed.* as Ezek. 34.16. Mic. 5.4.) or, *that should feed*, (as, *learn*, for, *should learn*, Esai 26.9. but do nothing less, Ezek. 34.2,3,8.) or *that feed upon, my people;* that feed upon those whom they should feed, Ezek. 34.3.8,10. See on Chap. 22.22.

*{ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them:}* Or, *but* (as chap. 22.27.) *have not visited them;* you expel them, and drive them out of their dwellings; but you look not after them, nor take any course for their welfare, Ezek. 34.4,6,8,21. vers. 1.

*{behold I will visit upon you the evil of your doings, saith the LORD.}* Or, *I will punish you for your evil doings* as Exod. 31.34. there is an elegant *antanaclasis* in the various notion of the word, *visit;* which in Hebrew signifies sometime to *take care of*, and *provide* for, Ruth 1.6. Job 7.17,18. sometime, to *punish*, Exod. 20.5. & 34.7. Psal. 89.32. *I will visit you*, says God, *for your not visiting them.* I will visit you in wrath and indignation by taking of vengeance upon you, for your not visiting of them by taking care of them, making provision for them, and procuring their welfare, according to your duty, Ezek. 34.8,10.

**Verse 3.** *{And I will gather the remnant of my flock, out of all Countries, whither I have driven them,}* To the foregoing commination denounced against those bad rulers is subjoined, for the comfort of the faithful, a promise of recollection, and restitution of a remnant, after such dispersions as had been made of the main body of God's people, partly through the iniquity of those their rulers, and partly also in way of castigation by God himself for their sins. See the like, Esay 1.9. and 4.3. and 6.13. and 10.20,22. and 11.11,12. Ch. 3.14. and 12.14. & 16.15. & 31.7. Ezek. 20.40,41. & 34.11,12. Mic. 2.12. Zac. 10.3. see Deut. 30.1–5. Of the redundancy here, see Ch. 22.26.

*{and will bring them again to their folds;}* Or, *pasture;* for the word is singular; and it is used for *pasture.* Ezek. 34.14. to the places of their former abode in their own: and for *a dwelling* also the word signifies. Esay 32.18. and 33.20. Josh. 24.6.

*{and they shall be fruitful and increase}* Or, *multiply.* as Gen. 8.17. Exod. 1.7. Ezek. 36.11. See the like promises, Esay 44.3,4. Chap. 31.27. Zach. 2.4.

**Verse 4.** *{And I will set up shepherds over them, which shall feed them}* Heb. *feeders;* as before, ver. 1. *and they shall feed them:* not feed upon them as the former did, ver. 2. the copulative for the relative; as Chap. 17.6. fulfilled in Nehemiah, Zerobabel, and other faithful governors of the Jewish people, after the captivity, that sought not themselves, but the good and welfare of God's people, Neh. 2.10. & 5.14–19. Hag. 2.23. Zach. 4.9. & 6.10,14. as also in Christian princes and rulers under the Gospel. See Ch. 3.15. So Ezek. 34.11,12.

*{and they shall fear no more nor be dismayed}* They shall dwell in safety, and good security; free from fear of any adversary, So ver. 6. Chap. 28.25,26.26. & 34.30. See the same terms, 2 Chr. 20.15,17. and 32.7.

*{neither shall they be lacking, saith the LORD.}* None of them shall be missing, whom God will have saved and reserved for a remnant. See Esai 27.12,13. So is the word used, Numb. 31.49. 1 Sam. 25.7,15,21. 2 King. 10.19. Esai 34.16.

**Verse 5.** *{Behold the days come, saith the LORD, that I will raise to David a righteous branch,}* Heb. *behold* (so are the prophecies concerning Christ usually ushered in, to stir up unto attention and due consideration. See Esai 7.14.) *the dayes coming* (as vers. 7. Chap. 16.14,18.) *and* (as Chap. 9.25.) *I will raise*, or *set up*, (as vers. 4. for the term is the same) or, *settle*, (and establish; for so also the word may signify, as Gen. 6.17.) *to David*, or *for David*, (of his issue to succeed him in the government of my people, Psal. 132.11. Chap. 33.16.) *a righteous branch*, or *bud*, or *sprout;* for the Hebrew word signifies no other: and that great learned man therefore, who requires to have it here rendered with the Septuagint, *the Sun-rising;* and with much confidence condemns them all that render it so as we do after some of the Greek, the old Latin, and other later versions in several languages, of *unskillfulness*, and going *against the word of God*, should have had better grounds, than any that he has produced, for so severe and peremptory a censure: sure it is, that they go besides Scripture, if not against it, that otherwise expound it; the word itself being nowhere found therein used but of plants, or with reference unto them, the root also that it springs from never applied but to plants, or to hair, that sprouts out from the body, as plants and herbage from the ground, and in metaphorical forms, with allusion to the one, or the other. Now this passage another learned late writer expounds of Zerobabel: and we deny him not to be of the *shepherds*, or *rulers* before-mentioned, vers. 4. but the party here described is distinguished from them, nor can be any other than our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. Yea, the Jewish doctors themselves, both on the place, and elsewhere, acknowledge, that by the *bud* or *branch*, or *sprout*, here spoken of, is meant *the Messias.* Though they add withal some vain devices of their own, to confirm the same to wit because, say they, the letters of the word *Menachem* that signifies *a Comforter*, and is the name of the Messias, Lam. 1.16. and the letters of the word *Semach* here used, do both make up the very same number to wit, 138. But this is but a frivolous fancy of theirs; nor does the truth of God need such sandy supports. Thus is he styled, as here, so also Zach. 3.8. because he was to spring up, as *a Bud, Branch*, or *Sprout*, from *the root of Jesse*, and *of David*, Esai 11.1,10. Rev. 5.5. and 22.16. though in regard of his meanness and weakness to outward appearance, like some young *bud*, or tender *shoot*, at its first sprouting out, Esai 53.2. yet that should, in process of time, *bud*, *sprout* and *branch* out, like some such plant, as retains its verdure perpetually, flowing and flourishing unto all eternity, Psal. 132.11,18.

*{a righteous branch}* As Chap. 33.15. *a branch, bud*, or *sprout of righteousness;* so termed, not only, because he is perfectly *righteous* in himself, *that righteous one*, Act. 7.14. *that holy and righteous one*, Act. 3.14. *the Holy of Holies*, Dan. 9.24. but also because he *maketh multitudes righteous;* he makes *all his people righteous* like himself, Psal. 27.7. Esai 53.11. and 60.21. Rom. 5.18,19. 1 John 3.3,7. And it is as if the prophet had said, Be you not dismayed, when you see so many wicked rulers of David's posterity for their wickedness removed, so many of them, as degenerate and rotten buds, or branches, cut off and cast away, without hope of recovery, Chap. 22.10,11,18,19,24,30. Lam. 4.20. God in the room of them will raise up *a bud*, or *branch* of the same stock, that shall be therein altogether unlike unto them, shall not only be most just and righteous himself, but shall administer justice equally unto all, and make others also therein like unto himself. See the like prophecies and predictions of Christ and his kingdom, Esai 4.2. and 40.11. and 45.8. Chap. 33.14,15.

*{and a King shall reign and prosper,}* Jesus Christ, *the King of Israel*, Joh. 1.49. the true *Melchisedek, the King of righteousness.* Heb. 7.1,3. yea, *the King of Kings*, 1 Tim. 6.15. Rev. 19.16. he shall *reign and prosper;* that is, *reign prosperously*, or *prosper in his reign:* unlike therein to Jeconiah and his seed, Chap. 22.30. he shall be successful in all his undertakings, Psal. 45.4. Esai 52.13. and 53.10. Rev. 6.2.

*{and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.}* Or *upon the earth*, as Chap. 31.22. Mat. 6.20. he shall execute judgment throughout the whole world, Psal. 96.13. and 98.9. Esai 2.4. or *in the land;* as Esai 5.8. Ezek. 9.9. vers. 8. among his people: as is said of David, 2 Sam. 8.15. 1 Chr. 18.14. a type of Christ; therefore also called *David*, Ezek. 34.23,25.

**Verse 6.** *{In his days Judah shall be saved,}* For he shall save his people from their sins, and rescue them out of the hands of their enemies, spiritual especially, and deliver them from this wicked world, Esai 33.22. and 63.1. Mat. 1.21. Luke 1.74. Gal. 1.4.

*{and Israel shall dwell safely,}* Heb. *in*, or *unto confidence;* that is, securely, confidently; as Judg. 18.7. Lev. 26.5. So Deut. 33.12,28. Ezek. 34.25,27,28. *Judah* and *Israel* here, one and the same, God's people. So Chap. 33.16. where the same thing is repeated.

*{and this is his name whereby he shall be called, The LORD our righteousness.}* Heb. *this is his name whereby he shall call him, Jehovah tsidkenu:* he *shall call him;* that is, say some, *God shall call him.* Others, *Israel shall call him.* Others again, *each one shall call him:* and the word is here indefinite; and it therefore, as in our version, best rendered by the passive; *he shall be called.* But some question is made, whom this title is here said to be given unto: and some would have it given to God's people, to Israel. So it should be rendered, *Jehovah*, or the *Lord* is *our righteousness:* as, the name of the new Jerusalem, *Jehovah-hammah;* the *Lord*, or *Jehovah* is *there*, Ezek. 48.35. and it may not unfitly be given unto Israel, whose *righteousness* Christ is, 1 Cor. 1.30. being made one with him, 1 Cor. 6.17. and 12.12,13. and professing to have their *righteousness in* and *from* him, *in whom all the seed of Israel are justified*, and *do glory*, Esai 45.24,25. that which by this title they should acknowledge. But others rather, and so the most and best conceive it to be the name of Jesus Christ the Messias, as *Immanuel, God with us*, Esai 7.14. So, *Jehovah Tsidkenu;* *Jehovah*, or *the Lord, our righteousness:* who, as he came *to bring in everlasting righteousness*, Dan. 4.24. So. *he is by God made unto us righteousness*, 1 Cor. 1.30,31. while by his being *made by God sin* (that is, *a sin-sacrifice*, as Heb. 9.28.) for us, *who had no sin* himself, *we become the righteousness of God in him*, 2 Cor. 5.21.

**Verse 7.** *{Therefore, behold the days come, saith the LORD, that they shall no more say, The LORD liveth, which brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt:}* Or, *Furthermore*, or, *Moreover:* for so the coherence of this with the former, (and the subject matter of either being duly considered) requires the particle here to be rendered, which Chap. 16.14. (where the very same thing was before recorded) is upon the like ground, another way rendered: for these terms of connection do frequently alter their notion according to the relations, that the members, or passages of the discourse, which they come between, have one to another.

*{they shall no more say}* Or, *it shall no more be said;* as it is, Chap. 16.14.

**Verse 8.** *{But the LORD liveth, that brought up, and which led the seed of the house of Israel, out of the North Country, and from all countries, whither I had driven them, and they shall dwell in their own land.}* See the same in effect, Chap. 16.15.

*{which led}* Or, *brought* Heb. *made to come* as Chap. 2.7.

*{the seed of the house of Israel}* A remnant of them, v. 3. that should be as *a seed*, Esai 1.9. and 6.13. and 65.9. Rom. 9.29.

*{I had driven them}* As vers. 3.

*{and they shall dwell in their own land}* Or, *that they might dwell* (as John 2.4,9.) *in their own land.* Heb. *on* (as Esai 24.22.) *their land.* So, *their own heart*, v. 16.

**Verse 9.** *{My heart within me is broken because of the Prophets}* Here, from the princes and rulers before dealt with, ver. 1,2. the prophet passes to the priests and prophets, whom he taxes as the principal authors of that general corruption that was so rife among the people: and threatens them therefore with some dreadful judgment to be inflicted upon them for the same.

*{My heart within me is broken}* Heb. *As for*, or *Concerning the Prophets*, (as Esay 32.1. See there) *my heart in the midst of me* (as Psal. 22.14. and 39.3. and 55.4.) *is broken:* as Psalm 51.17. Esay 65.14. Thus the prophet expresses his extreme grief of heart, to consider how the false *Prophets* (for such he here means, as c. 4.9.) did deceive, delude, and mislead the people, to the utter ruin of them both. See c. 14.13,16.

*{all my bones shake}* With extremity of fear and trembling, to think what will befall them. See the like, Hab. 3.16. the word signifies properly to *hover* or *flutter*, as a fowl does over her young, Gen. 1.2. Deut. 32.11. in which places, and here, it is only found, and so is the heart wont oft to do, to flutter as a bird, in fainting qualms, or sudden vehement fears. See Psalm 38.10. Chapter 4.19.

*{I am like a drunken man, and like a man whom wine hath overcome}* Not able to stand on my legs, so astonished; or as one at his wit's end, not knowing what to do: as Psalm 107.27. Esay 24.20.

*{and like a man}* Or, *even;* as Chapter, 15.13. and 19.12.

*{whom wine hath overcome}* Heb. *passed over him*, as we use to say, one that is *in drink*, or that is *drowned in drink;* as overwhelmed with it: in like manner as *waves* and *billows* are said to *pass over* one, that is not on, but in the sea, Psalm 42.8. Jon. 2.3. and the pronoun demonstrative in place of the relative, as Esay 42.1. and 46.4.

*{because of the LORD, and because of the words of his holiness.}* Or, *his words of holiness: his holy*, or *most holy words:* as Psalm 105.42. that which the Jewish commenter expounds of the words of the false prophets, who had the name of God, and the word of God, continually in their mouth, as if whatsoever they delivered, were no other than God's oracles, verse 17.31. So the prophet's meaning should be, that he was affected and transported with grief and dread, to hear God's name so horribly abused by them, fathering their lies upon him, and strengthening men thereby in their rebellions against him, verse 17. Ezekiel 13.19,22. But the most rather understand it of God himself, his wrath hereby incensed, and words of dreadful menaces thence proceeding, and expressing the same by denunciation of such hideous effects of it, as were shortly to ensue, So Hab. 3.16. Heb. *from the face*, or *wrath of the Lord*, as Psalm 34.16. or, simply, *because of the Lord;* as in the next member and ver. 10.

**Verse 10.** *{For the land is full of adulterers,}* So Chap. 5.8. and 9.2. either while the false prophets connive at them, and preach nothing but peace to them, verse 22.30. or because by promising of peace unto them, they encourage them to loose and licentious living, v. 17. Ezek. 13.22.

*{for because of swearing the land mourneth}* Because of oaths and perjuries that are so rife in it. So the Chaldee, whom the Jewish doctors follow; and so the ancient Greek seems to have had it. It is word for word, *from the face*, or, *because*, (as verse 9.) *of the curse*, which they therefore so render; because *oath* and *curse, swearing* and *cursing* go commonly together, Levit. 5.1. Judges 17.2. 1 Kings 19.2. Neh. 10.29. Ezek. 17.18. Howbeit the old Latin, and divers others of the best note, retaining the express term render the text: *for because of a curse the land mourneth;* that is, by reason of the curse of God upon our land, in such manner as follows, the land mourns, as Chapter 12.4. and 14.2. So, *the curse hath devoured the land*, Esay 24.6. and I suppose it to be as well the genuine, as the plainer sense; only I should render it, *though by reason of a curse the land mourn:* as if he had said though manifest expressions of God's displeasure be already upon us, and the land by means thereof seems to wear a mourning weed, as is apparent to the eye, yet it is full of abominable filthiness; and these wicked wretches still tell them, that all shall go well with them, Chap. 6.14. and 8.11. and 14.13. There is an elegancy in the sound of the words of *malediction* and *mourning;* and between it again, and the term of *filling* in the former member, neither of which, our English can fitly express: the use of the particle in this discretive notion, is very frequent, as Gen. 8.26. Josh. 17.18. Psalm 23.4.

*{the pleasant places of the wilderness are dried up.}* This seems to be a knitting of things repugnant together, for what *pleasantness* can be looked for in a wild waste, or a *wilderness?* Some therefore render it, *the habitations*, or, *habitable places of the wilderness;* that is, of the wilder, and less peopled part of the land, called *the wilderness of Judea*, Matth. 3.1. But the words would rather be rendered, *the pastures of the wilderness*, or, *of the plain;* for so the word rendered *wilderness* oft-times signifies, See Esay 63.13. Lamentations 4.19. and the former word here joined with it, is rendered *pastures*, Psalm 65.12. & Joel 2.22. and so should be rather than *habitations*, Chapter 9.9. And this is that wherein the curse before mentioned did consist, to wit, in a great drought that had dried up their pastures; that is, say the Jewish commenters, the places where beasts feed. See Chapter, 14.1,2.

*{and their course is evil}* Word for word, *their race*, See Chapter, 22.17. from whence some also render it, *violence* here: but I rather take it as our version renders it, *their course* (by that very word, one of the rabbines here expounds it) *is naught;* only I should otherwise render the prefixed particle in a notion of reddition, as reflecting upon, or having reference unto the words before-going; *yet* (as Chapter 14.9,15.) *their course is naught*, or, *evil;* though God's curse be upon the land, and his hand thus upon them, yet they will not learn to amend their ways, Esay 26.9,11. Chapter 5.3. but run on still in a wicked course, and refuse to be reclaimed, Esay 59.7. c. 8.6.

*{and their force is not right}* Heb. *their might*, or *valour*, (as Esay 3.25. and 63.15. c. 49.35.) *is unlike.* So the old Latin, following the Greek, that renders it *such*, to wit, evil and naught, as their course before; or, as they expound the Latin, *unlike* to God's prescript, *not such* as it should be, because the word sometimes signifies *so*. or, *such*, Psalm 1.4. Prov. 1.19. the Chaldee renders it, *they shall not prosper by their might;* having an eye, I suppose, to a speech used of Moab to that effect, where this word is used, Esay 16.6. Chap. 48.30. but I conceive that our version is here in the right, and has approbation from the Jewish commenters, who for the exposition of it, point us to that in Moses, Num. 27.7. *the daughters of Zelophehad speak right*, to which may be added, Prov. 15.7. *the heart of the foolish* casts abroad (supplied from the former branch) that which *is not right.* But we need not go far, to find out the prophet's meaning here, two places of his put together will fully explain him; the one, chap. 8.6. *no man spake aright*, or, what *was right;* the other, chap. 9.3. *they bend their tongues like their bows for falsehood, but have no courage*, or, *are not valiant* at all *for truth*, or *right;* that which is said here; their courses are stark naught, nor is their courage or valor shown for ought that is right, but rather employed wholly the contrary way; they run on in a violent course unto evil; and bend themselves with all their might thereunto, Psalm 36.4. Chapter 9.3.

**Verse 11.** *{For both Prophet and Priest are profane}* Heb. *Prophet also, Priest also*, or *even Prophet, even Priest*, are both *profane*, or, *deal profanely;* for though the nouns are singular, (but collectively taken: as, *from the Prophet to the Priest*, Chap. 6.13.) yet is the verb plural, to include both; and is here aright rendered, having in it a notion of *profaneness;* not of *hypocrisy*, as is too oft given it; and as some of prime note render it here, *play the hypocrites*, See on Esay 9.17. and 32.6. It is as if he had said, No marvel, if the corruption be so general in the land, when the teachers, as well those that are set over them by God to instruct the people, Mal. 2.7. as those also that profess and pretend to be sent by him on messages to them, do both by their bad lives, and false relations, lead them into loose courses, and confirm them therein. See ver. 14,15.

*{yea, in my house have I found their wickedness, saith the LORD.}* Heb. *also*, or, *even.* (as before) *in my house.* My very temple itself is not free from, but full of their abominable superstitions and idolatries, and horribly profaned with their lewd and loose practices, which they forbear not to perpetrate even there in my presence, 2 Chronicles 36.14. Chap. 7.10,11. Ezek. 7.20. and 8.5,17. See verse 14.

**Verse 12.** *{Wherefore their ways shall be unto them as slippery ways in the darkness, and they shall be driven on, and fall therein.}* Heb. *Therefore their way shall be unto them as a way of slipperinesses in the dark*, or, *in a mist.* It shall fare with them, as with one that is constrained to travel in the dark, or in a thick mist, where he cannot discern his way, and in some slippery way, where though he could see it, yet he should find no sure or firm footing; and withal so put forward, and driven on by those that either push him on; or pursue him close at his heels, that he can neither make any stay and stand still, nor slacken his pace, nor take time with his foot to feel and try his way before him; but must of necessity, being so put upon with all these disadvantages, run on headlong, until he fall and miscarry: an emblem, to the life, of unavoidable miscarrying. See the very like, Psalm 35.6.

*{their way shall be unto them}* An elegant redundancy: as, *my deliverer unto me*, Psalm 144.2. and, *their pathes they have made crooked to them*, Esay 59.8.

*{as slippery ways}* Or, *as a very slippery way.* Heb. *slipperinesses:* the word signifies sometime, *smoothnesses*, (for in the singular it is not read) and so it is used for *flatteries*, Dan. 11.21,34. And because smooth things are commonly *slippery;* hence it is that it comes also to signify *slipperinesses;* and so here otherwise a smooth or even way is a matter desirable, Esay 26.7. and 40.3,4. and *slipperinesses*, for, *a way* of *slipperinesses*, (the word *way*, supplied from the former member; as Deut. 32.4. *all his wayes are judgement*, that is, ways of *judgement*) that is *a most slippery way.* So Psalm 35.6. as also *slipperinesses*, for *most slippery* places, Psalm 73.18. for these plurals are in Hebrew much used to enhance and improve. See Esay 58.11. and 59.9. c. 14.1.

*{in the darkness}* Or, *in the dark;* as Deut. 28.29. Prov. 7.9. or *in a mist;* as Exod. 10.22. See Esai 8.22. so that they cannot see to choose their way, nor discern ought that may lie to endanger them in their way, nor know which way to turn themselves, Esai 8.22. and 59.9. Prov. 4.18. Chap. 13.16. John 11.10. 1 John 2.11. Some render the words, not, *in a mist;* but, *as a mist;* and these two particles, in Hebrew, are for shape much alike; but the originals exhibit that, not this; and the Jewish commenters so read it.

*{driven on}* So Esai 8.22. Psal. 35.6.

*{and fall}* Or, *untill they fall;* being pushed forward (Ps. 118.13.) until they do fall. So is the copulative used, Dan. 12.12.

*{for I will bring evil upon them}* So Chap. 6.19. and 11.11. and 19.3,15.

*{even the year of their visitation, saith the LORD.}* Or, *in the year of their visitation;* as Chap. 46.21. When in wrath I come on visiting of them, vers. 2. So Chap. 11.13. and 48.44. and 50.27.

**Verse 13.** *{And I have seen folly in the Prophets of Samaria:}* Or, as some render it, *I saw indeed* (when time was) *folly;* so it is rendered, Job 1.22. and 24.12. or, as some render it, *absurdity*, or, *an absurd thing.* Heb. properly, *insulsity*, or, *unsavoriness:* a metaphor taken from meats, that for want of salt, being unsavory, are offensive to the palate, Job 6.6. See the like metaphor, Ephes. 4.29. compared with Col. 4.6. it is applied to the false prophets' fictions, Lam. 2.14. and to their ill-tempered daubings, Ezek. 13.10,11,14,15. and 22.28. *in the Prophets of Samaria:* those of the ten tribes, whereof Samaria was the head city, Esai 7.9.

*{they prophesied in Baal, and caused my people Israel to err.}* They delivered their prophecies not in my name, but in the name of Baal; and so caused my people to go after Baal. See 1 King 18.18,21. and 22.6,7. *Israel*, those of the ten tribes; as Chap. 3.6.

**Verse 14.** *{I have seen also in the Prophets of Jerusalem an horrible thing:}* Or, *But* (Heb. *And;* as Chap. 22.5,27.) *in the Prophets of Jerusalem I see fedity*, or *fetidity;* *filthiness*, or *stench;* most vile and abominable practices, far worse in some kind, than in those of Samaria. See Chap. 5.30. and 29.17. Hos. 6.18.

*{they commit adultery}* Do as Eli's sons did, 1 Sam. 2.17,22. whence adultery became so rife in the land, vers. 10.

*{and walk in lies}* Or, *walk* up and down *with lies.* Heb. *with falsehood*, or *a ly;* as Esai 28.15. they utter their lies not in Baal's name, but in mine, and so father their lies upon me, Chap. 14.14. See vers. 26. Heb. *committing adultery, and walking with a lie;* that is, at full, *committing* they *commit adultery; and walking*, they walk about *with lies;* they make a common trade and practice of either: a form, though defective, yet very significant. See on Esai 59.11,13. See these two vile practices joined together in the false prophets again, Chap. 29.23. For those that here restrain the term of *adultery* to idolatry, spiritual adultery, seem therein to wrong the text.

*{they strengthen also the hands of evil doers, that none doth return from his wickedness:}* Heb. *and they strengthen the hands of evil doers, that they may not return, a man* (that is, *each one;* as Ch. 22.7. or *any one;* as Chap. 5.1.) *from his wickedness.* They confirm them in their wickedness, and so keep them from repentance, by bearing them in hand that they shall do well enough, whatsoever God's messengers tell them, though they do continue in their sins. See Ezek. 13.22.

*{they all are become to me as Sodom, and the inhabitants thereof as Gomorrah.}* By their means it is come to pass, that this city of Jerusalem is become as another *Sodom*, and the inhabitants thereof as the inhabitants of *Gomorrah:* for so it is to be supplied; as *way*, vers. 12. See Deut. 32.32. Esai 1.10. *to me:* either an elegant redundancy; as Chap. 12.8. See there, and before, vers. 12. or *to me;* that is, in my account: as Amos 9.7. I make no other reckoning of them, than as of those abominable cities, Ezek. 16.46.

**Verse 15.** *{Therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts concerning the Prophets;}* Or, *these Prophets:* for the article is here restrictive, and demonstrative; as Chap. 27.7. the prophets before deciphered.

*{I will feed them with wormwood, and make them drink the wine of gall:}* Or rather, *I will feed them with poyson, and drench them with juice of hemlock*, or *wolfs-bane.* See of the terms here used on Chap. 8.14. and 9.15.

*{for from the Prophets of Jerusalem is profaneness gone forth into all the land.}* See before, ver. 11. for *hypocrisy*, put in the margin, has no place at all here.

**Verse 16.** *{Thus saith the LORD of hosts, Hearken not unto the words of the Prophets that prophesy unto you:}* So Chap. 27.9,14,16,17.

*{they make you vain:}* Or, *beguile you.* Heb. *they are making you vain:* it is their practice to delude you; while they feed you with vanities, and make you trust in vain things that will fail you in the end, and so make you vain, as all such are, that follow after, and rely upon ought that is vain. So 2 King. 17.15. Psal. 62.10. Chap. 2.5. Rom. 1.21.

*{they speak a vision of their own heart and not out of the mouth of the LORD.}* They vent the devices of their own heads and hearts, not ought that comes from God, Chap. 14.14.

*{a vision}* Alluding to the title given to God's messages, Esai 1.1. So Chap. 14.14.

*{of their own hearts}* As, *their own land*, vers. 8.

*{out of the mouth}* Or, *from the mouth, of the Lord;* as 2 Chr. 35.22. and 36.12.

**Verse 17.** *{They say still to them that despise me, The LORD hath said, Ye shall have peace, and they say unto every one that walketh after the imagination of his own heart, No evil shall come upon you}* See Chap. 6.14. and 8.11. vers. 14. Ezek. 13.10,22. Zach. 10.2.

*{They say still:}* Or, *Saying still:* or *In saying, saying;* as, *in slaying slay*, Exod. 21.16. see Chap. 3.1.

*{that despise me}* Or, *provoke*, or *reproach me.* See on Esai 1.8.

*{that walketh after the imagination of his own heart.}* See Chap. 7.24. and 16.12. and 18.12. *his own heart;* as *his own way*, Esai 53.6.

*{No evil shall come upon you.}* See Chap. 14.13. directly contrary to what God had threatened, Deut. 29.19,20.

**Verse 18.** *{For who hath stood in the counsel of the LORD, and hath perceived and heard his word? Who hath marked his word, and heard it?}* The speech either of the prophet himself, as the most, concerning these counterfeit prophets, demanding which of them God had acquainted with any such secret purpose of his, as they pretended to have received from him, as if they came like angels dropped down from heaven, and sent by God to reveal his will and pleasure to his people. See vers. 22. or, as some other, of the false prophets, moving the question, how Jeremy, or any other beside themselves, should come to know any such thing from God, as they delivered in his name; as if they were the only men that were acquainted with God's privy counsels, and none could know them, but from them: and so heartening the people against the menaces of God's prophets. See the like, 1 King. 22.24. And the text thus taken, it would be read with a supply, *For who*, say they, &c. as Esai 22.13. Act. 15.5. Some suppose that the words of the Apostle, Rom. 11.34. were taken from hence; but they are much mistaken; for they were taken from Esai 40.13,14. and are of a far other notion than this passage is: they speak of God's taking counsel from others, this of understanding God's counsel from himself.

*{who}* *Who* but we, or besides us; which some also thrust into the text, So Esai 40.16. and 44.7.

*{hath stood}* Waiting or attending upon God, as servants do upon their masters great personages especially, ministers and officers upon kings and princes, 1 King 10.8. Prov. 22.29. and as, on God, the angels do in heaven, 1 King 22.19. Esai 6.2. Dan. 7.10. Mat. 18.10. his ministers and messengers here upon earth, expecting his pleasure, 1 King. 17.1. Habb. 2.1.

*{in the counsel of the LORD}* Heb. *secret.* Psal. 25.14. Prov. 3.32. and 11.13. and 20.19. and 25.9. but sometime it is used for *counsel*, as Prov. 15.22. Amos 3.7. because counsel oft requires secrecy: and sometime again for an *assembly* in general, Chap. 6.11. though properly and primarily of such as meet to consult about ought, Gen. 49.6. and it seems to allude unto the manner of such ministers, or officers, who attending on kings when they sit in council, do by means thereof, many times, come to the notice of such things, as are wont to be concealed from others. So Job 15.8.

*{and hath perceived}* Heb. *and shall see;* or, *that he might see*, (as Chap. 10.4. and 22.10.) to wit, in some vision; as Esai 2.1. and 6.1.

*{and heard}* Or, (as Chap. 22.3,18.) *hear;* as Psal. 85.8.

*{marked}* Or, *attended*, or, *hearkened;* as 2 Chr. 23.10. Esai 21.7. Chap. 8.6.

**Verse 19.** *{Behold, a whirlwind of the LORD is gone forth in fury,}* *Behold*, mark what I say, and assure yourselves of it, (as Esai 10.30.) whatsoever these false prophets preach to you, as from God, of peace and safety, there is a grievous tempest in coming, that will fall heavily on the heads of those whom they promise peace to, vers. 14. and you will find to your grief, when it will be too late, that what is now told you, was true, vers. 20. See the same Chap. 30.23,24.

*{a whirlwind}* Or, *a storm*, or, *tempest*, as it is rendered, Ps. 83.15. Amos 1.14. Jon. 1.4. for the allusion is not to wind alone; but to a storm of rain, or hail, that lights on men's heads; as in the words ensuing.

*{of the LORD}* That is, *from the Lord;* *a storm*, or, *tempest*, coming from him, sent by him; as Jon. 1.4. So, *an evil spirit of God*, 1 Sam. 16.15,16. for, *an evil spirit from God:* as it is there expounded, v. 14. or, *a tempest of the Lord*, for, *a mighty tempest:* as, *mountains of God*, for, *great mountains*, Psal. 36.6. and, *the trees of the Lord*, for, *great*, and *tall trees*, Psal. 104.16. So, *a sleep of God*, that may be taken either way, 1 Sam. 26.12. The former way goes the Chaldee, which the Jewish commentators concur with.

*{is gone forth in fury}* Or, *with fury*, or, *in wrath:* a defect of the particle; as Esai 52.8. and 56.11. and so the Jewish doctors after the Chaldee: or, *wrath is gone forth;* as Num. 16.46. as an explication of the former.

*{even a grievous whirlwind}* Or, *even* (Heb. *and;* as vers. 9.) *a grievous tempest.* Heb. *grievously paining:* from a root that signifies, *to be in pain*, Job 15.20. Esai 53.5. or, as some *lighting* or, *falling* because the word is after here so rendered. Others, *continuing;* as the word seems to signify, Lam. 4.6. Hosea 11.6. see Chap. 30.23.

*{it shall fall grievously upon the head of the wicked.}* Or, *that shall fall grievously:* the relative supplied; as Chap. 22.6,30. the word here used signifies sometime, *to be in pain*, Chap. 5.3. Ezek. 30.16. sometime, *to light*, or *fall upon;* or, as some, *to stay* and *abide.* 2 Sam. 3.29. *let them fall* or, *rest upon the head of Joab:* and Hos. 11.6. *the sword shall light*, or *abide upon their cities:* our version has joined both together, and it may well be deemed a complexive form of speech, (of which kind see on Esai 38.17,21.) as if it were said, *it shall with pain light* and *rest* (as *Damascus shall be its rest*, Zach. 9.1.) *upon the head* (whereby it appears that some such kind of storm, or tempest is alluded unto, as is wont to light upon men's heads, as Psalm 11.6.) *of the wicked:* either the false prophets themselves, vers. 15,30. or those that are confirmed in their wicked courses by them, vers. 14. or both, Ezek. 14.9,10. See Chap. 14.15,16.

**Verse 20.** *{The anger of the LORD shall not return, until he have executed, and till he have performed the thoughts of his heart:}* So Chap. 30.24. Heb. *done*, and *established.* This storm of God's wrath will not be laid, till what he has purposed be fully accomplished. See Esai 55.11. 1 Sam. 3.12.

*{in the latter days ye shall consider it perfectly.}* Or, *hereafter.* Heb. *in postering of dayes*, (as Num. 24.5.) *consider* of *it* with *understanding*, or *consideration:* for the verb in this form is applyable to either signification, Esai 1.3. and 52.15. Chap. 2.10. and 9.16. a defect of the particle; as vers. 19. When these days are once over, after a while, you will fully understand and seriously consider, what you will not believe at present. See the like, Ezek. 2.5. and 6.10. For there is little reason to refer this with the Jewish master, to the days of Messias, when, says he, the wicked shall at once be destroyed; though of those times this form be found oft used, Esai 2.2. Chap. 48.47. and 49.39. Joel 2.18. Mic. 4.1. Nor is there any necessity of carrying on this clause, by knitting the words of the next verse to it; as if it were said, That when the evils now denounced overtook them, then they should come to know that these false prophets were never sent on any such message from God as they pretended: true indeed; but seems not the sense of the prophet in this place.

**Verse 21.** *{I have not sent these Prophets, yet they ran: I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied.}* They do on their own heads all they do, vers. 16. they have neither mission nor message from me. So Chap. 14.14. and 17.15. and 28.8,9. *yet.* Heb. *and;* or, *and yet:* so Chap. 14.9,15.

**Verse 22.** *{But if they had stood in my counsel, and had caused my people to hear my words, then they should have turned them from their evil way, and from the evil of their doings.}* Or, *For* (as rendering this as a reason, to prove, that they came with no message from him. Heb. *And;* as Chap. 14.15. and 16.15.) *if they had stood in my counsel* (as they pretended, and professed to have done, vers. 18. if they had been admitted into so near attendance upon me, as to be made acquainted with my counsels and purposes) *they would then* (as Gen. 28.21,22. but misplaced there, as here, and Chap. 4.1,2. and 15.19.) *have declared my words to my people.* (Heb. *made to hear*, as Chap. 4.5,15,16. they would have told them nothing, but what I have spoken, vers. 28. acquainted them with my will) *and would have turned them from their evil way, and from the evil of their doings:* they would have endeavored to withdraw and reclaim them from their wicked courses, as other my faithful prophets and messengers do, Chap. 25.3–5. and not have confirmed and strengthened them, as now they do in them, vers. 17. So rather, than as some others following the old Latin, which our version concurs with, if they had faithfully declared God's word to his people, the people then had been converted; for that is not always the lot of God's true prophets, and faithful ministers, Esai 49.4. and 53.1. was not of Christ himself, when he was here upon earth, Mat. 11.20. John 12.37,38.

**Verse 23.** *{Am I a God at hand, saith the LORD, and not a God afar off?}* Some of the ancient Greeks read these words, not by way of interrogation, but by way of enunciation, *I am a God at hand, and not a God afar off;* I am alike near you everywhere, Psal. 139.1–12. Prov. 15.3. the sense is good, but not proper to this place: for the interrogative, though oft suppressed, as Hos. 4.14. Mal. 1.8. is in the Hebrew here expressed: the meaning is, Am I not a God here upon earth, that seems farther from me, Job 22.12–14. Ps. 103.11. and 138.6. and 139.15. as well as in heaven, that seems nearer to me, as being the place of my special residence, Psal. 33.13,14. and 115.3. do you think, because my place is in heaven, Ps. 11.14. that I take no notice of what is done upon earth? Psal. 113.5,6. See Ezek. 8.12.

**Verse 24.** *{Can any man hide himself in secret places, that I shall not see him? saith the LORD.}* Heb. *Shall a man be hid in hidnesses*, or, *hiding places?* the indicative potentially, as Chap. 13.23. and 15.22. and the passive reciprocally; as Chap. 4.4. and 36.19. and *man*, for, *any man;* as Chap. 5.1. and *hidnesses*, or *secrecies*, for, *hiding*, or *secret places;* as Psalm 10.8. and 64.4. and *secret*, or *hiding places*, for, *any secret*, or *hiding place;* as, *our sepulchres*, for, *any of our sepulchres*, Gen. 23.6.

*{that I shall not see him}* Heb. *and I shall not see him:* the copulative for the infinitive; as Psalm 119.73. Chap. 14.19. vers. 18. or *where I shall not see him:* the copulative for the relative; as Gen. 6.13. *and they shall serve*, for, *where they shall serve them*, or rather, *serve themselves of them.* See on Chap. 25.14. See Psal. 139.7–12. Amos 9.2,3.

*{Do I not fill heaven and earth? saith the LORD.}* Not by my powerful and efficacious providence only, 2 Chr. 16.9. Psal. 33.12. and 139.6. Prov. 15.3. Zach. 4.10. but with my essential presence, Psal. 139.3,5,7–10. Am I not everywhere present? do the heavens so confine, or enclose me, that I am not present on earth, as well as in heaven? 1 King. 8.27. Is not the earth my footstool, as well as heaven my throne? Esai 66.1. Act. 7.49.

**Verse 25.** *{I have heard what the Prophets say, that prophesy lies in my name, saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed.}* Or, *I hear what these Prophets* (as vers. 15.) *say*, &c. whatsoever these wicked and wretched counterfeits and impostors imagine of me, as if I kept aloof, were pent up in heaven, and had no place of presence, or residence here upon earth, nor took notice of ought that were spoken and done here; yet I hear their lying, and see their doings. So, *I see*, Chap. 7.11. and 13.27. vers. 14. and, *I know*, Esai 37.28. Hosea 5.3.

*{lies in my name}* Heb. *a ly*, or *falsehood;* as vers. 14. so vers. 26. see vers. 17.

*{I have dreamed}* Or I have a prophecy, or message from God, revealed to me by dream, one of the ways, whereby God, in ancient times, imparted his mind to his messengers the prophets, Num. 12.6.

**Verse 26.** *{How long shall this be in the heart of the Prophets that prophesy lies? yea, they are Prophets of the deceit of their own heart}* Or, *How long?* an abrupt, but very passionate form: like that, Psal. 6.3. *but thou, O Lord, how long?* and, *How long, O Lord? wilt thou forget me for ever?* Psal. 13.1. as also that, Chap. 13.27. *after how long yet?* as if he had said, How long will it be ere they leave this course? are they resolved to make a perpetual practice of it? So I read the next words; *Is it in the heart of these Prophets* to be ever *prophesying of lies, and prophesying the deceit of their own heart? Is it in the heart* (that is, is it their desire and delight? as, *the Law of God is in his heart;* that is, he desires and delights in it, Psal. 40.8. and 112.1. or are they desperately bent upon it? as, *the day of vengeance is in my heart;* that is, I am fully resolved upon it, Esai 63.4.) *of these Prophets* (as vers. 15.25.) to be ever (a defect of the verb substantive: as, *give Jerusalem a praise*, for, make her to be matter of *praise*, Esai 62.7. and Rom. 8.29. *be predestinated conformable*, for, to be *conformable:* and, *he hath chosen rich in faith, and heirs*, for, to be *rich in faith*, and to be *heirs*, Jam. 2.5. that, *for ever*, is supplied, as implied in the former *how long?* expressed, Psal. 13.1.) *prophesying lies;* Heb. *Prophets*, or propheciers of *a ly*, or *falsehood;* as vers. 25. Chap. 14.14.) *and prophesying* (as before) *the deceit of their own heart;* as Chap. 14.14. their own fancies and devices, wherewith they deceive and delude people vers. 16. Thus rather, in my mind; than as some great ones; *Should there be a dream* (to wit, a divine one sent from God) *in the heart, of these Prophets that Prophesie falsehoods? that prophesie the deceit of their own heart?* Or, yea, *they prophesie the deceit of their own heart.* But I leave this to the judgment of others. Some continue these words with those ensuing; *Is it in the heart of these Prophets that prophesie lies*, &c. *Do they think*, I say, *to cause my people to forget my name*, &c. so, *to have in the heart*, and, *to think*, should be all one: as 1 Chr. 28.2. and this seems not improbable.

**Verse 27.** *{Which think to cause my people to forget my name, by their dreams, which they tell every one to his neighbour, as their fathers have forgotten my name for Baal.}* Or, *That devise* (as the word is very frequently used, Psal. 21.11. and 140.2,4. Chap. 11.19. Amos 6.5.) *how to make my people forget my name* (forget me and their duty to me, and all regard to my prophets that come in my name, and with messages from me) *by their dreams* (their vain dotages, and lying devices, which they term *dreams*, vers. 25. as indeed they are no better, vers. 27.28.) *which they tell one to another* (so Chap. 22.8. *the false Prophets to the people*, as *one from another*, *the false Prophets from the people*, vers. 30. as men use to do their dreams, Judg. 7.13.) *as their fathers* (either their ancestors, or those false prophets of Samaria, vers. 13. whom herein they imitate) *forgat my name* (as before, so Chap. 2.32.) *by Baal;* by joining themselves to him, and serving him, instead of me, the true God, and their God, Chap. 2.5,13. Judge 2.11. So that those counterfeit prophets, though they would not be counted Baal's prophets, as those Samaritans; but would be deemed the prophets of the true God, yet carried men away from God, as well as those prophets of Baal did. Thus those that pretend revelations from God, may prove no less dangerous in making men forgetful of God, neglectful of God's word and regardless of their duty unto God; from whom yet either being deluded themselves, or on purpose to delude others they would be deemed to speak, than those that profess to deliver oracles from idols.

**Verse 28.** *{The Prophet that hath a dream, let him tell a dream,}* A learned scholiast, by *dream*, here understands *a divine dream:* but *the word of God* in the opposite member, does evidently show, that those dreams of theirs are here intended wherewith these impostors cheated and deluded God's people, vers. 25,27. The words may very well be rendered, *The Prophet that hath a dream* (Heb. *with* *whom a dream is with:* an elegant redundancy, as in the next member also, in that language very rife) *let him tell it as a dream;* which are usually full of vanity, Eccles. 5.7. as were these dreamers' relations, Zachary, 10.2. not as a divine revelation: for such defects of *it*, and *as* are frequent. See the former, Chapter 17.21. and 22.17, the latter, Psalm 11.1. and 21.2. Esay 13.8. and 21.8.

*{and he that hath my word let him speak my word faithfully.}* Heb. *let him with whom my word is*, as Chapter 27.18. *speak my word truth*, that is, either *in truth, truly, faithfully:* as Judges 9.15,16,19. without addition of ought to it, or mixture of ought with it, Chap. 2.7. 2 Cor. 2.17. 1 Pet. 2.2. and 4.10,11. a defect of the particle *in*, as Esay 33.7. and 34.2. or *as a truth:* such as indeed it is, Psal. 119.142,151,160. John 17.17. a defect of the note of similitude, as before.

*{what is the Chaff to the Wheat? saith the LORD.}* According to this version the meaning should be; *what is the chaffe in comparison of the Wheat?* Or, *what comparison is there between Chaffe and Wheat?* or what use or worth is the one of, in regard of the other? But the Hebrew form (which the Greeks and Latins also very frequently imitate) here used, *what to the Chaffe with the wheat?* seems to have another notion: and that not so much as a learned late writer, *What similitude is there between the one and the other:* but, *what should the one doe with the other?* or *what hath the one to doe with the other?* as the like, 2 Samuel 16.10. *what have I to doe with you?* Hosh. 14.9. *what have I to doe with idols?* and *what have I to doe with thee?* John 2.4. to what end should lies and fancies that are no better than chaff, light stuff, and useless for man's food, be mingled with my word, the bread of life, and the only wholesome food of men's souls, John 6.27. 1 Tim. 6.3. Tit. 2.1. the form is not unlike to that of the Apostles, 2 Cor. 6.14,15,16. and it seems to have been a proverbial kind of speech.

**Verse 29.** *{Is not my Word like as a fire? saith the LORD.}* Heb. *so as the fire:* God's word is not like these men's vain and idle dreams, void of life and spirit; but such as has a powerful and efficacious work upon men's souls, to confirm and comfort some, and to affright and disturb others, to mollify men's hearts, and to eat out their corruptions: in regard thereof like unto fire that warms, and heats, and enflames, melts metal, and burns out dross, and burns up chaff and stubble, and other like light combustible matter, Chapter 5.14. and 20.9. Luke 24.32. 1 Corinthians 3.12,13. 2 Corinthians 2.16. Hebrews 4.12.

*{and like an hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces}* Or (as ver. 28.) is it not (supplied from the former branch) *as an hammer*, (as, Chapter 50.23.) that (supplied, as Chapter 22.6,30.) *will breake a rocke to pieces;* or, or. will it not (the negative supplied from the former, as Psalm 9.18.) *breake a rocke to pieces as an hammer?* Is it not able to break the stoutest and strongest heart, Chapter 5.3. Zeph. 7.12.) and to beat and bear down any opposition that is, or can be made against it? 2 Chronicles 10.4.

**Verse 30.** *{Therefore behold, I am against the Prophets, saith the LORD, that steal my word every one from his neighbour.}* Or, *Behold, I am coming against* (Chap. 21.15.) *those Prophets* (as verse 15.) *that steal*, or *filch, my words* (for the word is here plural) *one from another*, as Genesis 31.49. So verse 27. *one to another.* Many strange expositions are given of these words which I forbear to relate, confining myself to those alone, that seem to carry some show of probability with them: the Jewish doctors whom some of ours also follow, understand of such of them, as did make use of those prophecies, which they heard from God's messengers, but turned them another way, and applied them to other purposes: they instance in Hananiah, (who say they) hearing Jeremiah say, *I will breake the bow of Elam*, Chapter 49.37. made use thereof, and applied to Babylon, what he had said of Elam, saying, *I will breake the yoke of the King of Babel* Chapter 28.2. and the better to back this abusive application, should add, if God would thus break the might of the Elamites, then of the Chaldees also under whom they served, Esay 22.6. Others, going also much the same way, expound it of the terms borrowed from God's prophets; which were so rife with them, *Thus saith the Lord*, and *the Lord hath said it*, verse 17.31. Others, that by their wiles and delusions, they withdrew the people from giving any credit to God's messages, brought to them by his prophets, and so stole away the authority of God's word, and people's affections thereunto. As Absolom by his fawning flatteries did the hearts of David's subjects from him and his government; 2 Samuel 15.6. Others, of their conspiring together to back one another, in their false prophecies, which yet they pretended to be God's words, and such messages as they had received from him: those that propound and assert this sense, reject those former expositions that have reference to God's prophets, whom they should either imitate or undermine, because it is said, *each one from his friend, fellow*, or *familiar;* in which manner the Holy Ghost would not speak of the true prophets: as if any such relation and communion were between them and these counterfeits: but not to insist on that, which might be hereunto returned, that *a man and his neighbour, brother, friend, fellow*, or *familiar*, is in the Holy language no more than *one and another:* and *one from another*, here may well be no other than the false prophets from the people; as *one to another*, the false prophets to the people their followers, verse 27. against this exposition may well be objected, that *my words* here, answerable to what went before, where they are opposed to the dreams, dotages, devices and deceits of the counterfeit prophets, v. 28,29. cannot so fitly be understood of them, or applied unto them, as by this interpretation they are. Others therefore understand them of concealing from God's people such necessary truths, as they ought to have delivered unto them, and have acquainted them withal: to which purpose they are charged not to have endeavored, as they should have done, to reclaim people from their wicked courses, v. 22. that which the Scribes seem charged with, Luk. 11.52. and the Apostle purges himself of, Acts 20.27. But I conceive rather the meaning to be, that by their cunning fetches and flatteries, they filched out of people's hearts those words or messages of God, which by his prophets had been delivered unto them, and they had sometime seemed to heed and regard, yea, to put in execution as our Savior says, that the *Devil comes and stealeth the seed of the word out of the hearts* of some, with whom it has been sown, Matt. 13.19. Luke 8.12. that which comes somewhat near to that before, of infringing of the credit and authority of God's word. An instance whereof we may see in that revolt, in likelihood by the delusions of these false prophets procured, from that which by Jeremiah's sermons they had been formerly wrought unto, c. 34.8–11.

**Verse 31.** *{Behold I am against the Prophets, saith the LORD}* See before, ver. 30.

*{that use their tongues}* The word here used is by divers diversely taken, and that among the Jewish critics themselves. Some of them expound it, as the word in its native, proper, and most usual acception sounds, *that take their tongue*, that is, as our version gives it, *that use* it, or *make use of* it. But this others of them deeming too slender, would have it rendered, *that teach*, or *learn*, or *enure*, (for the word of *teaching*, or *learning*, is oft so taken. See Chapter 13.23.) *their tongue.* See Chapter 9.4. *they have taught*, or *learned their tongue to tell lies:* the word is singular, though collectively taken both here and there) for the word of *taking*, say they, is used of *teaching* or *learning:* and we use indeed the term of *learning* sometime promiscuously, of *teaching*, as well as of being *taught:* but whether the word of *taking* (which we use also of *learning*, strictly and properly so termed) be ever used in Hebrew for *teaching*, I much doubt: though *Doctrine*, or that which is taught, has thence a denomination in use: so termed, because taken and received by the scholar. Some of them keeping the same root and notion, but with some restriction, render it, *that sweeten their tongue:* for, say they, the word of *doctrine* thence derived, signifies properly, *a sweet, pleasant, plausible*, or *delightful doctrine*, Prov. 4.2. and 16.21. So it should signify that which the Greeks call, *an acceptable speech*, or *a speech worthy of acceptance*, Luke 4.19. 1 Tim. 1.15. and 2.3. but in a more general sense seems *Doctrine* so termed; because as it is *given out*, or *delivered* by the *teacher:* Prov. 4.2. and 9.9. so it is *taken* and *received* from him by the *learner:* and the same exception that was taken to the former interpretation, is of force against this also. Others therefore render it, *that stroke* or *smooth their tongue:* fetching the word from another root that so signifies, by transposition of the radical letters; that speak nothing but smooth, pleasing, and plausible things, such as the people desired and delighted to hear, Esay 30.10. See Chapter 6.14. and 8.11. vers. 17. So is that word used, Psalm 5.9. *they smooth their tongue*, or *make smooth* work *with their tongue.* And Proverbs 28.23. *one that smootheth his Tongue* or, *that smoother*, that is, *flatters with his tongue:* thence David also of the dissembler, the words *of his mouth were smoother than butter*, Psalm 55.21. and Solomon of the strumpet, *the roof of her mouth is smoother than Oyle*, Proverbs 5.3. and, *a smooth tongue*, for, *a flattering tongue* Proverbs 26.28. and *smoothnesses of tongue*, Proverbs 6.24. and *lips of smoothnesses*, Psalm 12.2,3. for, *a flattering tongue*, and *flattering lips.* And to this I incline, both because it suits so fitly with the smooth carriage of these counterfeits; and because such transposition of letters is not unfrequent in Scriptures: *lakach*, for *chalak;* as Ecclesiastes 9.4. *bachar*, which signifies *to choose;* for, *chabar*, which has a notion of *conjunction*, or *association*, as the Massorites there observe. So *chedel.* Esay 38.11. for *cheled, the world*, Psalm 49.1. *taphel*, Psalm 18.26. for *patal*. 2 Samuel 22.27. *to be perverse.* *alwah*, Hosea 10.9. for *awlah*, Psalm 43.1. *iniquity.* *Zewwaah*, Esay 29.18. and *Ze-awah*, Deuteronomy 28.25. *commotion*, or *a removal.* *simlah*, and *salmah*, Exodus 22.9,27. *a garment:* *cebes*, and *ceseb*, Levit. 4.32,35. *a sheep.* *cesel*, Chap. 10.8. and *celes*, Chap. 4.22. and 5.21. *folly.* *shachis.* Esay 37.30. for, *sachish*, 2 Kings 19.29. *self-growth.* *almuggim*, 1 Kings 10.11. and *algummim*, 2 Chronicles 9.10. the same kind of trees or timber; and more of the like stamp: these the rather I recite, that this here may appear the less uncouth; as to some peradventure it may. For as for those that expound it of *taking their tongues* to themselves and using them at their pleasure, like those that say, *our lips are our own* Psal. 12.4. whereas God's prophets give up their tongues to be moved and guided wholly by him; and his Spirit, 2 Pet. 1.20,21. as also those that by *their tongues*, understand not their own tongues, but the tongues of the true prophets, whose words and terms they imitated, see on verse 30. they seem to warp too much from the text.

*{and say, He saith.}* That is, *the Lord saith*, as before, *Saith the Lord*, Heb. *Said:* and so there, *Said of the Lord*, or, *That which the Lord hath said:* for that is the proper notion of the term, so used, Chap. 18.15,19. verse 29,30. that father that lying flatteries upon me, verse 17.

**Verse 32.** *{Behold I am against the Prophets}* Or, *I am coming against these prophets.* See on verse 3. Now because here is a threefold denunciation, some of the rabbines would have three several sorts of false prophets here designed; some that filched forms from the true prophets, but misapplied them, verse 29. some that were men of smooth and eloquent language, ver. 30. and some that pretended visions and dreams, in this verse. But this seems groundless; they may rather be deemed several attributes of the same parties, who counterfeited revelations and visions, and those of such matter, as was pleasing to the people; whereby pretending to have received them from God, they withdrew the people from the belief and liking of those truths that from God were brought to them by his prophets. The denunciation is thrice inculcated, to confirm the truth of it, and cause it to make the deeper impression, if not on the prophets, yet in the hearts and minds of the people. See Chap. 22.29. and the like threefold *Behold* but in a divers argument, Esay 62.11.

*{that prophesy false dreams, saith the LORD, and do tell them:}* Heb. *dreams of falsehood:* as, *words of falsehood*, for, *lying word*, Esay 32.7. not such dreams, as God appeared in sometime to his prophets and people, 1 Sam. 28.6. though they pretended them to be such, ver. 25. and told them to the people as such, see ver. 27.

*{and cause my people to err by their lies,}* See verse 13–16,26,27.

*{and by their lightness,}* Or, *Looseness* or, *lewdness.* So Zeph. 3.4. *her Prophets* are *light*, or *loose*, or, *lewd* ones: as we use the word *light*, when we say, *a light woman:* the word is used by Jacob of Reuben, *light as water.* Gen. 49.4. and what his carriage was, in regard whereof his father gave him that title, is in the same place expressed: not unlike that which these false prophets are also charged with in the first place, verse 14. It is used also of those lewd wretches that Abimelech hired to be assistant to him in the prosecution of his wicked designs. Judg. 9.4. where by the Chaldee according to some copies it is rendered by a word that signifies persons *debauched:* for that seems overlight that the Jewish critic here gives it, either *lightness of tongue*, that is, *quickness*, (which some of ours also follow) or, *hastiness*, not *smoothness*, (as some amiss render him) *of speech*, or, *lightness of knowledge;* that is, *shallowness*, want of solidity or sound knowledge: for these are not so much the faults or defects charged upon them, as their lies and loose lives. The Chaldee renders it here by a word that signifies *rashness*, or *presumptuousness:* the Greek, *errors:* the Latin, *miracles:* but both much out of the way; the latter especially.

*{yet I sent them not, nor commanded them:}* Or, *whereas I had not sent them*, or *given them* ought in *charge.* See Chapter 14.14. So ver. 21.

*{therefore they shall not profit this people at all, saith the LORD.}* Heb. *and* (as Chap. 16.13. which yet may well be here retained) *they shall not profiting profit;* or, *nor do they profiting profit this people*, *nor do they profit this people at all:* a form of speech expressed in terms of extenuation, but closely importing matter of aggravation: they do this people no good at all, but much hurt, by their false prophecies, and their flatteries, Lam. 2.14. So, *the treasures of wickedness:* ill gotten goods, *profit not*, Prov. 10.2. they will do a man no good, but much hurt, Mat. 16.26. 1 Tim. 6.9,10. and, *the father of a fool shall have no joy*, Prov. 17.21. but abundance of grief, Prov. 17.25. and, *he that shall break the least of these precepts, and teach others* so to do, *shall be called the least in the Kingdom of heaven;* that is, shall have no part at all there, Mat. 5.19.

**Verse 33.** *{And when this people, or the Prophet, or a Priest, shall ask thee, saying, What is the burden of the LORD? thou shalt then say unto them, What burden? I will even forsake you, saith the LORD.}* God by the prophet, having before dealt, and that somewhat roundly, with the bad rulers, verse 1,2. and the false prophets, verse 9,32. proceeds now to the profane people also, who because the prophets of God used to begin their sermons with *The burden of the Lord*, or the like. See Esay 13.1. & 15.1. & 22.1. & 30.6. Zach. 9.1. Mal. 1.1. would in mockery demand of them, what burden they had from God for them: or as some would have it, when they intended in serious manner to ask one of another, or of some of God's prophets, what word was come, or they had from God, they used to say *what is the burden of the Lord?* as if *word of God*, and *burden*, were all one, and nothing but menaces came or could be expected from him. But the former seems the more probable.

*{And}* Or, *Moreover;* as Chap. 11.12. & 14.11. because he enters here upon a new matter.

*{when this people}* The profane sort of them; whom those false prophets seduce, ver. 14.17.32.

*{or the Prophet, or a Priest,}* One of those prophets that thus delude them, or some one of the priests that are combined with them, ch. 5.31. and he joins prophet and priest with the profane of the people; because the priests and the prophets were no less profane than the people, verse 11. and from them profaneness issued forth unto the people, verse 15.

*{burden}* See on Esay 13.1.

*{of the LORD}* That is, from him. as ver. 19.

*{then shalt thou say}* Or, *say then*, as Chap. 7.27,28. & 16.11. Heb. *and.* as Chap. 22.4.

*{what burden?}* As if he had said in way of indignation, Do you ask what burden?

*{I will even forsake you, saith the LORD.}* A burden heavy enough, as you are like to feel, when you shall undergo it, ere long. See Chap. 12.7. Howbeit, some understand it, as if the meaning should be, that God would rid them of those burdens, as they esteemed them, and it was no small mercy that he hitherto vouchsafed to continue with them; he would withdraw himself away from them, and the gift of prophecy by which he had been present among them. See Psal. 84.9. Others, that they themselves were the Lord's burden, such a burden to him, as he intended shortly to remove and ease himself of, Esay 1.24. Ezek. 6.9. Amos 2.13. But these things seem somewhat over-curious. Heb. *and I will forsake you.* and so verse 34. Chap. 14.14.

**Verse 34.** *{And as for the Prophet, and the Priest, and the people, that shall say, The burden of the LORD, I will even punish that man and his house.}* Or, *And* as for *the Prophet*, or *the Priest*, or *the people:* the copulative for the disjunctive; as verse 18. See verse 33. the words put absolutely, as Esay 65.11. that shall say, *the burden of the Lord;* in contempt and derision, as these now do: for otherwise the term was afterward used by God's own prophets who so entitled their prophecies, Zach. 9.1. Mal. 1.1.

*{I will even punish that man and his house.}* Heb. *and* (as ver. 33.) *I will visit upon* (as ver. 2.) *that man;* (be he priest, pretended prophet, or private man) *and upon his house:* not he alone, but his whole family, or issue, (for the word is used of either, Chap. 21.11,12.) shall smart for it; as Josh. 7.24,25. Zach. 5.4.

**Verse 35.** *{Thus shall ye say every one to his neighbour, and every one to his brother,}* Heb. *a man to his neighbour;* or, *friend*, or, *familiar, and a man to his brother;* that is, say you thus (as Chap. 21.8. verse 33.) *one to another.* as verse 27,28. Chap. 31.34.

*{what hath the LORD answered? and what hath the LORD spoken?}* Speak you in more reverent and religious manner, when you come to enquire of ought from me by my prophet. So ver. 35.

*{and what hath the LORD spoken?}* Or, *or what*, &c. as it is well rendered, ver. 37.

**Verse 36.** *{And the burden of the LORD ye shall mention no more}* Or, *But* (as ver. 14.) *mention ye the burden of the Lord no more.* This term being grown into such gross abuse with them, God would have to be forborne, and more reverent and respective language used to his messengers, and of his messages. See the like, Hos. 2.16.

*{for every man's word shall be his burden}* That which they thus deride and jeer shall befall them; and a burden indeed then shall they find and feel it to be. See Chap. 5.13,14. or this your mockery of God's messengers and messages, shall bring burden enough upon you, you shall pay dearly for it. See Esay 28.22. Heb. *a burden to a man shall his word be:* *a man*, for, *every one;* as ver. 35. or, as some; *because his word is a burden to every one of you;* because you count God's word as a burden, Chap. 6.10.

*{for ye have perverted the words of the living God, of the LORD of hosts our God.}* Or, *because ye have perverted*, (Heb. *and*, as Esay 64.5.) or, *pervert;* as Chap. 3.21,25. Some render it, *if ye pervert* (as Chap. 18.8. either by deriding, or misconstruing) *the words of the living God*, (the only true God, Chap. 10.10. and sensible therefore of the wrong you therein do him) *the Lord of hosts* (and able to take vengeance upon you for it) *our God:* from whom we speak, and who speaks by us and in us, Esay 1.2. Chap. 15.19. 2 Cor. 5.20. & 13.3. for that of the rabbine seems somewhat curious: *ours:* not yours, because you have rejected and forsaken him, Esay 1.4. Chap. 1.16.

**Verse 37.** *{Thus shalt thou say to the Prophet, what hath the LORD answered thee? or, What hath the LORD spoken?}* Heb. *And what*, &c. the copulative is a disjunctive notion, as ver. 35. See the same with this there, save that here that is delivered in the singular, as speaking to each particular person, as ver. 34. that was there spoken as to the main body of them, in the plural.

**Verse 38.** *{But sith ye say, The burden of the LORD: Therefore thus saith the LORD; because ye say this word, The burden of the LORD; and I have sent unto you, saying, Ye shall not say, The burden of the LORD.}* Or *And if* (so is the Hebrew term) *ye will say, The burden of the Lord:* (if you will still persist in using this scoffing language, as v. 36.) *for this cause thus saith the Lord; because ye say this word, The burden of the Lord:* (since that you still use this term) *albeit*, (so is the copulative used, Esay 10.5. & 40.5.) *I have sent unto you, saying.* *Ye shall not say, The burden of the Lord;* notwithstanding this my strict prohibition to the contrary.

**Verse 39.** *{Therefore behold I, even I will utterly forget you}* Heb. *And* (as verse 34.) *I will forgetting forget you;* as Deuteronomy 8.19. I will look no more after, take no more care of you, regard you no more for your good, than as if I had clean forgotten you. So Hos. 4.6.

*{and I will forsake you, and the City that I gave you and your fathers}* So verse 34. nor need we, with that Jewish critic, alter the word by change of a letter, to make it signify, *I will pluck you up;* of which change, see also on Chapter 18.14.

*{I gave to you and your fathers}* So Chap. 25.5.

*{and cast you out of my presence}* As heavy and unuseful burdens, says one, are wont to be cast away: or, rather, as things loathsome and abominable are wont to be cast out of sight, chap. 15.1. the word of *casting* is not in the text: there is no more, than *I will forsake you—out of my presence*, or, *from*, being *before my face:* but it is not amiss supplied: see the like defective, or complexive forms of speech, Psalm 89.39, with 44. Esay 14.12. and 38.17.
