*{and because of his fierce anger.}* God's, verse 37. who sends that sword, verse 16.

## CHAPTER 26

**Verse 1.** *{In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah King of Judah,}* This prophecy seems to be of a former date than that before-going was, chap. 25.

*{came this word from the LORD, saying,}* Heb. *was this word,* or *charge;* as chap. 1. 1. & 21. 1.

**Verse 2.** *{Thus saith the LORD, Stand in the court of the Lords house}* In the great court, 1 Kings 7. 9, 12. in which the people from all parts assembled to worship, chap. 19. 14.

*{and speak unto all the cities of Judah}* The inhabitants of them, chap. 7. 2. Psal. 122. 4.

*{which come up to worship in the Lords house}* Chap. 7. 2. Psalm 122. 4.

*{all the words that I command thee to speak unto them;}* All those *things,* or, *matters* (as Esth. 9. 31.) that I give you in charge; that neither they may plead ignorance, nor you fail in your duty, chap. 1. 7. & 7. 27. & 11. 6. Act. 20. 27.

*{diminish not a word}* Or, *detract not* (Deut. 4. 2. & 12. 32.) *ought;* as Josh. 23. 14. chap. 42. 4.

**Verse 3.** *{If so be they will hearken, and turn every one from his evil way, that I may repent me of the evil, which I purpose to do unto them because of the evil of their doings}* So loath is God to proceed in rigor against his people, if by any admonition or warning given they might be reclaimed, 2 Chron. 36. 15, 16. Lam. 3. 33. Ezek. 18. 31, 32. & 33. 11. See the same in effect, chap. 36. 3.

*{If so be,}* Or, *It may be;* as Gen. 18. 24, 28.

*{hearken}* Chap. 22. 2, 5.

*{turn every one}* Heb. *a man;* as chap. 18. 11.

*{that I may repent me of the evil.}* Heb. *and I will,* or, *shall repent:* the copulative for the finitive; as Josh. 24. 9. chap. 14. 19. Mal. 1. 9. See chap. 18. 8. Jon. 3. 10.

*{which I purpose to do unto them}* Heb. *which I am thinking,* or *devising to do unto them.* So chap. 36. 3.

*{because of the evil of their doings}* Thus evil begets evil: a just retaliation of evil for evil: evil of iniquity, and evil of penalty, are as needle, or bristle, and thread, the one goes before, and makes way for the other; and where the one has found passage, it draws on the other: So Chap. 4. 4, 6.

**Verse 4.** *{And thou shalt say unto them,}* Or, *And say unto them;* as chap. 19. 3. 11.

*{Thus saith the LORD, If ye will hearken to me, to walk in my Law which I have set before you;}* *Walk in my law;* that is, live according to it: as Psal. 119. 1. chap. 44. 10. *which I have set before you.* Heb. *given before you:* as Deut. 30. 1, 15, 19. acquainted you with, and delivered to you for a rule of direction, to order your lives and courses by: a borrowed speech from artificers, novices especially in some art, that have models, and patterns set before them, whereby to frame and carry on their work: So chap. 9. 13. & 44. 10.

**Verse 5.** *{To hearken unto the words of my servants the Prophets,}* Or, *In hearkening unto* (as Esay 50. 10.) *the words of my servants the Prophets:* by whom, and in whom, I speak, 2 Chron. 36. 12. Jer. 15. 19. 2 Chron. 5. 20. & 13. 3. and whom therefore when you hear, you hear me; and hearkening to them, you hearken to me, Luke 10. 16. Thus is the form here found frequently used, Gen. 3. 22. Exod. 14. 11. Deut. 9. 28. 1 Sam. 12. 17.

*{whom I sent}* Heb. *whom I am sending* (or, *send* daily from time to come) both have sent, and do still send, 2 Chron. 36. 17.

*{both rising early and sending them.}* Sending them early; sedulously and diligently, So chap. 7. 13, 25. & 11. 7. & 25. 3. 4. the pronoun *them* is not in the text, nor is needful here.

*{(but ye have not hearkened}* Or, *yet ye would not heare.* Heb. *and* (as chapter 25. 2.) *ye have not heard,* as chapter 25. 3. 4, 7, 8.

**Verse 6.** *{Then will I make this house like Shiloh}* Heb. *And* (as chap. 4. 2. & 15. 19. *I will give* (as chap. 9. 11.) and so in the next branch) *this house as Shiloh:* see chap. 7. 14.

*{and will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.}* Heb. *this city will I give for a curse:* that men in cursing one another may say; *God do to thee, and to thine house, as he did to Jerusalem, and to the men of that city:* So Esay 65. 15. chap. 24. 9. & 29. 18, 22. & 42. 18. & 44. 8.

**Verse 7.** *{So the Priests, and the Prophets, and all the people, heard Jeremiah speak in these words in the house of the LORD.}* Heb. *And;* as Esay 8. 7. chap. 18. 3, 4. which here may be thus rendered with connection of this verse, to the next. *Now when the Priests and the Prophets* (the false ones, chap. 23. 9.) *and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words; So it was, that as soon as he had made an end of speaking:* the like syntax, see chap. 8. 6. & 12. 5. and hereafter, verse 10.

*{in the house of the LORD}* In the court where he preached it, verse 2.

**Verse 8.** *{And it came to passe}* Heb. *It was;* as Chap. 20. 3.

*{when Jeremiah had made an end of speaking all that the LORD commanded him to speak,}* According to the charge given him, verse 2. See on verse 7.

*{that the Priests, and the Prophets, and all the people took him,}* As Pashur had before done, chap. 20. 1, 2. Heb. *and;* as chapter 20. 3.

*{saying, Thou shalt surely die}* Heb. *Dying thou shalt die;* as Gen. 2. 17. & 20. 7. Exod. 21. 12, 16, 17.

**Verse 9.** *{Why hast thou prophesied in the name of the LORD, saying, This house shall be like Shiloh,}* verse 6.

*{and this city shall be desolate without an inhabitant}* Or, *for want of inhabitants.* Heb. *from no inhabitant;* as chap. 2. 14. & 47. & 9. 10. & 33. 10. & 34. 22. & 51, 37.

*{and all the people were gathered against Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.}* See verse 7. The rude multitude incited by the priests and false prophets against him, ver. 8. 11. so the particle is used, ver. 12. chap. 1. 19. & 15. 20. Yet some take it here in its most usual notion, rendering it, *unto Jeremy,* as intimating the flocking of the people about him, to hear what he delivered: that which vexed the priests and the false prophets: for the people are said afterward to have stood for him with the princes: see ver. 16.

**Verse 10.** *{When the Princes of Judah heard these things, they came up from the Kings house, unto the house of the LORD,}* Or, *Now when the Princes of Judah heard these things, they came from the Kings house into the house of the Lord.* Heb. *And they heard those words* (*words,* for *things;* as Gen. 40. 1. chap. 7. 22. ver. 2.) *and they came up:* of which term, see on chap. 37. 5. for otherwhile the palace is deemed to have stood on higher ground than the temple: of this manner of syntax, see chap. 2. 7, 20. & 7. 27. and above on verse 7.

*{and sat down in the entry of the new gate of the Lords house}* *In the entry,* or, *in the porch.* Heb. *in the opening,* or, *at the door.* chap. 36. 10. Ezek. 8. 14. & 18. 19. *of the new gate.* So called, because by Jotham repaired, 2 Kings 15. 35. 2 Chron. 27. 3. This *new gate,* the Chaldee, whom some of the Jewish commenters here follow, say was the east gate of the temple; in the porch whereof those of the great consistory (of which some conceive these princes to have been) used to meet and to sit. Howbeit, their great doctor, of whom they have a saying, that *from Moses to Moses he had no mate,* is reported to affirm, that it was the western gate, in which the great assembly used to sit: Which to reconcile, some suppose that under the second temple that court might be translated from the one gate to the other.

**Verse 11.** *{Then spake the Priests and the Prophets unto the Princes and to all the people,}* To enrage against the prophet, as well the one as the other: see verse 9.

*{Then}* Heb. *And;* Which may well be here retained.

*{saying, This man is worthy to die,}* Heb. *the judgement of death is for,* or, *belongs to, this man,* or *is this mans;* as Deut. 21. 22. So verse 16.

*{For he hath prophesied against this city.}* Thus they arraign God's prophet, as guilty of sedition, for prophesying against the state: So chap. 38. 4. Amos 7. 10. Acts 6. 11, 12. & 24. 5.

*{as ye have heard with your ears}* As you of the people, that heard him speak, are able to witness: *to hear with the eares:* an emphatic elegance; as Psalm 44. 1. 2 Sam. 7. 27. 1 Chron. 17. 20.

**Verse 12.** *{Then spake Jeremiah unto all the Princes, and to all the People:}* Before whom the priests and false prophets had thus accused him, and clamoring against him, required to have sentence of death passed upon him, verse 11.

*{Then}* Heb. *And;* as verse 6.

*{saying, The LORD sent me to prophesy against this house, and against this city, all the words that ye have heard.}* I have delivered nothing but what I had in charge given me by God, verse 2, 3. So the apostle, 1 Cor. 11. 23.

**Verse 13.** *{Therefore now amend your ways and your doings.}* Heb. *And now* (as chap. 23. 12.) *make good:* So chap. 7. 3.

*{and obey the voice of the LORD your God}* Heb. *hear;* or, *hearken to;* as Psal. 95. 7. ver. 3.

*{and the LORD will repent him of the evil, that he hath pronounced against you.}* As chap. 18. 8. or, *that he may repent him;* as verse 3.

**Verse 14.** *{As for me}* Or, *And as for me.* Heb. *And I:* as Esay 65. 11. *And ye,* 1 Chron. 28. 2. *And I;* a nominative absolute: the like whereunto, see on chap. 25. 31.

*{Behold, I am in your hand,}* In your power at present, *hand,* for, *power,* as chap. 20. 4, 5.

*{do with me as seemeth good and meet unto you:}* Heb. *as is good and right in your eyes;* as 2 Sam. 15. 26. chap. 40. 4.

**Verse 15.** *{But know ye for certain,}* Heb. *Knowing know;* as chap. 13, 12.

*{That if ye put me to death, ye shall surely bring innocent blood upon yourselves, and upon this city, and upon the inhabitants thereof.}* You shall be so far from averting and escaping the evil by me from God denounced against you and this city, by taking my life away from me; (See Zach. 1. 5, 6.) that you shall, by murdering of God's messenger, bring a further guilt and evil of a crying nature, both upon yourselves, and upon the state. Num. 35. 33, 34. 2 Kings 24. 4. 2 Chron. 24. 23, 28. Matth. 23. 34, 38.

*{bring}* Heb. *give,* as Deut. 21. 8.

*{blood}* The guilt of it, as Psal. 51. 14.

*{for of a truth the LORD hath sent me unto you to speak all these words in your ears.}* Or, *to utter all these things,* (as verse 2. 10.) *in your hearing;* as Esay 5. 9. & 22. 14.

**Verse 16.** *{Then said the Princes and all the people, unto the Priests and the Prophets;}* Then; having heard the prophet's apology for himself. Heb. *And,* (as verse 6.) the princes, that came from the king's court, hearing of the tumult raised about the prophet by the false prophets and the priests, verse 10. as the Roman colonel about Paul. Acts 21. 31, 32. & 23. 10. and all the people before incited, and incensed against the prophet, by the priests and false prophets, but now pacified by his apology, and the princes' inclination to equity in favor of the prophet, being in likelihood by their carriage and countenance discovered by them. Thus the promiscuous multitude are like waves and billows, moving this way and that way, as some blast of wind blows upon them; crying *Hosanna* this day, and, *Crucifie him,* the next: Matth. 21. 9. & 27. 20, 22, 23.

*{This man is not worthy to die:}* Or, *is not guilty of death,* does not deserve death: ought not to be put to death. Heb. *judgement of death, is not for,* or, *to this man,* as verse 11.

*{for he hath spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God.}* He has delivered nothing but God's message to us. Thus they pronounce a sentence of absolution in behalf of Jeremy, as being no counterfeit, but a true prophet; the cognizance whereof the Jewish masters tell us belonged to this supreme court, the great consistory.

**Verse 17.** *{Then rose up certain of the Elders of the land, and spake to all the assembly of the people, saying,}* Heb. *And* (as verse 16.) *there rose up,* or, *stood up* (as men use to do when they are either to plead as advocates, or to advise as counselors, or to give sentence, as judges, Esay 3. 13, 14. Acts 5. 34.) *men of the Elders of the land,* the same, as some, that were before styled princes, or, as others, some others by their example encouraged; who plead in the prophet's behalf. 1. The like matter before prophesied by Micah, verse 18. 2. The practice of a pious king, Ezekiah upon that occasion; who was not incensed against the prophet: but by earnest supplication and serious humiliation, obtained at God's hand a respite of that judgment for his days: and the peril they might procure to themselves by taking away his life, verse 19.

**Verse 18.** *{Micah the Morashite prophesied in the days of Ezekiah king of Judah}* See Mich. 1.

*{and spake to all the people of Judah, saying: Thus saith the LORD of hosts, Zion shall be plowed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house, the high places of a forest}* Jerusalem and Zion with that part of it, whereon the temple stands, shall all become a wild waste. See Mic. 3. 12.

*{plowed like a field}* A defect of the note of similitude, as Psal. 11. 1. Esay 21. 8. & 12. 13. or, of the verb substantives participle, being, or, becoming, *a field;* being made a field, converted to tillage: the like defect See John 15. 5. being *without me* (or, severed from me) *ye can do nothing:* and Rom. 1. 29. being *whisperers,* and *unto whom ye come* being *a living stone,* 1 Pet. 2. 4. and, being, or, as being *a pillar and shore of the truth,* 1 Tim. 4. 15. spoken of Timothy, as divers of the ancient Greek writers expound it.

*{shall become heaps}* Being utterly ruined, Psal. 79. 1.

*{the mountain of the house}* Or, *of his house,* the article used in a demonstrative notion as pointing to the temple, and the mountain or part of it, on which the temple stood, Esay 2. 2. & 14. 13.

*{the high places of a forest:}* Heb. *high-places of a wood;* a woody high place, overgrown with trees and shrubs; See Esay 37. 26.

**Verse 19.** *{Did Hezekiah King of Judah and all Judah put him at all to death.}* Though he spoke as much as Jeremy now speaks; and that which he then spoke did as much concern, and as nearly touch Ezekiah, and the men of Judah that then lived, as that which Jeremy has delivered concerns Jehoiakim and the people that now are, yet neither did the king, nor the people, that then were, attempt aught against him touching his life, or call him in question for the same.

*{Did Hezekiah}* He did not: he did nothing less than seek his life.

*{and all Judah}* Banding together against him; as you incite the people now to do against Jeremiah, verse 6. or, *any of Judah, and,* for, *or;* as chap. 23. 18, 34. and *all,* for, *any;* as Job 8. 12.

*{put him at all to death}* Either do, or attempt aught in that kind, or to that purpose; as if he had been guilty of sedition for so prophesying. Heb. *slaying slay;* as chap. 38. 15. but here the gemination in a diminishing or extenuating notion: as such forms, which few observe, are sometime used: So Gen. 3. 4. *ye shall not dying die,* for, *ye shall not at all die;* and Gen. 43. 7. *could we knowing know?* for, *could we at all,* or, *by any means, know?* could we so much as surmise, or suspect? in which places for want of this observation, the words are slenderly rendered by interpreters of great note, besides the mind and drift of those that spoke them.

*{did he not fear the LORD, and besought the LORD; and the LORD repented him of the evil, which he had pronounced against them?}* See 2 Chron. 32. 25, 26. Some interpreters render the words, *Did he not fear the Lord; and when he besought the Lord, the Lord repented,* &c. Of which syntax, see before on verse 17. and the like again, verse 21.

*{did not he}* To wit, Ezekiah.

*{fear the LORD}* Humbled himself, 2 Chron. 32. 28.

*{besought the LORD}* Sought to him by prayer; as at other times also on the like occasions, Esay 37. 1.—4, 15.—20. & 38. 2. 2 Chron. 32. 20, 24. Heb. *besought the face of the Lord;* as Zach. 8. 2. Mal. 1. 9.

*{and the LORD repented}* Not bringing that judgment upon the land in Ezekiah's days, Esay 38. 6. & 39. 8. So did he also with Josiah, 2 Kings 22. 19, 20. See on verse 3. 13.

*{thus might we procure great evil against our soules}* Heb. *and we doing* (for, *we should do;* the enunciative in a potential notion; as chap. 16. 20.) *great evill against our soules;* that is, *against our selves:* as chap. 17. 21. & 44. 7. We by taking this course, that the priests and prophets would put us upon, contrary to the practice of that religious prince, should, instead of averting the evil denounced, hasten the execution of it, and bring further evil upon ourselves.

**Verse 20.** *{And there was also a man that prophesied in the name of the LORD, Urijah the son of Shemaiah of Kiriath-jearim, who prophesied against this city, and against this land, according to all the words of Jeremiah.}* Some would have these words to be part of the elders' speech before mentioned, who spoke in Jeremy's behalf, verse 17. But that is nothing likely: for by this latter instance they should rather cross, than back, what before they had delivered: but they seem rather to be the words of the penman (whether the prophet himself, or any other, peradventure Baruc his scribe) of this story concerning the present business, relating the issue of it; and to illustrate God's providence in the preservation of Jeremy, reporting another story of the same subject, much about the same time, but diversely managed, and with divers event. This to clear, the text might well be thus rendered; *Now* though *there were also,* &c. (the copulative used; as Esay 8. 7. the other supplied, as chap. 5. 22.) and so the context carried on unto, verse 24.

*{according to all the words of Jeremiah}* The same things in effect and substance with him: So chap. 27. 11.

*{Urijah}* Heb. *Urijahu;* as *Jirmijahu,* here also, and elsewhere, Chap. 1. 1. of this name was one of David's worthies, 2 Sam. 23. 39. and the high priest under Ahaz, Esay 8. 2. and some other. But of this prophet, save here, we find no mention in the sacred records.

*{of Kiriath-jearim}* A city in the lot of Judah, Josh. 18. 14. where the ark returned by the Philistines, remained a long time, 1 Sam. 7. 2.

**Verse 21.** *{And when Jehoiakim, with all his mighty men, and all the Princes heard his words, the King sought to put him to death:}* As he would have done also with Jeremy and Baruc, Chapter 36. 26. Heb. *And Jehojakim heard——and sought:* See the like, ver. 17, 19.

*{with all}* Heb. *And all;* as Chap. 22. 7, 14.

*{heard his words}* By relation in likelihood from others; as chapter 36. 16.

*{but when Urijah heard it, he was afraid, and fled, and went into Egypt}* Heb. *And Urijah heard it, and feared and fled:* the same syntax with that before. This man's distrustful fear cast him into a snare; when as he that trusts in the Lord is safe, Prov. 29. 25.

**Verse 22.** *{And Jehojakim the King sent men into Egypt:}* From whose king he held, with whom also he had correspondence to his own ruin, 2 King. 23. 34. & 24. 1, 2. and who therefore he knew would deny him nothing, were it never so unequal.

*{namely Elnathan the son of Achbor}* Mentioned among the princes in Jehoiakim's reign, Chap. 36. 12.

*{and certain men with him}* Heb. only, *men:* So Chapter 41. 5.

*{into Egypt}* Or, *even into Egypt:* as, *God will come,* even *God,* Esay 35. 4. The repetition is of force: implying, as the king's malicious disposition; who would send so far after God's prophet to slay him; so that no far flight can secure any, when they once pass the verge of God's protection: see Jon. 1. 3, 4.

**Verse 23.** *{And they fet forth Urijah out of Egypt:}* Or, *Who* (as chap. 15. 19. & 17. 7.) *fetched,* or, *brought away Urijah out of Egypt.* Heb. *made to come out;* as Deut. 6. 21.

*{and brought him unto Jehojakim the King, who slew him with the sword;}* Caused him to be put to death: yet gained thereby no more, than he did by the burning of Jeremy's book, Chapter 36. 28.—31.

*{and cast his dead body into the graves of the common people.}* Heb. *sons of the people;* the promiscuous multitude, men of the meanest condition: Not permitting him to have so much as an honest sepulture, such as persons of the better rank had, who had burial places usually in their private possessions, 2 Sam. 19. 37. 1 Kings 13. 22, 30, 31. such an extreme spite had he against God's messenger, in regard of his message, both living and dead: by this his cruelty exercised on him, supposing that he should affright any from coming again on the like errand: which yet with Jeremy he could not do.

**Verse 24.** *{Nevertheless the hand of Ahikam, the son of Shapan, was with Jeremiah, that they should not give him into the hand of the people to put him to death.}* This has a manifest reference to that which this relation began with ver. 20. Though it fared so with Urijah, who, out of fear, thus deserted his employment; yet it fared better with Jeremy, that stayed by it, and stuck close to his tackle: for albeit, the king himself were so cruelly minded, and had those about him ready enough to put his cruel designs in execution, ver. 22, 23. yet God stirred up the spirit of some of his princes, and one of them more especially, to stand by him, and deal so effectually for him, that he was not delivered unto the power of those that would have taken his life from him, according to promise for protection made to him, chap. 15. 20, 21.

*{the hand of Ahikam was with Jeremiah}* *Hand,* for, *authority, power, help, assistance;* as Deut. 7. 8. 2 Sam. 14. 19. and so afterward again. This Ahikam was one of Josiah's princes and counselors, 2 Kings 22. 12. whose name God would have to be left here upon record, for an honor to him unto all posterity, as having been the principal agent among them that were instruments here of the prophet's delivery: and he seems to have been the father of that Gedaliah, whom Nebuchadnezzar made governor of those whom he left in Judea, 2 Kings 25. 22. chap. 39. 14. God, as may well be conjectured, for this pious act of his father, in patronizing and rescuing his prophet, causing his son to find favor in that heathen king's eyes: howsoever by his folly, and fond credulity, he made it afterward unuseful both to others and himself, chap. 40. 13.—16. & 41. 1, 2.

*{that they should not give him into the hand of the people to put him to death}* Heb. *to make him die;* *to slay him;* as verse 19. *hand,* for, *power,* as before; and chap. 22. 25. It may be objected, that the people spoke in the prophet's behalf, as not deserving to die, ver. 16. But the tickle and fickle disposition of the multitude hence appears, who though partly by the prophet's own speech, and partly by the pleading of the princes for him, were satisfied at present concerning his innocency; yet had not this worthy prince stuck close to him, would by the wicked priests, and false prophets, soon again have been drawn to seek his destruction. See ver. 16.

## CHAPTER 27

**Verse 1.** *{In the beginning of the reign of Jehojakim, the son of Josiah king of Judah}* This prophecy, by the date of it, may seem to have gone before that recorded, Chap. 25. and to have been near of the same time with the story related, chap. 26. for that the several prophecies, or sermons are not in this book entered and ranked according to the exact order of time, wherein they were delivered, has been before showed on chap. 22. 11. And about the date of this there is among interpreters some disagreement: the ground whereof does from hence arise. There is a charge here said to come to the prophet in the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim, for the making of bonds and yokes to be rendered to the ambassadors of foreign states in the reign of Zedekiah: there being eleven years between the beginning of the reign of the one, and of the other; for so many years did Jehoiakim reign, and Jehoiachin his son some few months after him before Zedekiah, 2 Kings 23. 36. & 24. 8, 17. This difficulty to assoil, some, both of the Jewish writers, and other, say, that this prophecy was revealed to Jeremy in the first year of Jehoiakim's reign, three year before Nebuchadnezzar came to the Chaldean crown upon his father's decease, Dan. 1. 1. but that he was to conceal it, and not to publish it, nor put in execution the thing itself enjoined, until eleven year after in the reign of Zedekiah. Others, that he was presently to make these bonds, and to wear them for eleven year, at least, together, and then to send them, as hereafter abroad. But neither do the former seem to give any good reason why a prophecy of this nature should be so long concealed and smothered: nor does that seem to carry any show of probability with it, which the latter have, that the prophet should go up and down yoked in that manner for so long a time together. Those therefore who take this prophecy to be of a lower date, and to have been delivered in the beginning, not of Jehoiakim's, but of Zedekiah's reign; do some of them conceive, that this verse does not belong to this chapter, but to that before-going; and to be the close of it, shut up with the same words, wherewith it began; somewhat like that Hagg. 1. 1, 15. where the last verse formerly in most versions, for want of such observation, was rent from the foregoing chapter, and prefixed amiss to the next: and so many of our Hebrew Bibles, indeed, divide the chapters, both here, and there. But neither show they how this passage can be fixed handsomely to the forepassed relation: nor do those instances they bring from Exod. 6. 10, 29. help any whit to clear the context from an abrupt tearing of this verse, concluded with *saying,* from the next verse, wherein the charge, or injunction is expressed, because they are not the express words of God, but of the prophet rather, speaking from God; and yet why not of God himself, putting words into the prophet's mouth, or speaking of himself in the third person, as he oft does? See chap. 25. 31, 33. some place would be produced, where the word, *saying,* shuts up a sentence, without any speech, or charge at all ensuing. Other therefore of those that go this latter way, say that Zedekiah is here called Jehoiakim, and that *Jehojakim* was a name common to the sons of King Josiah. But of this there is neither any proof, nor good probability. And others therefore suppose, that through the scribe's negligence, who having his eye on the title of the chapter next foregoing, wrote *Jehojakim,* for *Zedekiah;* an error was by oversight at first committed, which afterward being not regarded, bred that general mistake, that all commonly known copies now have. And this their conjecture, they suppose, to receive further strength, from the repetition of Zedekiah's name again, verse 12. and the date of the next prophecy, Chap. 28. 1. said to have been delivered *in the same year* with this, and that *in the beginning,* not of *the reign of Jehoiakim,* but *of the reign of Zedekiah.*

*{came this word unto Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,}* Heb. *was this word;* as verse 26.

**Verse 2.** *{Thus saith the LORD to me:}* Or, *Thus hath the Lord said unto me;* as ch. 3. 6. God suggesting to the prophet by a kind of intimation, the terms wherein he should deliver his message.

*{Make thee bonds and yokes}* *Make thee;* as *Buy thee;* or, *Get thee,* Chap. 13. 1. & 19. 1. an elegant redundancy; whereof see there: *bonds and yokes,* that is, *yokes with bonds;* (as *chariots and wheels,* for, *chariots with wheels,* Ezek. 23. 24.) such as they are wont to be fastened with for slipping and falling off from the neck of the beast that wears them, and draws in them: See on Esai 58. 6.

*{and put them upon thy neck}* *Them,* for, *some one of them;* as Judg. 12. 7. Psal. 1. 3. Joh. 6. 45. wear of them first yourself, (which accordingly he did, chap. 28. 10.) and after dispose of them, as I shall further direct.

**Verse 3.** *{And send them to the King of Edom, and to the King of Moab, and to the King of the Ammonites, and to the King of Tyrus, and to the King of Zidon,}* All neighboring states: of which before see chap. 25. 21, 22.

*{by the hand of the messengers which come to Jerusalem unto Zedekiah King of Judah}* Tender them to the ambassadors of these states; *by their hand* that is, by their ministry; as Mal. 1. 1. or, *by the hand of their messengers;* that is, *by their messengers,* simply; as Esai 37. 24. See chap. 29. 3. *which come,* or *are come,* or *shall come;* and the reason of this their repairing, some render; because Nebuchadnezzar, say they, who made Zedekiah king, 2 King. 24. 17. had given him some power of jurisdiction over these neighboring kingdoms: But others rather with more probability, to solicit him to join with them in rebellion against Nebuchadnezzar, and endeavor to shake off the Babylonian yoke: that which his false prophets also enticed him unto, Chap. 28. 12. and he, in vain, to his own ruin, attempted, 2 King. 24. 20. 2 Chron. 36. 13. but why not to congratulate with him, for the honor, newly conferred upon him, and to pretend, at least, a desire of compliance, and continuance of amity, with him? as foreign princes, neighboring especially, are wont to do one with another: However it may well be not unlikely, that by occasion of such their convening, matters of other nature might withal begin to be hinted and agitated with them.

**Verse 4.** *{And command them to say to their Masters, Thus saith the LORD of Hosts the God of Israel, Thus shall ye say unto your Masters}* Or, *say;* as before, *command.* Heb. *Thou shalt command;* as Numb. 27. 19.

*{The LORD of hosts}* Whose, and at whose disposal, all the creatures are, vers. 6. Gen. 2. 1. Esai 1. 9.

*{the God of Israel}* The only true God, Chap. 10. 10, 16. who though he be in a more peculiar manner *the God of Israel,* yet rules and reigns, not in Israel only, but in your lands also, and to the world's end, Psal. 99. 13. and 103, 19.

**Verse 5.** *{I have made the earth,}* Gen. 1. 1. Chap. 10. 12.

*{the man and the beast:}* Both *the men, and the beasts:* for the words are taken collectively, as Psal. 36. 6. and 40. 11, 12.

*{that are upon the ground}* Upon the habitable part of the earth, Gen. 1. 9, 24—27.

*{by my great power, and by my outstretched arm;}* Chap. 10. 12. *arm out-stretched,* for, power exercised in a remarkable and conspicuous manner; as Deut. 4. 34. and 5. 15. Psal. 136. 12.

*{and have given it unto whom it seemed meet unto me.}* Or, *do give it,* Dan. 4. 17, 25. Heb. *unto whom it is in mine eyes* to give it; as Chap. 18. 4. having an absolute right and interest, therefore, as the maker and author of all, both in it, and in all things therein contained, Psal. 24. 1. and 95. 5.

**Verse 6.** *{And now have I given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar the King of Babylon my servant,}* I am resolved to put them under his power, as by these yokes now rendered to be brought unto you, I would have you take notice: See chap. 25. 9.

*{and the beast of the field have I given him also to serve him.}* I have given him power over both the nations, and all that they have, or possess, goods, chattels, or cattle: So chap. 28. 14. Dan. 2. 38.

**Verse 7.** *{And all nations shall serve him,}* Or, *all these nations;* as vers. 6. *all these lands;* for the article seems here demonstrative; as chap. 23. 15. See chap. 25. 11.

*{and his son}* Evil Merodac chap. 52. 31.

*{and his sons son}* Belshashar, Dan. 5. 1, 11.

*{until the very time of his land come:}* Heb. *the time, even it.* The set time prefixed by God, for the visitation, and dissolution of that state, chap. 25. 11, 12. and 50. 27, 31.

*{and then many nations, and great Kings, shall serve themselves of him}* Such as before served that state, shall then subdue it: See the same before, Chap. 25. 14. and the like, Zach. 2. 9.

**Verse 8.** *{And it shall come to passe}* Heb. *It shall be:* as Chap. 25. 12, 18.

*{that the Nation and Kingdom that will not serve the same Nebuchadnezzar the King of Babylon, and that will not put their neck under the yoke of the King of Babylon, that nation will I punish, saith the LORD, with the sword and with the famine, and with the pestilence, until I have consumed them by his hand}* So of those that refuse to drink of the cup of wrath, Chap. 25. 18. and of Jerusalem in particular, and the inhabitants thereof, Chap. 21. 9. and 38. 1.

*{that the nation that will not serve,——that nation will I punish}* Heb. *the nation that will not serve,——and that nation will I punish:* *and,* for, *that;* as chap. 25. 28.

*{the same Nebuchadnezzar}* Heb. *him:* as Psalm 102. 27. So Chap. 28. 1.

*{put their neck under the yoke}* Their subjection intimated by those yokes before mentioned, vers. 2, 3. See the like metaphorical use of the word *yoke,* Esai 9. 4. and 58. 6. Lam. 1. 14.

*{punish}* Heb. *visit upon:* as chap. 21. 14. and 23. 2.

*{until I have consumed them}* As chap. 24. 10.

*{by his hand.}* By his power and force: or simply, by his means. See vers. 2. 6.

**Verse 9.** *{Therefore hearken not ye to your Prophets, nor to your diviners, nor to your dreamers, nor to your enchanters, nor to your sorcerers, that speak unto you, saying, Ye shall not serve the King of Babylon,}* Give no heed nor belief unto any, that tell you the contrary. So Chap. 23. 16. vers. 14, 17.

*{Therefore}* Heb. *And:* as chap. 26. 13.

*{Prophets}* False prophets, chap. 23. 9, 15.

*{diviners}* See Deut. 18. 10. Esai 44. 5.

*{dreamers}* Heb. *dreams;* for *men of dreams, dreamers:* as *enchantments,* for, *men of enchantments, enchanters;* Esai 47. 12. See chap. 23. 25, 28. and 29. 8.

*{enchanters}* Of this term, see on Esai 2. 6.

*{sorcerers}* See on Esai 47. 9.

**Verse 10.** *{For they prophesy a lye unto you, to remove you far from your land, and that I should drive you out, and ye should perish:}* Heb. *from of your land:* as 2 Chr. 33. 8. Nor that these false prophets and wizards properly intended what is here said; but that this would undoubtedly and unavoidably be the issue of that which they animated them unto. See on Chap. 7. 18. So vers. 15. See also Lam. 2. 14.

**Verse 11.** *{But the nations,}* Heb. *And* (as chap. 25. 3.) *the nation:* or as some render it, as for *the nation:* as chap. 26. 14.

*{that bring their neck under the yoke of the King of Babylon, and serve him}* or, *that put their neck under,* to wit, willingly, on their own accord, as verse 8. before by violence and hostile force they be constrained so to do.

*{those will I let remain still in their own land,}* Heb. *that* (nation) *will I leave:* or it shall be *that* (as vers. 8.) *I will let it remain on its own land:* as chap. 20. 23.

*{saith the LORD, and they shall till it, and dwell therein.}* Or, *that they may till it, and dwell therein:* as chap. 11. 19, 21. and 29. 5.

**Verse 12.** *{I spake also to Zedekiah King of Judah,}* They seem to go here out of the way, who would have the ensuing part of this chapter, to be another prophecy from the former delivered at another time. See on vers. 1, 2. I spoke thus to him, though not to him alone, but to his princes and people too; as appears by the tenor of his words.

*{according to all these words;}* The same things in sum and substance: as Chap. 26. 20.

*{saying, Bring your necks under the yoke of the King of Babylon, and serve him and his people}* The Chaldeans, Chap. 28. 2. *Bring,* or, Put: as verse 8. Think not much to stoop so low, for the saving of your lives, Esay 10. 4.

*{and live}* For, *that ye may live:* as Chapter 29. 5. *dwell,* for, *that ye may dwell;* or, *ye shall live:* You shall save your lives: as, *Doe thou and live,* Genesis 20. 7. and 42. 18. that is, *ye shall live:* as it is expressly, Chapter, 38. 2. Luke 10. 28. So verse 17.

**Verse 13.** *{Why will ye die?}* A compassionate and affectionate expostulation: Why will you needs wilfully work your own ruin, when you may save yourselves, if you will? See the like, Ezek. 18. 31. & 33. 11.

*{thou and thy people}* Regard the safety of your people, if you regard not your own: so he pleads with them, and him, also for the saving of the state and city, verse 17. Chapter 38. 17.

*{by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence?}* The repetition of the instrumental particle, and the copulative, makes the sentence more emphatic. So verse 8. Chapter, 14. 15.

*{as the LORD hath spoken against the Nation that will not serve the King of Babylon}* See ver. 8.

**Verse 14.** *{Therefore, hearken not unto the words of the Prophets, that speak unto you, saying, Ye shall not serve the King of Babylon; for they prophesy a lie unto you.}* As verse 9, 10. So Chapter, 14. 14.

**Verse 15.** *{For I have not sent them, saith the LORD}* So chap. 23. 21. & 28. 15. & 29. 8. Ezek. 13. 6.

*{yet they prophesy a lie in my name,}* Heb. *and* (as chap. 23. 21.) *they prophesie in my name to a lie,* or *to a falshood;* that is, *lyingly, falsely:* as Lev. 19. 12. Chap. 7. 9. See Chapter, 14. 14, 15. & 23. 25. and 29. 9.

*{that I might drive you out, and that ye might perish}* See on verse 10.

*{Ye and the Prophets that prophesy unto you.}* Being sure, if you follow them, to fare alike with them, Chapter 20. 6. Ezekiel, 14. 10.

**Verse 16.** *{Also I spake unto the Priests, and to all this people}* The Jewish people at the same time, when to the messengers of foreign nations, verse 4. and to King Zedekiah himself, verse 12.

*{saying, Thus saith the LORD, Hearken not to the words of your Prophets,}* Not mine, as v. 9.

*{that prophesy unto you, saying, Behold, the vessels of the Lords house shall shortly be brought again from Babylon,}* Those of them that were carried away under Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin his son, 2 Chr. 36. 7, 10.

*{Shortly,}* Within two year, ch. 28. 3.

*{for they prophesy a lie unto you}* As ver. 10.

**Verse 17.** *{Hearken not unto them}* verse 9. 16.

*{serve the King of Babylon and live,}* See verse 12.

*{wherefore should this City be laid waste?}* Heb. *become a desolation:* as Chapter 25, 38. & 44. 2. as undoubtedly it will, if you refuse to follow the advice given you by God. See Chapter 38. 17, 18.

**Verse 18.** *{But if they be Prophets,}* Prophets sent from God, as they pretend to be, Chapter, 23. 17, 31. the pronoun demonstrative for the verb substantive: as c. 10, 3, 8.

*{and if the word be with them;}* as c. 23, 28.

*{let them make intercession to the LORD of Hosts, that the Vessels which are left in the House of the LORD, and in the house of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem, go not to Babylon,}* Let them make trial of their interest in God, whose prophets and privy counselors they pretend to be, for the stay of that goodly plate that yet remains here, either sacred or profane: it is not unlike that speech of Malachy to the wicked priests, Mal. 1. 8.

**Verse 19.** *{For thus saith the LORD of Hosts, concerning the Sea, and concerning the pillars, and concerning the bases}* Of which, see 1 King 7. 15, 23, 27.

*{and concerning the residue of the Vessels, that remain in this City;}*

**Verse 20.** *{Which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took not, when he carried away captive Jeconiah the son of Jehojakim king of Judah from Jerusalem to Babylon, and all the Nobles of Judah and Jerusalem}* 2 King 24. 14, 15.

*{Nobles}* Heb. *white ones:* as Esay 34. 12. Chapter, 39. 6. such as use to go clad with white, that is, fair, and goodly garments, Ecclesiast. 9. 8. Matthew 17. 2. Mark 9. 3. Revelation 3. 4. and 7. 9.

**Verse 21.** *{They shall be carried into Babylon;}* So were they with Zedekiah, 2 Kings 25. 13. 2 Chronicles 36. 18. Chapter 52. 17. 19.

*{and there shall they be}* Abide and continue: as Daniel, 1. 21.

*{until the day that I visit them, saith the LORD}* For the space of seventy years, Chapter 25. 11. until the time that I visit the Chaldeans in wrath, subduing them by the Medes and Persians, Chapter 25. 12. and my people in mercy, by delivering them out of captivity, Chap. 29. 10. So Esay 24. 22. Chap. 15. 15. Ruth 1. 6.

*{then will I bring them up, and restore them to this place}* *bring them up.* or *bring them back,* (as Chapter 23, 7, 8.) to wit, from Babylon: not the people only, but the vessels also: fulfilled by Cyrus. 2 Chron. 36. 22. Ezr. 1. 1, 11. and 5. 15, 16.

## CHAPTER 28

**Verse 1.** *{And it came to pass the same year, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah King of Judah,}* Heb. *And it was* (as Chapter 26. 3.) *in that year,* to wit, before mentioned, Chapter 27. 1. *that,* for, *the same;* as Chapter 27. 8. and so hereafter verse 17. So that this prophecy seems to bear date with the former, both by the common title, and the subject matter of either. That which much confirms the opinion of those, who suppose that Jehoiakim there named, was at first, and should be Zedekiah.

*{in the fourth year,}* Here we meet with a new knot, that seems near as difficult, and as hard to unloose, as that other, Chap. 27. 1. to wit, how the passage here reported and recorded should be said to have fallen out *in the beginning* of Zedekiah's reign, and yet in his fourth year; the one seeming to cross the other. This seeming breach to make up, some make a rent in the context: for as before, they tore off the first verse of Chapter 27. to annex it to Chapter 26. So here they rent from this chapter, the foregoing words of this verse, and annex them to Chapter 37. Expounding the words; *And it came to pass* (to wit, all that was before related of my speaking on this wise to the king and his princes, the priests and his people, chap. 26. 12, 16.) *the same year in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah.* But this conceit of the author thereof has been deemed so uncouth, that I find not any other beside himself therein to concur with him. Howbeit, some of ours, though they tear not this branch off from the context ensuing, yet they suppose it to have reference by way of transition, unto what had been before related, thus rendering the words, *Now when* that (before mentioned) *had been in that year, and in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah; in the fourth year,* that which now followed fell out; to wit, *Hananiah spake unto me,* &c. Somewhat the like conceit the same authors have of another place, though not parallel to this, 1 Sam. 13. 1. whereof elsewhere. But besides that, this gives us a strained syntax, with needless insertions, nor suits well with the stops in the text. It seems thereby presumed, that four years together the prophet did wear a yoke on his neck, which Hananiah should now break: a thing nothing probable, that either the one should so long wear it, or the other have the patience to endure the sight of it so long worn. The Jewish doctors out of their Talmudists tell us, that Nebuchadnezzar, when Zedekiah went to Babylon in the fourth year after the captivity of Jeconiah, chap. 51. 59. gave him a kind of lieutenancy under him over those five kingdoms mentioned, chap. 27. 3. and that this therefore is here termed the beginning of his kingdom: but of that place before, and of the other when we come to it: for of the story itself there is no record produced, nor seems it to carry with it any great probability; though some of ours seem to warp somewhat this way. Others passing by these improbable relations, not admitting such forced breaches as the former sort seem to make in the context, suppose that the words, as they be simply conceived, may well stand together, without any such disagreement as they are supposed to import. The *fourth year* of Zedekiah, say they, may not unfitly be termed *the beginning of his reign:* for dividing his reign, being eleven years in all, 2 Kings 24. 18. as we use to do other things into three parts, the beginning, the middle, and the end; of those eleven years, the four first, or these first with the part of the fourth, may well go for the beginning; the six following for the middle; and the two last, in which his state was invaded and ruined, may well be reckoned for the end. But this, though carrying better show of probability with it, than any of the former, yet is not deemed satisfactory by divers: Nor indeed will the like I suppose be easily produced, where somewhat that fell out in *the fourth year,* of a reign of not above eleven, if so much entire in all, should be said to be done, *in the beginning of it.* And some other therefore lastly, both of the Jewish writers and ours, suppose the fourth year here mentioned to be not the fourth year of Zedekiah's reign; neither is it so said, but the fourth year of the sabbatical course or circle; or the fourth year after the seventh year's rest, Leviticus 25. 4. and the first of his reign. This some of ours seek to back with the like, Daniel 1. 1. as they there expound *the third.* But the places are not parallel. See before on chapter 25. 1. Howbeit, to this I here incline; because the Jewish writers, and our best chronologers do herein agree, that the year wherein the city was taken, the temple burnt, and Zedekiah captived, being the eleventh and last of his reign, was a sabbatical year; some hints whereof they suppose to be given, 2 Chronicles 36. 21. and chap. 34. 9, 15. whereof when we come to it: but they ground this their assertion principally upon the jubilee calculations: and some of those who are deemed most exact in the computation of times, affirm that year to be the fourth sabbatical year of the eighteenth jubilee. Now his first year being the fourth of the seventh, the seventh will begin in his third, and the seventh after that in his tenth, and expire with his reign in the eleventh: and this also some confirm from Ezekiel 29. 17. where the *twenty and seventh year mentioned,* can hardly be deemed any other, than of the jubilee then current; and that being the *tenth year* of Jechoniah's captivity, and Zedekiah's reign; as from the first verse of that chapter is observed: the next after it being Zedekiah's last, must of necessity be the twenty eighth and consequently the sabbatical year.

*{and in the fifth month}* Consisting of half July, and half August, by the Jews called *Ab.*

*{that Hananiah the son of Azur the Prophet, which was of Gibeon spake unto me in the House of the LORD, in the presence of the priests, and of all the people saying,}* This Hananiah, a pretended prophet, so called, because he took upon himself so to be, is by some fondly conceived to have been the high priest; but neither did any of that name about those times hold that place; and his parentage also here recited refels it. Yet a priest he might be: for *Gibeon,* the place of his abode, was a city assigned to the priests and Levites in Benjamin's lot, Josh. 21. 13, 17. See c. 27. 16.

*{that}* This particle is not expressed in the text. Which some therefore omit, to begin a new relation here. Whereof see before. But the suppression of it requiring a necessary supply, is so frequent, as nothing more. See Esay 4. 3. & 7. 1. 21. & 10. 20. & 11. 11.

*{Azur}* Or, *Azzur;* as another of that name also, Nehemiah 10. 17.

*{in the House of the LORD}* In the court where Jeremy used to preach and deliver God's messages to the people. See Chapter 26. 2.

*{in the presence}* Or, *to the face.* Heb. *to the eyes:* as 1 Chron. 29. 10. Chap. 19. 10.

**Verse 2.** *{Thus speaketh the LORD of Hosts the God of Israel}* Thus this wicked and wretched counterfeit imitates the style of God's true prophets chap. 24. 5. & 27. 4. in God's name publishing his own lies, chap. 23. 25, 31. & 27. 15.

*{saying, I have broken the yoke of the King of Babylon}* Thus again in a prophetical strain he would speak to gain the more credit to his lies. See verse 4. of the form of speech, see Gen. 27. 4. Esay 9. 4. verse 11.

**Verse 3.** *{Within full two years I will bring again into this place all the vessels of the Lords house, that Nebuchadnezzar King of Babylon took away from this place, & carried unto Babylon}* That which Jeremy tells you shall be seventy years hence, I know not when, chap. 25. 11, 12. & 27. 22. shall be accomplished before two years be fully expired. See chap. 27. 16. whence it appears, that either this false prophet, or some other of his complices had been delivering the like before.

*{two full years}* Heb. *two years of dayes:* as Gen. 41. 1. and *a month of dayes,* Gen. 29. 14. So again verse 11.

**Verse 4.** *{And I will bring again to this place Jeconiah the son of Jehojakim king of Judah, with all the captives of Judah, that went into Babylon, saith the LORD}* See 2 Kings 24. 12, 16. Heb. *and all the captivity of Judah:* as chap. 26. 21. & 4. 5. and 29. 1.

*{for I will break the yoke of the King of Babylon.}* What he spoke before in the time past, to imitate the manner of God's prophets, verse 2.

**Verse 5.** *{Then the Prophet Jeremiah said to the Prophet Hananiah,}* The true prophet to the false one, though so professing himself, and so esteemed, verse 1. chap. 27. 16. & 29. 15.

*{Then}* Heb. *And:* as chap. 26. 6, 12.

*{in the presence of the Priests, and in the presence of all the people,}* Heb. *to the eyes;* as ver. 1.

*{that stood in the House of the LORD}* See v. 1.

**Verse 6.** *{Even the Prophet Jeremiah, said,}* Heb. *And:* as Chapter 23. 9.

*{Amen; the LORD so do, the LORD perform the words which thou hast prophesied to bring again the vessels of the Lords House, and all that is carried away captive, from Babylon unto this place.}* This the prophet spoke, not as confirming the truth of his prophecy which he knew to be most false, but expressing his own earnest, and hearty wish and desire, that, if God pleased, it might be so.

*{Amen}* A particle in Hebrew commonly used, either to signify our assurance of the certain truth of somewhat related; and then usually it is prefixed to the words of him that speaks; as Matthew 5. 18, 26. or our desire of something to be performed: and so it is subjoined to the speech of some other commonly, as Numb. 5. 22. Deut. 27. 15, 26. 1 Kings 1. 36. 1 Chr. 16. 36.

*{the words}* Or, *those things:* as chap. 26. 2. and 27. 12.

*{to bring again}* Or, *in bringing backe.* See on Chapter 18. 15.

*{all that is carried away captive}* Or, *that have been carried away captive.* Heb. *all the captivity:* as Chapter 29. 4. 20, 31. this concerning the persons, as the former, the vessels, verse 4.

**Verse 7.** *{Nevertheless, hear thou now this word that I speak, in thine ears, and in the ears of all the people.}* Hear and consider well this thing that I speak, (as v. 6. c. 22. 1.) in your hearing, because it principally concerns you; and in the hearing of the people here present, because it also concerns them: *ears* for *hearing:* as chap. 2. 2. and 26. 14. & 29. 29. & 36. 6, 15. So *eyes* for *face* or *sight,* verse 1, 5.

**Verse 8.** *{The Prophets that have been before me and before thee of old, Prophesied both against many countries, and against great Kingdoms; of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.}* The prophet admonishes this counterfeit, and the people together with him, of what other prophets had before time prophesied in such manner, and of such evils as himself now did, which could not therefore be any good ground to detract aught from the truth of his present prophecy, since that he prophesied no other things than they had formerly done. See Chap. 26. 18.

*{of old}* Heb. *from age;* in time past, so Joel 2. 2.

*{prophesied}* Or *even prophesied:* or *they, I say, prophesied.* Heb. *and:* as chap. 24. 9. & 27. 5.

*{against many countries}* Heb. *unto:* as chap. 27. 12. yet the particle is used also for *against* c. 15. 20.

*{many}* Or, *great, ample,* ones: as some here render it: for the word is in the use of it indifferent to either. See Chapter, 27. 7.

*{of war}* Heb. *unto war:* but so also is the particle used, c. 14. 10. So in the rest here.

*{of evil}* Or *affliction:* as Esay 45. 7. Chapter 18. 11. Howbeit, some conceive, not without some good probability, that some particular evil or affliction, should here be intimated; because it is on either side clasped in with such; in regard whereof they suppose that by a letter miswritten, it is *raah, evil,* or *affliction* for *raab;* that is, *famine:* the rather because these three are so frequently found conjoined in this prophet: as Chapter 21. 9. & 24. 10. & 27. 13. & 38. 2. & 39. 18. & 44. 12, 13. 18, 27. and elsewhere, Ezekiel 5. 11, 13. & 7. 11, 12. & 7. 15. & 12. 16. & 14. 21. The same surmise some good authors of note have concerning that place, Heb. 11. 37. where in the midst of many particular executions done upon the faithful, comes in, *they were tried* or *tempted;* supposing that for *ἐπειράσθησαν*, as we now have it, it was at first, *ἐπυρώθησαν*: but there is no such word as that found: and I suppose therefore it was rather *ἐπρήσθησαν*, *they were burnt:* and there is an elegant consonancy (such as the apostle oft uses in his epistles) between that and the word next before going, *ἐπρίσθησαν*, *ἐπρήσθησαν*, which differ but in a letter: nor is there much difference in writing between this and that which the copies now exhibit.

**Verse 9.** *{The Prophet which prophesieth of peace}* Or, *As for the Prophet* (for the word is here put absolutely, as the like, Psalm 125. 2. Chapter 26. 4.) *that prophesieth of peace,* or *prosperity:* as ch. 29. 7. as you Hananiah now do, verse 3, 4. Heb. *that shall prophesie unto,* or *of peace,* as v. 8.

*{when the word of the Prophet}* Or, *that Prophet:* as Chapter 25. 15.

*{shall come to pass, then shall the Prophet be known, that the LORD hath truly sent him}* Whether a prophet prophesy of good or evil, the event of that which they foretold was that whereby they were to be tried, Deut. 18. 22. albeit God sometime extraordinarily to try his people, suffer such things, as false prophets also foretell, to fall out, Deut. 13. 1, 3. but then have God's people another rule given them, whereby they may be discovered, to wit, by their doctrine brought to the touchstone of God's written word, and thereby examined, Esay 8. 20. But the prophet here the rather applies the rule, to the prophets of peace, such as this counterfeit; because people are wont more to give credit to such as prophesy what they desire.

*{then}* Heb. *and* as v. 5.

*{truly}* Or, *of a truth:* as it is well rendered c. 26. 15. Heb. *in truth* as there also.

**Verse 10.** *{Then Hananiah the Prophet}* As v. 1. Heb. *And:* as verse 9.

*{took the yoke from off the Prophet Jeremiahs neck, and brake it.}* The yoke which by God's appointment he had made, and did then wear. See Chapter 27. 2. whence it appears that this was done about the time of that command by God there given unto the prophets. Thus this wicked wretch, led away with ambition and covetise, and desirous to please the people, breaks forth into this height of impiety and extremity of outrage, to pluck from the prophet's neck that yoke, which God had enjoined him to put on, and to break that asunder, that he had commanded to be made; as one desperately bent to act directly contrary unto God himself in either; thereby as by a visible sign to justify and confirm such lies, as against knowledge and conscience he had vented and to maintain his own credit and repute with those whose favor he affected. So the like, 1 Kings 22. 11, 24.

**Verse 11.** *{And Hananiah spake in the presence of all the people,}* Heb. *to the eyes;* as v. 1, 5. *{saying, thus saith the LORD, Even so will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar King of Babylon from the neck of all nations within the space of two full years}* Even as I now break this wooden yoke: see v. 3, 4.

*{all nations}* Before mentioned, Chapter 25. 15, 17.—26. & 27. 7.

*{and the Prophet went his way}* Or *So:* as Chap. 13. 2, 5. As not not enduring longer to hear him vent such gross falsehood and lies in God's name: as those, Esay 36. 20. having no further errand then to deliver to them from God; which yet afterward he had, verse 12.

**Verse 12.** *{Then}* Or, *Moreover,* Heb. *And;* as Esay 8. 1. for it, it was not at the present.

*{the Word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the Prophet}* Heb. *was to him;* as chap. 27. 1.

*{(after that Hananiah had broken the yoke from off the neck of the Prophet Jeremiah) saying,}* See v. 10.

**Verse 13.** *{Go and tell Hananiah, saying,}* Heb. *Going go,* (as chap. 13. 1.) *and thou shalt say to Hananiah,* that is, say you to him; as Chap. 22. 2.

*{Thus saith the LORD, Thou hast broken the yoke of wood, but thou shalt make for them yokes of iron.}* Heb. *and* (as chap. 27, 11.) *thou shalt make* (or do you make, as before, *say,* you Jeremy: for they seem out of the way, that apply it to Hananiah) *instead of them* (those wooden yokes, one of which he has broken) *yokes of iron;* such as shall not so easily be broken: a type of a cruel, hard, and strong bondage; and such as cannot be shaken off, Deuteronomy 28. 48. this was all that he and they that gave credit to him should gain by that presumptuous and impious act of his, an improvement of their bonds. So Esay 28. 82. See also, Chapter, 36. 27, 28, 32.

**Verse 14.** *{For thus saith the LORD of Hosts the God of Israel}* As Chap. 28. 4.

*{I have put a yoke of iron upon the neck of these Nations, that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar King of Babylon;}* Heb. *I have given* (as Esay 42. 1. I am resolved to do it) or *I will put* (as Chapter 31. 33.) *a yoke of iron,* or *an iron-yoke* (as verse 13.) *upon the neck of these Nations* (of which v. 11.) *to serve Nebuchadnezzar;* as Psalm 102. 22.

*{and they shall serve him}* Chap. 27. 7.

*{and I have given him the beasts of the field also.}* Thereby implying, that all shall be his, and at his service: see Chap. 27. 6. Daniel 2. 48.

**Verse 15.** *{Then said the Prophet Jeremiah unto Hananiah the Prophet}* Or, *Furthermore,* as Chapter 14. 11. or, *Also: The Prophet Jeremiah also said;* as Chapter 27. 12. Heb. *And.*

*{Hear now Hananiah, The LORD hath not sent thee, but thou makest this people to trust in a lie.}* See Chapter 27. 15. and 29. 9.

**Verse 16.** *{Therefore thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will cast thee from off the face of the Earth,}* Heb. *Behold, I am casting thee from off the face of the Earth;* as Gen. 6. 7. I will without any long delay, take you away by death: the form of speech is thence taken, because the living keep above ground. Gen. 1. 9. & 6. 1. whereas the dead usually are laid up in the earth, and lie under ground, Gen. 23. 4. Psalm 115. 17.

*{this year shalt thou die}* You that tell lies of things that shall be within two years complete, shall not live so long yourself, v. 10. Heb. *the year,* for *this year;* as Esay 37. 30. so *the day,* for *this day,* chap. 2. 10, 18.

*{because thou hast taught rebellion against the LORD;}* Heb. *thou hast spoken* (as Deut. 13. 5. Chap. 29. 32.) *revolt* (as Chap. 5. 23, 29. *unto,* or *against, the Lord;* as verse 8. because by your lying tales you have heartened and encouraged men to stand out against God's word, and against his admonitions and menaces by his prophets. See chap. 23. 27.

**Verse 17.** *{So Hananiah the Prophet died the same year in the seventh month:}* Heb. *And;* as Chap. 13. 2, 5. *the same year.* Heb. *that year;* as v. 1. *in the seventh moneth;* containing part of September, and part of October: whereby it appears that he survived not this presumptuous act of his, and the prophet's denunciation thereupon, full two months to an end. See v. 1. that which might yet have been to this people, both a sufficient conviction of his false and wicked dealing with them: and a strong confirmation of the truth of those things that by Jeremy had been delivered. But nothing could avail, or prevail with them, to bring them to repentance: (Such is the obstinacy of man's hard heart,) until by some gracious work upon it, it be altered and renewed: See Numb. 16. 41. Deut. 29. 3, 4. Ezek. 11. 13, 15. John 12. 37. The Jewish doctors here tie us needless knots, and untie them again with groundless tales. They make question, how Hananiah died that year, when as the seventh month began the next year according to the civil account: and this difficulty, indeed none, to take away, they tell us, (the Chaldee paraphrast hinting to them somewhat to that purpose) that he died indeed on the last day on the sixth month at even, but gave in charge to his people, to conceal his death till the beginning of the seventh month, to make Jeremy a liar. But what need these fictions, when as the prophet's words are plain enough, and were true, what month soever he should die in, if he died within a twelvemonth after that denunciation: and much more, if he died ere the year then running were expired, according to either account, civil or sacred: this latter the rather; because the date of prophecies, and of this among the rest, were usually reckoned according to it. Besides, that this fabulous relation directly crosses the text, which says, expressly, that he died in the seventh month.

## CHAPTER 29

**Verse 1.** *{Now, these are the words of the letter, that Jeremiah sent from Jerusalem unto the residue of the Elders, which were carried away captive, and to the Priests, and to the Prophets, and to all the people, which Nebuchadnezzar had carried away captive from Jerusalem to Babylon.}* In this chapter, as by the inscription of it, verse 1.—3. may appear, is related the sum and substance of a letter sent by Jeremy to the Jews that abode then in captivity in Babylon, wherein he persuades them to rest contented with their present estate there, until God's time set for their deliverance should come, v. 4.—7. and not to hearken unto such prophets, as should tell them of a more speedy enlargement, verse 8, 9. promises restitution of them upon their sincere return to God, when seventy years are expired, vers. 10.—14. and denounces judgments from God both upon the residue of that nation, who remained yet behind, v. 15—20. and against two of the false prophets that abode with them at Babylon, ver. 20.—23. together with a relation of a letter upon the receipt of this, written back by one Shemaiah, enticing some of the priests to call Jeremy in question for it, with a denunciation of God's vengeance upon him for the same, verse 24.—32.

*{Now}* Heb. *And;* The copulative here used, not for connection of this with any foregoing relation; but to make introduction only into the discourse here ensuing; as Ezra 1. 1. Jon. 1. 1.

*{the words}* *Matter* or *tenour;* as Est. 9. 31.

*{the letter}* Heb. *booke;* as 2 Kings 5. 5, 6. So ver. 25.

*{the residue of the Elders}* So he speaks, because some of them, in likelihood, died by the way; and others of them, shortly after their access thither.

*{which were carried away captive}* Heb. *of the captivity;* as Chapter 28. 4.

**Verse 2.** *{(After that Jeconiah the King and Queen, and the Eunuchs, and the Princes of Judah and Jerusalem, and the Carpenters, and the Smiths were departed from Jerusalem)}* See the like parenthesis, chap. 28. 12. and the very same for the most part of it, Chap. 24. 1. to which relation this also has some reference: See v. 17. whereby it appears that this relation is of somewhat a later date than that.

*{the Queen}* His mother, Chapter 13. 18. & 22. 26. 2 Kings 24. 12.

*{Eunuchs}* Or, *Officers,* or, *Chamberlains:* See Gen. 39. 1. Esay 39. 7.

**Verse 3.** *{By the hand of Elasah the son of Saphan, and Gemariah the son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah King of Judah sent unto Babylon to Nebuchadnezzar King of Babylon, saying,}* In what year of Zedekiah's reign, or upon what occasion these messengers were sent to Babylon, is not expressed. Some surmise, that judgment of God manifested in the hastened decease of that false prophet, Hananiah, related chap. 28. 16, 17. Zedekiah being somewhat disheartened, sent these men shortly after with his yearly tribute unto Babylon, the rather to remove all suspicion of having any compliance with the Egyptian, or thoughts tending to the least disloyal carriage towards him, unto whom, having raised him unto the crown, he had by oath obliged himself, Ezek. 17. 13.

*{by the hand of Elasah}* Or, *by Elasah;* as Esay 37. 24. Chapter, 27. 3.

*{Elasah the son of Saphan}* Of this name we find divers, 1 Chronicles, 2. 39, 40. & 8. 37. & 9. 43. Ezr. 10. 22. but all divers from this *Elasah the son of Saphan:* who whether he were brother to Ahikam before mentioned, chap. 26. 24. is uncertain: there seeming to be sundry Saphans living in some place of note in those days.

*{Gemariah the son of Hilkiah}* So described to distinguish him from another Gemariah the son of Saphan the scribe, Chap. 36. 10.—12. nor is it certain what *Hilkiah* this was, whose son this *Gemariah* is said to have been; divers about that time being of the same name: see chap. 1. 1.

*{saying}* This word has not reference to their message, but to Jeremy's letter mentioned, ver. 1.

**Verse 4.** *{Thus saith the LORD of Hosts the God of Israel,}* As Chapter 27. 4.

*{unto all that are carried away captive}* Heb. *unto all the captivity;* as ver. 1.

*{whom I have caused to be carried away from Jerusalem unto Babylon.}* I the Lord whose work this was, Chap. 24. 5. Ezek. 11. 16. though effected by Nebuchadnezzar, chap. 25. 9. and procured by their sins, chap. 1. 15, 16. & 4. 18.

**Verse 5.** *{Build ye houses and dwell in them:}* Or, *that ye may dwell in them;* as Genesis 35. 1. chap. 27. 12. a defect of the pronoun; as Chapter 6. 16. & 9. 10. or, *to dwell in;* and so there needs no supply.

*{and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them}* Or, *that ye may eat the fruit of them;* as 1 Sam. 28. 22. 1 Kings 13. 15. and as before: or, *the fruit thereof you may eat:* the copulative with the demonstrative, for the relative; as chapter 17. 7. & 26. 23. & 28. 7. See verse 6.

**Verse 6.** *{Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters;}* Or, *that ye may beget sons and daughters;* or *on whom ye may beget* such; contrary to the advice given to those that abide at Jerusalem, Chap. 16. 2.

*{and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands,}* The power of parents intimated in this form of speech: as also, Deut. 7. 3.

*{that they may bear sons and daughters}* Heb. *and they shall bear* as chap. 4. 4. and 26. 3. Mal. 1. 9.

*{that ye may be increased there, and not diminished.}* Heb. *and multiply* (as before, *dwell* and *eat,* vers. 5.) *there* (to wit, at Babylon) *and be not diminished.*

**Verse 7.** *{And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried captive, and pray unto God for it.}* Or, *Seek the welfare;* as it is rendered, chap. 38. 4. Heb. *seek after,* or *seek to* God (for it is the same word that is used, Esai 55. 6. Ezek. 36. 37.) *and pray to God for her:* to wit, for Babylon; for the affix is feminine; howbeit they are willed and advised thus to do, not out of any special affection to that place, or state, as they are willed and said to *seek the welfare of Jerusalem,* Psal. 122. 6—9. but in regard of their own interest and share in the common rest and quietness, during the time of their abode there, that they might with less molestation and distraction patiently expect the time of deliverance. For otherwhile they were to pray for the downfall of Babylon, when the time by God thereunto designed should come, Psal. 137. 8, 9. ch. 51. 35. as for that, whereat not they alone, but the whole world should rejoice. See Esai 14. 4.

*{for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace.}* Your own welfare while you abide there is enwrapped in the rest, quiet, and welfare of that state, as of passengers in the welfare of the vessel, wherein they are embarked.

**Verse 8.** *{For thus saith the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel,}* As verse 4.

*{Let not your Prophets and your diviners that are in the midst of you, deceive you,}* *in the midst of you,* or, *among you:* as chap. 39. 14. to wit, at Babylon: as verse 15. 1. See chap. 27. 9, 15. and 23. 26.

*{neither hearken to your dreams, which ye cause to be dreamed}* Or, *which ye dream:* those fancies which you conceive within yourselves, of some speedy delivery, which are indeed no better than dreams: or, *which ye make* (your dreamers) *to dream,* (a form, though irregular, yet whereof a parallel is found, 2 Chron. 28. 23.) by giving heed to them; which if you did not, they would not dream them. Yet the words may well be rendered, as some do, *neither hearken to your dreamers* (your *men of dreams,* your dreamwrights) whom (by listening unto) *ye make* to dream; you give occasion and encouragement to devise dreams, wherewith to delude you. See Chap. 27. 9. Of these dreams also, Chap. 23. 25–28.

**Verse 9.** *{For they prophesy falsely unto you in my name}* Heb. *they prophesie in a lie:* as chap. 27. 15.

*{I have not sent them, saith the LORD,}* So chap. 14. 14. and 23. 21. and 27. 15. and 28. 15.

**Verse 10.** *{For thus saith the LORD, that after seventy years be accomplished at Babylon,}* Or, *But* (as Chap. 14. 12, 13. *thus hath the Lord said,* (as opposing what God himself had indeed said to their lying relations fathered on him) *that after seventy years accomplished at Babylon* nor before, nor sooner, as your prophets bear you in hand, and diviners and dreamers falsely inform you, chap. 28. 3. vers. 8, 15. those seventy years, which by this place appear to commence from the time of their deportation whom the prophet wrote this letter to, see on chap. 25. 12. Heb. says the learned scholiast, *according to,* or *at the mouth filling, of seventy years:* but the term that he renders *mouth,* is nothing but a syllabical adjection, joined frequently, both with this, as Exod. 16. 21. Num. 6. 21. and 7. 56. and with other prepositions of the like nature with it; as 1 King. 17. 1. Prov. 27. 21. than which also in the rabbines' commentaries nothing is more rife.

*{I will visit you}* In mercy and for good: as Ruth 1. 6. chap. 27. 12. Luke 1. 68.

*{and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return to this place}* Heb. *to cause you to return,* or *to bring you back.* See the like, chap. 18. 15. and 28. 6.

**Verse 11.** *{For I know the thoughts that I think towards you saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil;}* I well know what my purposes are concerning you: not such as concern your evil, but your welfare and prosperity; *peace:* as before, vers. 7. See Esai 55. 8. Act. 15. 18.

*{not of evil}* Heb. *not to evil:* such as may tend to your hurt; as chap. 38. 4.

*{to give you an expected end}* Or, *in giving you* (as before v. 9.) *an expected end:* in not failing your expectation. Heb. *an end and expectation.* Such an end as yourselves hope for, desire, and expect. Of the form of speech, see on Esai 4. 5. Some render it, *an end* and *an end of expectation;* which comes much up to the former. Howbeit, whereas by *end* they would have understood *a reward;* (because the word is so used Prov. 23. 18.) and so also expound that 1 Pet. 1. 9. *receiving the end* (that is, *the reward) of your faith: end,* for, *reward;* because the reward comes usually at the end. I suppose overnice, and unnecessary, either in the one place, or in the other; though of reward some mention be made in this argument, Chap. 31. 16. but I conceive the *end,* or *issue* only to be here intended. See Psal. 9. 18. and 37. 37.

**Verse 12.** *{Then shall ye call upon me, and go and pray unto me, and I will hearken unto you.}* *Then.* Heb. *And:* as chap. 28. 5, 9. *go and pray;* or *go to pray:* address and set yourselves seriously thereunto; as did Daniel, Dan. 3. 9. See the like promise made, Esai 65. 24. pressed by Daniel, and performed by God, Dan. 9. 17. 19, 23. and 10. 2.

**Verse 13.** *{And ye shall seek me and find me,}* A defect of the pronoun in the latter sprig, supplied from the former; as Psalm 139. 1. Chap. 15. 16. but it may well be rendered without the supply; *Ye shall seek me and finde:* not miss, or fail of what you seek for, Esai 45. 19. Mat. 7. 7, 8.

*{when ye shall search for me with all your heart,}* Or, *because you shall seek unto me* (as Ezek. 36. 37.) *with all your heart:* Psal. 119. 2. that is, sincerely and entirely. See Chap. 24. 7. Deut. 4. 29. being thoroughly humbled by your forepassed afflictions, for all your former transgressions and rebellions against me, Levit. 26. 40, 41. Ezek. 6. 9. and 36. 31.

**Verse 14.** *{And I will be found of you, saith the LORD}* As Psal. 32. 6. Esai 55. 6. and 56. 1. A speech borrowed from those that are willing to be spoken with by those that repair to them for advice, aid, or relief.

*{and I will turn away your captivity,}* Or, *bring back,* or *turn again;* as Psal. 14. 7. and 126. 1. *captivity,* for, *captives:* those of you, that are in captivity. So ver. 1, 4. See chap. 32. 3.

*{and I will gather you from all the nations, and from all the places, whither I have driven you, saith the LORD}* Heb. *which I have driven you there,* or *thither:* as chap. 13. 7. See the like promise, Deut. 30. 3. Esai 11. 11, 12. Ezek. 11. 16, 17. and 20. 34, 41.

*{and I will bring you again into the place, whence I have caused you to be carried away captive}* Or, *from whence I had transported you.* Heb. *which from there;* as before. See Chap. 24. 6. and 32. 37.

**Verse 15.** *{Because ye have said,}* Or, *Because ye say.* The prophet here turns his speech from them, at least, from the well affected among them, and the gracious promises of good intended by God to them, unto those that listened unto the false prophets among them, whom he had given them warning of before, verse 8. and unto those more especially, that remained yet at Jerusalem; foretelling how God intended to deal with them, howsoever their false prophets gave them assurance of the contrary, ver. 16—19. and withal what should befall those false prophets abiding with them at Babylon, ver. 20—23.

*{The LORD hath raised up Prophets in Babylon}* Some interpreters here depart from the received both reading and interpretation of this verse, rendering the words on this wise, as depending upon ver. 14. without reference to what ensues; Then will I deal thus with you, when you shall say, (that is, acknowledge) *The Lord did* indeed *raise us up Prophets,* (who told us) that we should be carried captive *to Babylon:* like that, Ezek. 2. 5. and 33. 33. But this forced exposition they seem to have pitched upon, in regard of that word, the termination whereof commonly imports motion to a place, rather than of abode in it: but that scruple may easily be removed, for divers places may be produced, wherein words so formed, are used in this latter notion: as here, *to Babylon,* for, *in Babylon:* so, *to reach the earth,* for, *on the earth,* Gen. 28. 12. and, *to the altar,* for, *on the altar,* Exod. 29. 13, 16. Lev. 16. 5. and, *to the North,* for, *in the North,* Chap. 46. 6, 10. as it is afterward there expounded: and this cleared there is nothing left, that may persuade much less enforce us, to depart from the received interpretation of the place. See further on ver. 16. Because some among you are overprone to heed these counterfeits, to wit, Ahab, Zedekiah, and Shemaiah the dreamer, ver. 21, 24. hear how far it shall be from that which they would make you believe concerning the dissolution of your captivity, and your speedy return into your country; that those who remain yet there at liberty, shall within a short time be transported and brought over unto you, after they have sustained much misery at home, ver. 17, 18.

**Verse 16.** *{Know that thus saith the LORD,}* This supply, I suppose, is needless. The particle that begins the verse is in the original of various use, and the old Latin, which many herein follow, renders it, *Because,* or, *For:* which some thus knit on to the former relation; as if the prophet had said, I have told you what God says, but you listen to other prophets who have brought you to Babylon, and are so far from furthering your delivery thence, that they would rather help to bring you thither, if you were at liberty in your own country; *for thus saith the Lord* concerning those that yet remain there: And this coherence would do very well, if the words of the foregoing verse would admit the sense here given them; which I see not how it can, even by any force, be wrung from them: and for that which seems to have put these also upon such tentering and torturing of the text, enough has been said before. The particle being rendered, *Therefore; Therefore thus saith the Lord;* as answering to that, *Because ye say,* verse 15. the context will run on fairly and clearly, without need of help from any either superfluous supply, or overstrained coherence. So an interpreter of prime note renders it: and so is the particle used, Psal. 116. 10. compared with 2 Cor. 4. 13. and in this prophecy, Chap. 16. 5. and 20. 9.

*{of the King that sitteth upon the throne of David,}* Of Zedekiah, verse 3. whom David's throne shall not secure. See Chap. 22. 2.

*{and of all the people that dwelleth in this city, and of your brethren that are not gone forth with you into captivity}* *dwelleth,* or *abide, remain:* as Chap. 39. 14. *and,* even (as Esai 35. 4.) *your brethren that went not forth with you into captivity;* but were left behind with Zedekiah, Chap. 24. 8.

**Verse 17.** *{Thus saith the LORD of hosts,}* This attribute is added to give the more emphasis to the menace subjoined.

*{Behold, I will send upon them the sword, the famine, and the pestilence,}* Chap. 24. 10. and 27. 8. so that they shall be in worse case at Jerusalem, than you are in Babylon.

*{and will make them like vile figs that cannot be eaten, they are so evil}* Or, *so bad, so naught.* See Chap. 24. 8. and hence it seems to appear, that this prophecy, or epistle was penned and delivered some space of time after that there related.

*{make them}* Heb. *give them:* as Chap. 9. 10. or *I will deal with them:* as Hosea 11. 8. *How should I deal with thee.* So the words would there be rendered; and so here: for God made them not so vile and bad; but they by their wickedness having made themselves such, God justly resolves to deal with them, as men are wont to do with such vile fruit, and rotten stuff, as is good for nothing but the dunghill: the word rendered *vile,* is nowhere else in the concrete, or adjective, but in the abstract, or substantive Chap. 5. 30. and 18. 11. and 25. 14. See there.

**Verse 18.** *{And I will persecute them,}* Or, *pursue them:* the fitter term here: and so Psal. 35. 6. and 83. 15.

*{with the sword, and with the famine, and with the pestilence.}* As verse 17. with these evils will I follow them, whithersoever they go, and wheresoever they become. See Chap. 42. 16, 17. and 44. 12, 13.

*{and will deliver them to be removed to all the Kingdoms of the earth,}* So Deut. 28. 25. 2 Chr. 29. 8. See Chap. 15. 4. and 24. 9.

*{to be a curse and an astonishment, and an hissing, and a reproach}* Heb. *for a curse,* &c. as Chap. 24. 9. and 25. 4. and 34. 17.

*{among all the nations whither I have driven them}* As verse 14. or *whither I shall drive them:* as chap. 24. 9.

**Verse 19.** *{Because they have not hearkened unto my voice, saith the LORD, which I sent unto them, by my servants the Prophets, rising early and sending them, but ye would not hear, saith the LORD}* See chap. 7. 23–26. and 11. 7, 8. and 13. 11. and 17. 23. and 25. 4. a passage from person to person: as chap. 22. 24, 25, 27.
