*{in the day that I took them by the hand}* In this manner of speech implying, as their imbecility and weakness, having need then as younglings, and weaklings, to be led by the hand, so his own tender affection to them, and fatherly care of them, that did not drive them before him, like beasts or cattle, nor leave them behind him, and bid them come after him, as servants: but as an affectionate father takes his young weakling and darling child by the hand, and so leads him gently along with him as he is able to go. See Exod. 19.4. Deut. 3.10——12. Hos. 11.1, 3. Heb. *in the day* (or, *at,* or, *about, the time;* *day,* for, *time;* as Esay 29.1.) *of my taking them by the hand:* for it is an infinitive, not a verb finite, as the authors of our version seem to have taken it, supposing therefore a defect of the relative, which in a divers character they therefore needlessly express.

*{which my covenant they brake;}* By this adjection God implies, as their former disloyalty, and unfaithfulness concerning the former covenant; so withal a greater steadfastness that should be in this latter; as that which should be more firm and effectual in regard of persistance and continuance in it, than that former had been, which in a generality almost the whole body of them had so oft relinquished and abandoned, making revolt from God's service unto the worship of idols. See chap. 32.40. & 50.5. Esay 59.29.

*{although I was an husband unto them, saith the LORD.}* Heb. *and* (but so is the copulative oft used in a discretive or adversative notion, as Psal. 78.23. Esay 49.5. 1 Pet. 3.6. for it would there also in the last clause be so rendered) *I have married them;* for the verb is active: whereof see on chap. 3.14. a place parallel to this. I had taken them, and joined them unto me, as in a conjugal bond; and they had by solemn covenant obliged themselves to continue loyal to me; and yet did they notwithstanding break their faith, and dealt perfidiously and disloyally with me, chap. 3.20. Now though this interpretation be plain and familiar, suiting very fitly with the scope of the place, and course of the context, backed with that other place, and seconded by the Chaldee Paraphrast, and expressed by another word deduced from one that is used for an husband, so termed as *a companion,* joined to the wife in a bond of mutual society chap. 3.20. Hos. 3.1. as that here used from one, that imports an *husband,* as he is *owner* or *possessor* of her, Deut. 21.13. & 24.1, 3. Hos. 2.18. (see Esay 62.5.) Yet because the ancient Greek (whose words also the Apostle retains, Heb. 8.9.) renders it, *and I neglected them,* or *regarded them not;* and the old Latin. *I ruled over them;* hence divers interpreters beat and busy their brains, to make some other meaning of the words here used. And here some of prime note conceive it spoken by way of interrogation, with a kind of indignation, *And should I have continued an husband unto them?* as if he should say, I had no reason so to do, when they dealt so with me; and therefore I neglected them as they neglected me; I cast off them, as they cast off me. See chap. 3.8, 20. Others fastening on the Latin translation, render the words, *I domineered over them;* I dealt harshly and roughly with them; as, say they, the term of *ruling* is oft-times used; as, Psal. 110.2, 6. but the word here used is not there: they might better have alleged, Esay 26.13. But the matter it seems not here to admit it. One of the Jewish commenters tells us, that his father, of blessed memory, conceived the word *baalti,* to be taken as the word *bahalti,* or, *bachalti,* Zach. 11.8. and so renders it, *I loathed them,* or *abhorred them;* and so, says he, the word *baal,* is ever taken, when it is joined with *beth:* but of that his groundless criticism, see before on chap. 3.14. Howbeit, some taking hold of his fancy, would thence infer, that the text was by the authors of the Greek version so rendered; and others again, that it was anciently, neither the one of those, nor the other, but, *gaalti* that comes nearer to the now received reading, than that other of the Rabbi, and signifies the same with that, ch. 14.19.

Thus many ways men shift to and fro, and needlessly vex a plain reading, and trouble a clear text, to reconcile the Prophet and the Apostle, who retained the Greek version as he found it: having nothing in this clause contrary to that for which he alleged it, and speaking otherwise fully to that, for which he produced it. See the like, Esay 61.1.

**V. 33.** *{But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel; After those days, saith the LORD,}* Or, *But this is the covenant that I will make* (Heb. *cut:* as ver. 31.) *with the house of Israel* (and the house of Judah also jointly, with my whole Church of choice ones, vers. 31.) *after those dayes,* or, as some render it, *these dayes;* in the succeeding ages; in the times before spoken of, ver. 31. as having reference to the time, when this covenant should be made.

*{I will put my Law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts:}* He does not say, I will prescribe them another law, as if the law of the two tables were now to be utterly abandoned and abolished, and some other precepts substituted in the room of them. For our Savior himself informs us, that he came not to dissolve it, or the least tittle of it; and not only opens and clears much of it, but presses still the observation of it, as necessary and perpetual, Matth. 5.17——20, &c. But he promises to write that law in their hearts with the finger of his Spirit, which he had before time written in the tables of stone, whereby they should become conformable unto it, both in heart and life, Ezek. 11.19. and 36.26, 27. Heb. 8.9. So is *Gods Law* said to be in the *heart* of the godly, Psalm 37.31. and 40.8. See the like both allusion and expression, 2 Cor. 3.3. It is that in effect, though in a far larger extent to be made good, which God had beforetime promised by Moses, that upon their return, he would *circumcise the heart of them and their seed,* Deut. 30.6. to wit, with that inward circumcision, that is, not in the flesh, but in the spirit, Rom. 2.28, 29. Col. 2.11. See Chap. 4.4. For it is but a very slender sense, that a learned man here gives, to wit, that God's benefits conferred on them should be so great, that they could not possibly choose but mind him and his law.

*{and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.}* Heb. *I will be unto them for God, and they shall be unto me for people.* See the like form, Gen. 2.24. Judg. 17.10. 2 Sam. 7.14. I will take them as their sovereign Lord into my protection, and they shall yield me all willing subjection, loyalty and obedience, as my people. That which was the sum and substance of the ancient covenant, both before Moses, Gen. 17.7. and under him, Deut. 26.17, 18. and 29.13. chap. 7.23. and after him, chap. 24.7. & 30.22. Ezek. 11.20. and 36.28. but that spiritual grace is withal here promised, whereby they should be enabled to become God's people, not in title and profession alone, but in truth, John 1.47. Rom. 2.28, 29. Gal. 6.15, 16.

**V. 34.** *{And they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the LORD.}* This passage is not to be conceived, as if the meaning were, that they should need no teaching at all in those times; or that the office of teachers should then cease as superfluous: for while men live in this world, they know but in part, nor exactly indeed ought, 1 Cor. 8.2. and 13.19. nor can any, while they live here, attain to such an height of perfection, either in knowledge, or in grace, but that they may still grow in either, Phil. 3.12——15. 2 Pet. 3.18. and the office of teaching therefore is to continue to the world's end, Matth. 28.20. Eph. 4.11, 13. Yea, it is expressly said, in the prophecies of the very same times here intended, that people should call one upon another to repair together unto God's house there to be taught; by whom, but by his ministers? Esay 2.3. Mic. 4.2. But the question is then, how these words are to be understood: For answer whereunto, some render the words, *They shall not* only *teach one another;* as the like defect of the restrictive term is oft found omitted, Genes. 32.28. 1 Sam. 8.7. and so the meaning should be, that they should not be taught by their teachers alone, but God should cooperate together with their teaching, and instruct them inwardly by his Spirit, Esay 54.13. and 59.21. Joh. 6.45. 1 John 2.20, 27. Others conceive it to be understood, that none should ordinarily be so silly and ignorant, as not to have some competent measure of knowledge, of the main grounds, at least, and the first principles of saving truth, though having need further to be built up in the same, Heb. 6.1, 2. Others, that they should not need to be urged, or pressed upon the fear and service of God; they should be prone and forward to it of themselves; by *the knowledge of God,* after the Chaldee Paraphrast, understanding such a knowledge of him, as works in the heart a reverent dread and regard of him, and care to serve and obey him, chap. 22.16. 1 John 2.4. Others, that men shall not need to take so much pains and travel about teaching of the elect, as they had been constrained to take with the people in former times, and all to no purpose, Esay 28.9——13. the like manner of speech they suppose to be found, John 16.26. I conceive in this form of speech to be intimated; first, the great measure of clear light that should in those times be revealed, 2 Cor. 4.3, 6. Secondly, the great measure of knowledge that should by reason thereof abound, Esay 11.9. Hab. 2.14. Thirdly, the clearness of understanding, that many should so be possessed with, that they might seem rather to have been taught by some immediate irradiation, than by any means of instruction; as Gal. 1.12. Fourthly, the generality, or numerousness, at least of knowing persons, far above that, that had been in former times, and that even amongst the meaner sort. See Act. 18.25, 26. So in the next clause.

*{every man his neighbour, and every man his brother}* That is, simply, *one another.* See chap. 23.34.

*{for they shall know me from the least of them unto the greatest of them, saith the LORD}* Abundance of knowledge of God shall be among all sorts of them, as well the meaner sort as the greater, who have better natural endowments ordinarily, because better means of education and institution and more opportunity of intending the means of instruction. See chap. 5.4, 5. See Mat. 11.4, 5; 25. Rom. 1.14. 1 Cor. 1.26——28.

*{all know me}* As, *All taught of God,* Esay 54.13. Joh. 6.45. and, *all righteous,* Esay 60.21. which places and many other, imply a multitude of such in the Church, far above that which in former times had been: for to understand it simply, as some do, of the elect; though the doctrine be true, (for none but such so know God, as is here intended, nor are sincerely & soundly righteous) yet it reaches not the intent and scope of the places, which import a greater number than ordinary in other times of persons so qualified, whereas of the elect it would be true, were they never so few, or in those times no more of them, than had in any other age formerly been. The meaning is, that the knowledge of God should be much more common and familiar than in former times it had been, and that even among the meanest sort of people that were.

*{from the least to the greatest}* See of this proverbial form on Chap. 6.13. as all sorts there covetous and lying; so all sorts here, religious and knowing. See chap. 24.7.

*{for I will forgive their iniquity,}* Or, *when I shall forgive their iniquity;* as Chap. 11.23. and 13.21. as intimating that God forgives not sin to any, but such as know him in Christ, Esay 53.11. Psalm 36.10. See chap. 33.8. Mich. 7.18. Act. 10.43. Eph. 1.7.

*{and I will remember their sin no more.}* Or, *and shall remember their sin no more.* God where he forgives sin, forgets sin: no more regards it in some respects, than as if he had clean forgotten it. See on Esai 43.25. Ezek. 18.21, 22.

**V. 35.** *{Thus saith the LORD}* For the better assurance of the accomplishment of the foregoing gracious promises to his people, the Lord is pleased to give them further security in the words following, for the continuance of a seed with them, even to the world's end.

*{which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinance of the moon and of the stars for a light by night,}* Gen. 1.16. Psal. 136.8, 9.

*{which divideth the sea, when the waves thereof roar;}* Or as some, *who when I trouble the sea,* or, set it on working, *the waves thereof roar;* and one of the Jewish doctors here much to the same purpose, *that make the sea rough,* or, *rugged;* drawing in hither, that of Job, Job 7.5. *my skin is rugged,* or *wrinkled;* but neither is that word commonly deemed there so to signify: and the word, though being in the same form is transitive here, intransitive there. Others therefore rather, *that still,* or, *make quiet, the sea, when* (Heb. *and;* as Chap. 16.6.) *the waves thereof roar:* or, *that settle the sea,* (that is, keep it within compass, & make it rest within its bounds) *though the waves thereof roar.* See Chap. 5.22. and thus the rather I here take it, because he seems here to speak not of some extraordinary, or occasional act; as of dividing the Red Sea, Exod. 14.21. of the laying of tempests at some times, as Jon. 1.15. but of a constant course fixed concerning the creature, Gen. 9.15. Psal. 104.9. See on Esai 51.15.

*{the LORD of hosts is his name:}* Or, *whose name is the Lord of hosts;* as Esai 47.4. chap. 10.16.

**V. 36.** *{If these ordinances depart from before me, saith the LORD, then the seed of Israel shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.}* As sure as the course, which I have established in nature, for the constant motion and intercourse of the celestial creatures, and the confining of that vast body of the sea to the place assigned it, shall without interruption, or intermission persist unto the world's end, Psalm 72.5, 17. and 74.16. and 89.2, 6, 37. and 104.9, 19. and 119.89, 91. so as undoubtedly shall my Church and seed of Jacob in some of them adhering thereunto continue until the frame of the world itself be dissolved, Psalm 102.28. Mat. 16.18. and 24.34, 35. Rom. 11.3, 5, 26. As for that, which some add of God's continuance of the light of his word and Spirit shining forth in his Church, for the enlightening of men's minds, and directing of their lives, Psal. 19.7, 8. and 119.105, 130. Prov. 6.23. 2 Pet. 1.19. as those celestial bodies do in a constant course impart light unto the creatures here below; though it be true and solid, Esai 59.21. Mal. 4.2. 2 Cor. 4.6. Rev. 1.20. and 4.5. yet is beside the drift and intendment of this place.

*{these ordinances}* To wit, of the sun and the moon and the stars, says the Rabbine; but not of the sea: for the sea departed from its ordinary course when it stood on heaps, Exod. 14.21. and was here produced only to show, that as God wrought a new work then, so he would do the like here in refining his people, vers. 22, 23. Ezek. 36.26. But that ordinance of God concerning the bounding of the sea, at first settled, Gen. 1.9. and by solemn oath and covenant again after the flood established to continue for ever, seems rather here to be respected. See before on vers. 35. and Esai 54.9. and we need not therefore restrain it to the former only.

*{depart}* See Esai 54.10.

*{from before me}* Heb. *from to my face;* either ceasing to be, or being not looked after and regarded by me, and so left to an unsettled and confused course. See Esai 48.19. and 57.16. So in the next branch. See the like expressions, Chap. 33.20, 21, 25, 26.

*{cease from being a nation}* But that there shall be a multitude of them distinct from other people abiding in the world; to the world's end, as some: or, as others, that a Christian Church consisting of Jacob's seed, made up of Jews and Gentiles, shall continue so long, Matth. 16.18. and 28.20. or, as others again, that the Jewish people, when they shall be brought home unto Christ, they shall so persist without revolt to the last, Chap. 32.40.

*{for ever}* Heb. *all the dayes:* as Deut. 11.1. and 12.1.

**V. 37.** *{Thus saith the LORD, If heaven above can be measured, and the foundation of the earth searched out beneath, I will also cast off all the seed of Israel for all that they have done, saith the LORD}* As most sure it is, that these things cannot by any skill, or might of man be done; so certain is it that God will never cast off the whole race of Jacob.

*{If heaven above can be measured}* To wit, by man; for God is said to measure the heavens with his span; but withal implying that none beside him can do it, Esai 40.12. Heb. *if heaven above* (as Deut. 4.39.) *shall be measured:* but the word is taken potentially; as the like, Prov. 30.4. So also Esai 40.12. and 49.15. Nor need we, with a learned late writer, to have recourse to the third heaven, that above the stars, which the Apostle was rapt up unto, 2 Cor. 12.2. and whither Christ is now ascended, Eph. 4.10. for the Lord speaks, as before, of the celestial bodies, that are visible to the eye, verse 35. so here of that heaven, the vastness whereof is conspicuous to man's sight, and of which, what is here averred, is most true, that no man can make an exact dimension of it.

*{and the foundations of the earth searched out beneath,}* If men can, by search, pierce so far, and so deep, into the innermost parts of the earth, as to reach unto the very center thereof itself: for the verb is to be taken here potentially, as well as the former.

*{cast off all the seed of Israel}* This God never did, never will do; for some of them have still been, and shall ever be reserved, Rom. 11.1——5, 25——31.

*{for all that they have done}* Notwithstanding their manifold sins and iniquities, whereby, and for which, they have justly deserved to be utterly both cast off, and cut off, Lam. 3.22. Ezek. 36.32. but God in mercy would remit, vers. 34. Chap. 33.8.

**V. 38.** *{Behold the days come, saith the LORD,}* From hence to the end of this Chapter, is a prediction of the re-edification of Jerusalem, together with an exact delineation of the whole compass of the city. Heb. *Behold the dayes coming;* as before, vers. 31. But in this place, the Jewish masters, it seems, finding in some copies the word *coming* here wanting, were so scrupulous, that albeit they deemed it to have been by some escape omitted; yet would they not put it into the text, but left a blank for it with the vowel points underneath, and placed the head-letters in the margin.

*{that the city shall be built to the LORD}* The city Jerusalem shall *be built* again round about from the one end to the other, Esai 44.28. Neh. 3. and 12.28——40. *to the Lord,* or *for the Lord;* that the Lord may again dwell therein, and be served and worshiped there as formerly he had been: so vers. 40.

*{from the tower of Hananeel}* Whereof we find mention, as a place remarkable, Neh. 3.1. and 12.39. Zach. 14.10. This albeit, some learned late writers affirm to have been situate on the south side of Jerusalem; yet it is more generally deemed to have stood on the east side of the city: that which seems to receive strength from the course of the compass both here, and in Nehemy expressed; this *tower of Hananeel* being situate between *the tower of Meah,* and *the corner gate,* Neh. 3.1.

*{unto the gate of the corner}* Or, *the corner-gate:* which stood on the northeast corner of the city; as writers generally, for ought I find, agree: Of it, see 2 King. 14.13. 2 Chr. 26.9. Zach. 14.10.

**V. 39.** *{And the measuring line shall yet go forth over against it.}* Heb. *the line of measure* (as *a cane of measure,* Ezek. 40.3. and, *a cord of measure* Zach. 2.1.) *shall further go on,* or, *proceed forward of it,* or, *before it:* as the same term is used, Josh. 6.5, 20. for *straight forward;* or, as it is there rendered; because speaking of a person, *Straight before him.* For neither seems that there implied, that a learned man would gather from the term *further,* that the city should be built in a larger compass than formerly, the ancient limits of it being enlarged: for after the return from captivity, they repaired the walls according to the ancient situation and dimensions of them by towers, and gates, designed and distinguished, as here, so Neh. 3. and the word only has reference to the carriage on of the work: nor again is it intimated in the last term, as if having been begun on the one side, they should pass thence to the other over *against it:* as those two companies went over *against* one another, Neh. 12.38. but it notes rather a proceeding right on round about, taking their work still before them, as it came in their way.

*{upon the hill Gareb,}* Or, *unto* (as the particle is used, chap. 6.9. and 23.3.) *the hill of Gareb,* (for the word *hill* here governs, as *the hill of Jerusalem,* Esai 10.32.) the word signifies *a scab,* Lev. 21.20. and 22.22. Deut. 28.27. and it was so called, as some conjecture, as you would say, *the scabby hill;* because the lepers and lazers used to lie much thereabout: it is supposed to have lain on the north side of the city toward the east.

*{and shall compass about to Goath;}* Or, *it shall passe about* from thence *to Goath:* supposed to be so termed from its troublesome and difficult ascent: it is by some deemed to be the same with mount Golgotha, Mar. 27.33. lying on the west side of the city towards the north.

**V. 40.** *{And the whole valley of the dead bodies,}* A valley, as some think, not far from mount Golgotha, where were cast the carcasses of the persons there executed: As others, the valley of *Rephaim;* which, say they, signifies *dead men,* and lay on the west side of the city Josh. 15.8. but of that valley, and its name, see on Esai 17.5. Others taking their rise from the Chaldee understand it of *Tophet;* where, say they, the multitude of the Assyrians under Sennacherib were slain; but neither is there any certainty of that, (see on Esai 30.33.) and they seem far out of the way, when they affirm *Tophet* to have lain on the west side of the city.

*{and of the ashes}* The word here used, is ambiguous: for it signifies either *fat,* or, *ash:* for the term is singular; whence some of the Jewish doctors, taking it the former way, expound it, of the *fat* and burly-bodied Assyrians (the abstract for the concrete) whose corpses lay in Tophet: and the Chaldee Paraphrast makes of this and the former but one place: which the points, in the original, may seem to favor, carrying this on to that. But others of them affirm the latter to be the plain and simple notion of it here, and thereby to be meant that part of the valley, that was set apart and employed for the receipt of *ashes,* that came from the altar of burnt-offerings. Lev. 4.12. and 6.11. which is most probable: more at least, than that of others, who would draw it to Tophet, or Gehinnom, as so called from the *ashes* of the bodies there burnt, Chap. 7.31. and 19.5. which lay on the south side of the city, but near to the east. See Chap. 19.2. with Josh. 15.8.

*{and all the fields unto the brook of Kidron}* There is here some variety of reading: for in the text is written *hashsheremot,* which the Greek retaining, renders it *Assaremoth:* but because no such root as *sharam* is found in the Hebrew, some would cut it in two, and with somewhat ado would make it signify *the region,* or, *regiment of death,* not unlike unto that of *Adramyttium,* Act. 27.2. and what the Chaldee reads is uncertain: for he renders it by a word that signifies *pools,* or *water-courses,* which some would draw to those waterworks made by Ezekiah, 2 Chron. 32.30. But what ground for any such matter from the text, howsoever read? The Jewish master-critics, conceive not amiss, that by some scribe's regardlessness, taking one letter for another, being much alike in the Hebrew character, (the like whereunto, see on Chap. 2.20. and 17.4.) *sheremot* came to be written for *shedemot,* which signifies *fields:* many whereof lay on the south side of the city; as the *Fullers field,* Esai 7.1. and the *Potters field,* Matth. 27.7. See on Chap. 18.2. and 19.2. For that *the brook Kidron* (2 Sam. 15.3. Joh. 18.1.) ran on the east side of the city, is generally agreed.

*{unto the corner of the horse gate}* Of this gate, see 2 King. 11.16. Neh. 3.28. It was so called, as the Jewish commenters inform us, because by it the King's horses were wont to be ridden out, there being near unto it, a fair and large plain, in which they used to exercise and run them.

*{towards the East,}* Which as he began at, so he concludes with, giving in the whole compass of the city; whereby it appears that *the tower of Hananeel* stood on that side the city, contrary to that which some learned have without good ground deemed. See on vers. 38.

*{shall be holy unto the LORD}* Or, *it shall be* (as having reference unto the whole body of the city thus bounded and to be built) *holy* (Heb. *holinesse,* as Chap. 2.3.) *unto the Lord;* as if the whole city were now as the Temple had been formerly his house, his court, his palace, his Sanctuary. See vers. 38. Esai 52.1. & 63.18. Chap. 12.10. Zach. 14.20, 21. For it is somewhat too slender that some give it, as if the meaning only were, that the whole city should be full of, and ring again with the praises of God, Neh. 12.27——43.

*{it shall not be plucked up nor thrown down any more for ever.}* See somewhat the like, Esai 33.20. that is, say some, the city shall continue for a long time, being thus re-edified: but it is principally verified and accomplished in the Church of Christ, (whereof that city was a type, Gal. 4.25, 26.) which shall never be razed, Psal. 125.1, 2. Mat. 16.18.

## CHAPTER 32

**Verse 1.** *{The word which came to Jeremiah from the LORD,}* In this Chapter is a relation of a purchase of land made at God's appointment, by the Prophet, during his imprisonment, and the siege of the city ready to be given up, vers. 1——15. his prayer to God thereupon, vers. 16——25. and God's answer thereunto vers. 26. consisting of two parts; a denunciation of a speedy destruction of the city and state for their heinous and horrible sins, vers. 28——35. and a promise of restitution again after some time over, though it might seem never so unlikely, vers. 27, 36——44. In this verse, and the next, to make way thereunto, is the time of this prophecy, vers. 1. together with the condition of the city straitly besieged; and of the Prophet himself under restraint, vers. 2. with the cause for which he was restrained, vers. 3——5.

*{The word}* This has special reference to what follows, ver. 26. all before drives to that. See the like before, Chap. 14.1. and after, Chap. 40.1.

*{which came from Jeremiah to the LORD,}* Heb. *Was* to him; as chap. 21.1. So also, vers. 6.

*{in the tenth year of Zedekiah King of Judah}* The last but one of his reign; and the very last before the surprisal and sacking of the city by the Chaldeans, and the beginning of that deportation which thereupon ensued, 2 King. 25.2, 11.

*{which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar.}* Whose first year of absolute reign after his father's decease, concurs with part of the third, and part of the fourth of Jehoiakim's, Dan. 1.1. Chap. 25.1. his eighth year, with the deposition of Jehojacin, and advancement of Zedekiah, 2 King. 24.12, 17. and the nineteenth with the eleventh and last of Zedekiah, 2 King. 25.2, 8. Of his names, see before on chap. 21.2.

**V. 2.** *{For then the King of babylons army besieged Jerusalem;}* Heb. *And then the Army of the King of Babylon were besieging of,* or, *against Jerusalem.* Now his forces lay then in siege against the city: for the siege began in the ninth year of Zedekiah; but the city was not taken before his eleventh, 2 King. 25.1, 2. Chap. 39.1, 2. Ezek. 24.1.

*{and Jeremiah the Prophet was shut up in the Court of the prison, which was in the King of Judahs house.}* That is, say some, in the prison that was in the court of the King's house; as if there were some inversion in the words; but this seems needless & groundless; the *court* and the *Kings house* are distinguished in the text: nor is it the court of the King's house, but the court of the prison-house, though within compass of the King's house, wherein the Prophet then remained; being now at somewhat more liberty, though a prisoner still, than formerly he had enjoyed, while restrained to, and cooped up in the *cels,* or *wards,* chap. 37.16, 20, 21.

*{prison}* Heb. *custody,* or, *keeping;* as Mat. 14.3. See Neh. 3.25. and 12.39.

**V. 3.** *{For Zedekiah the King of Judah had shut him up, saying,}* The occasion of his imprisonment, the doing of his duty, the faithful delivery of God's message. Howbeit, we read nowhere Zedekiah himself is at any time related to have himself committed the Prophet; only he is said to have given order for the removal of him, at his own request, from a more loathsome prison to another more convenient one, where at present he was, Chap. 37.21. but what was done by his permission, and continued with his connivence, is not unjustly or undeservedly said to be done by him. See Chap. 37.15, 18. and 38.5.

*{Wherefore doest thou prophesy and say, Thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the King of Babylon, and he shall take it.}* The substance of that here related see foretold and denounced by the Prophet while yet at full liberty, Chap. 34.2——5. which then, it seems, had at first some good work upon the King and state for the present, but afterward belike proved the occasion of his commitment. See there. And see the like expostulation with the Prophet in the person of Jehoiakim, Chap. 36.29.

*{prophesy and say}* That is, *prophesie saying;* as, *stand and feed,* for, *stand feeding,* Esai 61.5.

*{Behold, I will give}* Heb. *Lo I am giving;* as Chap. 6.21. and *hand,* for, *power;* as Chap. 29.21. So ver. 4.

**V. 4.** *{And Zedekiah King of Judah shall not escape out of the hand of the Chaldeans, but shall surely be delivered into the hand of the King of Babylon.}* Though he do attempt and assay to make an escape, (as he did) yet shall he be taken by them, and delivered up to him, Chap. 39.5. Heb. *shall being given be given;* as Chap. 38.3. See Chap. 34.3.

*{and shall speak with him mouth to mouth,}* Heb. *and his mouth shall speak with his mouth.* See Chap. 39.5.

*{and his eyes shall behold his eyes.}* He shall see him face to face, or eye to eye; as Esai 52.8.

**V. 5.** *{And he shall lead Zedekiah to Babylon, and there shall be be until I visit him, saith the LORD.}* Until by natural and ordinary death I take him away: as Num. 16.29. for by the sword he was not to die Chap. 34.3.

*{though ye fight with the Chaldeans ye shall not prosper.}* No weapons or courses that you use, or take against them shall prevail, or avail to do you any good. See chap. 2.14. Esai 54.17.

**V. 6.** *{And Jeremiah said, the word of the LORD came unto me, saying,}* See ver. 1. The Prophet, having related the occasion of his imprisonment, and the time of it, does proceed to report a business moved to him, and transacted by him upon an apprehension of God's pleasure therein, about a bargain and sale of some land, which at that time might seem very unseasonable, and to the Prophet's great disadvantage, as not likely ever to be enjoyed either by him, or any his heirs.

**V. 7.** *{Behold Hanameel the son of Shallum thine uncle shall come unto thee, saying,}* God foretells him of his kinsman's purpose to repair to him, and move him to buy his land of him, that he might beforehand consider seriously of it, and apprehend withal for what purpose he had acquainted him with it.

*{Buy thee my field that is in Anathoth:}* *Buy thee;* as chap. 13.1. *my field:* for the Levites had a certain quantity of ground assigned them about each of their cities, Num. 35.3, 4. *in Anathoth;* that is, near unto it, (as Josh. 24.25, 26.) in the suburbs thereunto belonging; where Abiathar had fields sometime, 1 King. 2.26. and where Jeremy himself had lived, chap. 1.1. But there is some question here, how such fields could be sold: for the sale of them seems expressly prohibited, Lev. 25.34. But to this, some answer, that the meaning of that law is, that they might not be alienated, or sold to any other; the copulative prefixed retaining his proper notion, and the ground of the law rendered the same with the former there, vers. 33. because their *perpetual possession.* Some others understand it, that they might not be altered from their constant use, as converted to buildings, and so adjoined for enlargement to their cities. And others add, that the Levites might have other grounds and lands descending to them from mother, or grandmother, having no brethren: and that this might be some such parcel. See of Barnabas the Levite, Act. 4.36, 37.

*{for the right of redemption is thine to buy it.}* To have it before another; as being next of kin to him that desired to part with it, Lev. 25.25, 32.

**V. 8.** *{So Hanameel mine Uncles son came to me in the Court of the Prison, according to the word of the LORD, and said unto me, Buy my field, I pray thee, that is in Anathoth, which is in the country of Benjamin; for the right of inheritance is thine, and the redemption is thine: buy it for thyself}* Of *the prison-court.* see on ver. 2.

*{according to the word of the LORD}* Not of injunction to Hanameel, but of prediction to Jeremy.

*{in the country of Benjamin}* Or, *land*; as chap. 1.1.

*{the right of inheritance is thine.}* Heb. *is,* or *belongeth to thee:* you are to have it before another, as next heir to it. See Ruth. 3.12. and 4.3, 4.

*{and the redemption is thine,}* Heb. *is to thee:* and the possessions of the Levites might at any time be redeemed, Lev. 25.32.

*{Buy it for thyself}* That it may not pass to some other, upon your refusal; as Ruth 4.6, 8. or, *Buy it thee,* simply, as vers. 7. Such a motion, as might justly seem unseasonable, and a request somewhat unreasonable: to importune a friend to lay out money for land, that was, in likelihood, in the enemies' hands, who were shortly after to be masters of city and country, as the Prophet well knew, and had with confidence published, which his kinsman also could not be ignorant of, as being the known cause of his restraint, vers. 3. it is recorded indeed, that when Annibal was set down before Rome, and made full account to carry it, the ground on which his pavilion stood being offered to sale, was bought at a full value, Livy, lib. 26. and Florus, lib. 2. cap. 6. but that under hope yet, that he would be frustrate of his expectation; which with our Prophet was far otherwise, and the ground therefore of his proceeding in this disadvantageous purchase, is in the next words related.

*{then I knew that this was the word of the LORD}* Heb. *and I knew* (as Chap. 29.12.) *that a word of God,* or, *a businesse of God* (as 1 King. 12.24.) *it was:* the pronoun, for the verb substantive; as Chap. 10.3. I perceived by God's fore-acquainting me with his coming, that it was his mind and pleasure that I should deal and go through with him for it, though no express mention thereof had been made to me by God, verse 7. See the like, Act. 16.7, 9, 10.

**V. 9.** *{And I bought the field of Hanameel my uncles son, that was in Anathoth.}* Or, *So I bought the field that was in Anathoth, of,* or, *from, Hanameel mine uncles son.* For there is a trajection in the text: see the like, Chap. 11.16. and 18.7, 8. and 52.20.

*{and weighed him the money}* The manner being in those times to make payment, in greater sums especially, not so much by tale, as by weight. So Gen. 23.16. Zach. 11.12.

*{money}* Heb. *silver;* as Esai 55.2.

*{even seventeen shekels of silver}* Heb. *seven shekels and ten of silver;* and so the ancient Greek precisely gives it: and there is the like trajection to that before in the text: which not observed, has produced some misconstruction: for the Chaldee (whom also the Jewish doctors follow) renders it, *seven pounds and ten shekels of silver;* but that without any ground, or good probability: the old Latin ambiguously, *seven stateres* (a Greek coin of the same weight with the shekel, Mat. 17.27.) *and ten,* or, pieces of *silver;* as Mat. 26.15. But *seven shekels and ten* seems to be here no other, than *seventeen shekels:* (as, *four leaves,* or *five,* for, *four, or five leaves,* Chap. 36.33. so, 2 Cor. 13.1. two witnesses and three, for, two, or three witnesses.) the manner of the Hebrew being ordinarily to place the less number before the greater. So, *thirty and an hundred years,* Gen. 5.3. and *five years and an hundred years,* Gen. 5.6. and *silver* oft put alone for shekels of *silver;* as Judge 17.2. 2 Sam. 18.11. The Hebrew *shekel* weighing about our half crown, the sum amounts to some forty two shillings and six pence.

**V. 10.** *{And I subscribed the evidence,}* Or, *I engrossed it.* Heb. *I wrote in the book;* to wit, says the Jewish commenter, the words, or matter of the sale. I caused *a book,* or *a bill,* (as Mat. 19.7.) of bargain and sale to be made of it; or the bargain and sale to be solemnly entered and engrossed in a book: for that which some learned hence observe, that in those times there were no scriveners, or public notaries used commonly for such purposes, seems as groundless as that which some other gather; that in the Romans' courts men accused of criminal matters were not allowed counsel to plead for them, from Paul's speaking for himself, Act. 24.10.

*{and sealed it}* Heb. *and sealed.* *I writ, and sealed:* that is, I caused a writing to be drawn, subscribed and sealed: for the sealing, albeit it might be interchangeable, as in charter-parties is usual with us; yet the sealing of the deeds was principally required from the party that sold the land, and as the Rabbines here say, from the witnesses who were to testify the sale.

*{and took witnesses,}* Heb. *I caused witnesses to witnesse;* as Esai 8.2. and so ver. 25. See Ruth 4.9.

*{and weighed him the money in the balances.}* Or, *weighed out the money* (Heb. *silver;* as verse 9.) *in a balance;* (of which term see on Esai 40.12.) in the presence of those witnesses, who might testify, as well the payment of the money, as the agreement and bargain.

**V. 11.** *{So I took the evidence of the purchase}* Or, *Then* (Heb. *And;* as Chap. 28.5, 9.) took I *the evidence* (Heb. *the book;* as ver. 10.) *of the purchase.* So ver. 12.14, 16.

*{both that which was sealed according to the law and custom, and that which was open.}* That there were two several deeds, or instruments concerning this bargain and sale, and consequently in conveyances of the like nature, is from hence apparent: though it be not so clear, of what nature and use they were, or wherein they differed the one from the other: and learned men therefore do somewhat vary in their, either conjectures, or assertions, about them. One of the Jewish doctors (whom some also of ours follow) seems to make them for substance the same, only the one sealed up and kept close; the other being an exact copy thereof left open, that use might upon any emergent occasion be made of it, without breaking up the other. Another says, that the latter was to make known what had been done unto such other of the kin, as had right, or might desire to redeem it again. A third, that the one, to wit, *that sealed,* was made up in private at the time of the contract; the other was to be rendered to the judges in public, called therefore the *open one,* because it was openly published in the court, and by the judges' subscription, and consignation, made authentical: and this way also some of ours seem to go. Others would have in the one writing contained an express narration of God's injunction made out to the Prophet for the making of this purchase; together with an exact description of all passages concerning the purchase itself; the other, so much only, as was necessarily required for the passing of it in the civil court. Another learned man conceives, that in the one, which was showed open to the witnesses, that they might know between whom and whereabout the bargain was made, there was so much only recorded in general: whereas in the other which was sealed up, were contained divers further particularities, which they would not have to be so commonly known. And a latter learned writer would have here several books here mentioned, to wit, 1. The book of the purchase, containing the condition of the land to be bought, and the sum of money to be given for it. 2. The book sealed, wherein the bargain and sale were obsignated, and the right declared that Jeremy had to purchase it. 3. A public instrument of ratification of the whole. But I suppose rather with the Jewish commenters, that the word *book* in the front of the verse is collective, and takes in to it both the *sealed* one and the *patent;* as the very course of the context carries it: and I conceive those words *according to the precept and the ordinances,* to have relation as well to the one counterpart as the other; there being such a trajection in the words as was before, verse 9. So that it is, as if it had been said; *the books of the purchase, that sealed, and that patent,* both made *according to the precept and the ordinances;* that is, according to the prescript of God's law concerning such sales, and the ordinances about the same. Nor can I accord with those learned men that disjoin these two terms, by the one understanding the particular *command* that God had given in charge to the Prophet for the making of this purchase; by the other, the *ordinances* that God had enacted concerning such transactions in general, Lev. 25. See the like defect of the term of collation, Chap. 2.28.

**V. 12.** *{And I gave the evidence of the purchase unto Baruch, the son of Neriah the son of Maaseiah,}* Or, *And I delivered* (as ver. 16.) *the deed* (Heb. *book,* as vers. 11.) *of the purchase unto Baruch,* the Prophet's scribe and attendant, Chap. 36.4, 26. described here by his parentage, *the son of Neriah the son of Maaseiah;* and in like manner runs Seraiah's pedigree, Chap. 51.59. *the son of Neriah the son of Maaseiah.* Howbeit, the Hebrew here exhibits not *Maaseiah,* but *Mahseiah,* or *Machseiah,* which is a divers name.

*{in the sight of Hanameel mine uncles son,}* Heb. *to the eyes* (as Chap. 28.5.) *of Hanameel mine uncle:* but the word *son* is wanting; for he was before called *his uncles son,* vers. 7, 8. which to sample, the Jewish doctor fetches hither that of Lot, where Lot is called Abraham's *brothers son,* Gen. 12.5. and 14.12. and again *his brother,* Gen. 14.14. to which may be added the like of Zedekiah, called Jehojacin's *uncle,* 2 King. 24.17. and yet *his brother,* 2 Chron. 36.10. but the word *brother* is of larger extent; and neither therefore so well matches with this. That the word *son* is to be supplied, I suppose that no doubt is to be made: for the Rabbines' conjecture, that this Hanameel should be another of that name, uncle to the Prophet does carry no show of probability with it.

*{and in the presence of the witnesses, who had subscribed the book of the purchase,}* Heb. *to the eyes* (as before, and so after again) *of the witnesses, who had written in the book of the purchase,* ver. 10.

*{before all the Jews that sat in the court of the prison.}* In the presence of such as came to see, or hear the Prophet, and were staying there at that time in the court. See ver. 2. *to sit,* for, *to stay;* as Deut. 9.9. Ezr. 10.9.

**V. 13.** *{And I charged Baruch before them, saying,}* Heb. *to their eyes;* as ver. 12.

**V. 14.** *{Thus saith the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel,}* As Chap. 27.4.

*{Take these evidences, this evidence of the purchase, both which is sealed, and this evidence which is open;}* Heb. *books,* and *book:* as before, ver. 10, 12. See on ver. 11.

*{and put them in an earthen vessel that they may continue many days.}* That they may be kept safe, and being preserved from rotting and perishing by injury of air, or moisture (as the girdle did, Chap. 13.7.) they may last a long time, and be produced again, when occasion should be to make use of them. Heb. *that they may stand* (as Ps. 119.91.) *many dayes,* for, a long time; as Hos. 3.4.

**V. 15.** *{For thus saith the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel;}* As verse 14.

*{Houses, and fields, and vineyards, shall be possessed again in this land.}* Or, *shall be bought;* as ver. 44. Though the city shall be taken, the state subverted, and the people, a great part of them, carried away to Babylon, where they shall for many years abide in bondage; yet shall they, after the time by God assigned for their captivity expired, return to enjoy their possessions again: that which God would give assurance of by this act of the Prophet; and upon the thing executed, does now acquaint them with, and enjoins him to make known unto the people. See ver. 37.43, 44.

**V. 16.** *{Now when I had delivered the evidence of the purchase unto Baruch the son of Neriah, I prayed unto the LORD, saying,}* Heb. *And I prayed unto the Lord after I delivered the book,* &c. *{saying,}* a trajection; as ver. 9, 11.

**V. 17.** *{Ah Lord GOD, thou hast made heaven and the earth by thy great power and stretched out arm}* Gen. 1.1. Psalm 146.6. See Chap. 27.5.

*{and there is nothing too hard for thee.}* Heb. *no word* (for, *no thing;* as Deut. 17.8. Chap. 22.4. and 26.2. Luke 1.37.) *is hidden from thee;* as Deut. 30.11. or, *is wonderfull with thee;* as Psal. 118.25. that is, is difficult with you, or too hard for you to effect. So the phrase is used, because things that we deem impossible, or over-hard, seem strange to us, and are wont to be matter of wonderment with us; but are not so with those, that can easily effect them, Zach. 8.6. and in Scripture language to *know,* is as much as *to be able to do;* as Esai 7.16. and 8.5. Chap. 6.15. and 8.12. 2 Pet. 2.9. So Gen. 17.8. and hereafter again, ver. 37. See Job 42.2. Mat. 19.26. Mar. 14.36. Luke 1.37.

**V. 18.** *{Thou shewest loving kindness unto thousands,}* Even of their issue, whom you specially affect out of free love to their progenitors, Exod. 20.6. and 34.7. Deut. 5.10. and 7.7, 8.

*{and recompensest the iniquity of the fathers into the bosom of the children after them:}* Punishing the parents oft in their posterity, either to increase their grief surviving to see it, John 7.15, 24. 1 Sam. 2.33, 34. or to make them exemplary and monuments of his wrath unto others, 1 King. 14.10, 11. and 21.21, 22. So Deut. 20.6. and 37.7. Num. 14.18.

*{into the bosom}* Or, *lap,* Prov. 16.31. repaying it plentifully at last, though it seem long ere it light. See Esai 65.7.

*{of their children after them}* Even when they are dead and gone, 2 Sam. 21.6, 8. 2 King. 5.27. and 9.7——9. and 10.10. and 24.4.

*{the great, the mighty God.}* Or, *the God that is great, that is mighty;* (for the article thus repeated in the latter place usually has the notion of the relative. See Esai 5.16. Deut. 10.17. Neh. 9.32. Psal. 145.3. Esai 9.6. Tit. 2.13.

*{the LORD of Hosts is his name.}* Or, *whose name is the Lord of Hosts;* as Chap. 31.35. and 48.15. Amos 4.13.

**V. 19.** *{Great in counsel, and mighty in work.}* Heb. *doing;* as Ps. 66.5. See Esai 9.6. and 28.29.

*—{for thine eyes are open upon all the ways of the sons of men}* Or, *whose eyes* (Heb. *whose thine eyes,* by an elegant redundancy) *are open* (that is, who has your eyes *open) upon all the wayes of the sons of men.* Heb. *of Adam;* as Job 25.6. Psal. 90.3. noting God's incessant providence continually and constantly without intermission, overlooking all the courses of each particular person, as well as of all mankind in general, Job 34.22. Psalm 33.13, 14. and 119.168. Prov. 5.21. and 15.3. Chap. 16.17. and the parenthesis here is needless.

*{to give unto every one according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.}* Heb. *to give to a man,* for, *to each one,* as chap. 18.11. and 22.7. God is no idle spectator of what men do; but sees to take notice of their courses and carriages, and accordingly either to prosper, or punish, Psalm 62.12. Chap. 17.10. and 25.14.

*{fruit}* For, *effect,* or *reward,* that follows the work; as the fruit springs from the seed, and is proportionable to it, of the same nature and quality with it. So Prov. 1.31. and 31.31. chap. 6.19.

**V. 20.** *{Which hast set signs and wonders in the land of Egypt,}* Or, *Who didst set signes and wonders,* &c. Ps. 74.43. & 106.22. & 135.9.

*{even unto this day;}* The memory whereof endures still unto these times, and will never be forgotten, Psal. 78.4, 6. and 111.4.

*{and in Israel}* Among your own people especially. See Psal. 78. and 105. and 106.

*{and amongst other men}* Heb. *Adam,* or *Man,* taken collectively: as Psal. 144.4. not among his own people alone; but among other nations also. See the like defect, 2 Chr. 32.22. Job 8.12. Cant. 4.9. Esai 26.13.

*{and hast made thee a name}* *To get thee renown;* as Esai 63.12. So the copulative is oft used in a final notion; as Josh. 24.9. Mal. 1.9.

*{as at this day.}* Or, *as* appears *this day.* So chap. 25.18.

**V. 21.** *{And hast brought thy people Israel out of Egypt with signs and with wonders, and with a strong hand, and with a stretched out arm, and with great terror:}* Or, *And broughtest,* or *didst bring,* &c. Exod. 6.6. Deut. 4.34. 2 Sam. 7.23. 1 Chro. 17.21. Psalm 136.10——12.

**V. 22.** *{And hast given them this land}* Or, *And didst give them,* or, *gavest them, this land,* Psal. 105.44. and 136.21, 22.

*{which thou didst swear to their fathers to give them,}* Or, *hast sworn,* Psal. 105.9——11. chap. 11.5.

*{a land flowing with milk and honey.}* Abounding with most pleasant fruit, and plenty of all good things, Num. 13.27. and 16.14. Deut. 6.3. and 8.7——9.

**V. 23.** *{And they came in, and possessed it,}* Neh. 9.24.

*{but they obeyed not thy voice,}* Heb. *and they hearkned not to thy voice,* Chap. 7.24. Neh. 9.26.

*{neither walked they in thy law;}* According to the rule and prescript of it; as Psal. 119.1.

*{they have done nothing of all that thou commandedst them to do:}* Or, *they did nothing,* &c. that it may run in the same tenor with the rest. Heb. *all that thou commandedst them to do, they did not;* *all,* for, *ought;* as chap. 42.21.

*{therefore hast thou caused all this evil to come upon them.}* Which at present they sustain in the spoil of their land, and siege of their city, vers. 2, 24.

**V. 24.** *{Behold the mounts}* Or, *ramparts,* as some; or *engins,* of battery, to discharge shot and artillery, such as were in use before the invention of guns, and use of such ordinance as we now have. See 2 Chr. 26.15. Esai 37.33. So chap. 33.4.

*{they are come unto the city to take it, and the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans that fight against it,}* The Chaldean forces be set down with their warlike engines before the city: and the city is given for lost, it is as good as surrendered and taken already, as sure to be taken as if already surprised. So chap. 9.1. and 37.10. *hand,* for, *power,* as ver. 3, 4.

*{because of the sword, and of the famine, and of the pestilence:}* The first destroying without, the other two devouring and disabling to hold out, within, chap. 21.9. & 28.8. Heb. *from the face of,* or, *from before;* as chap. 25.16, 37.

*{and what thou hast spoken is come to passe,}* See Esai 14.24.

*{and behold thou seest it.}* Heb. *seeing it:* the pronoun wanting, as chap. 7.11.

**V. 25.** *{And thou hast said unto me, O Lord GOD, buy thou the field for money, and take witnesses:}* Or, *yet;* as chap. 23.21. notwithstanding that such is the condition of our state, that all is as good as lost, and no man like to enjoy ought that he either purchases, or is possessed of, yet you bid me buy land: for though God did not expressly enjoin him so to do; yet by the carriage of the business, he well knew it was God's will that he should do it, ver. 8.

*{for the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.}* This connection is nothing suitable to the subject matter: it would rather be, *when as the citie is given;* as the particle is rendered, Gen. 4.11. Psal. 102.16. *or* albeit, or *though the citie be given;* as it is rendered, Josh. 17.18. Ps. 23.4. and would be, Gen. 8.21. for the coherence is so more natural there than here: *hand* again, for *power;* as v. 24.

**V. 26.** *{Then came the word of the LORD unto Jeremiah, saying,}* Heb. *And the word of the Lord was unto Jeremiah;* as Chap. 1.2. And this is the word specially designed and aimed at in the beginning of this Chapter; which all the foregoing discourse and matter, intervening between this and that, tended to bring in. See on vers. 1.

**V. 27.** *{Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh:}* Or, *the Lord God of all flesh:* of every creature, Gen. 6.13. and 7.21. or rather of all mankind: as Gen. 6.12. Psal. 145.2. Rom. 3.20. which as he made at first, so he guides and governs at his pleasure; and as he sends them out when he will, so he can bring them back again when he sees good, Act. 17.25, 26, 28. Nor is he the God of their *flesh,* but of their spirits too, Num. 16.22. but the meaner part is the whole man described by, as Gen. 6.3. to imply man's disability to do ought against God, or to hinder his disposal of ought, Psal. 56.6.

*{is there any thing too hard for me?}* See before, vers. 17.

**V. 28.** *{Therefore thus saith the LORD, Behold, I will give this city into the hand of the Chaldeans, and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar King of Babylon, and he shall take it.}* As before vers. 3.

**V. 29.** *{And the Chaldeans that fight against this city, shall come and set fire on this city, and burn it;}* So Chap. 37.10.

*{with the houses upon whose roofs they have offered incense unto Baal, and poured out drink offerings unto other gods to provoke me to anger.}* One main cause of this great evil: see Chap. 7.18. and 19.13.

**V. 30.** *{For the children of Israel, and the children of Judah have only done evil before me from their youth:}* Heb. *have been onely doing that which is evil in mine eyes* (as Chap. 7.30. and 18.10.) *from their youth:* ever since they were first a people. See Chap. 2.2. and 22.21. Esay 43.8. they have not only failed in matter of omission, refusing to do that I required of them, verse 23. but they have given themselves incessantly to the practice of those things that I professed to be offensive and displeasing unto me, as if their minds were set on nothing else. See the like, Gen. 6.5. and 8.21.

*{for the children of Israel have only provoked me to anger with the work of their hands, saith the LORD.}* Heb. *have been onely provoking me:* They have been continual matter of provocation to me with their idols; as if they intended and minded nothing else, but how to anger me. See chap. 25.6, 7. and further, ver. 31.

**V. 31.** *{For this city hath been unto me, as a provocation of mine anger, and of my fury, from the day that they built it, even unto this day.}* Heb. *For this city hath been upon anger, and upon wrath, unto me.* (See Esai 65.5.) that is, the inhabitants of this city have been from time to time angring of me, ever since this city was built; (for the verb is indefinite; as the like, Mal. 1.4. Luke 12.20.) to wit, by Solomon, who so enlarged and beautified it, that he might seem to have made a new city of it, and not long after polluted it with idol-worship, 1 King. 11.4——8. so the children of Israel are said to have built Rameses, Exod. 1.11. though founded long before, Gen. 47.11. and Nebuchadnezzar Babylon, Dan. 4.30. though at first founded by Nimrod, Gen. 10.10.

*{that I should remove it from before my face,}* Or, *out of my sight;* as chap. 23.39. and 31.36. Of this form of speech, see on chap. 7.18. and 27.10. and the like, vers. 29.

**V. 32.** *{Because of all the evil of the children of Israel, and of the children of Judah, which they have done to provoke me to anger, they, their Kings, their Princes, their Priests, and their Prophets, and the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem,}* As if all sorts of them had conspired to join together in an angring of God, Chap. 2.26. and 8.10. 2 Chro. 36.14. Heb. *man of Judah;* as Esai 5.5.

**V. 33.** *{And they have turned unto me the back, and not the face;}* Heb. *the neck,* properly, the hinder part of it. See chap. 2.27.

*{though I taught them rising up early, and teaching them, yet they have not hearkened to receive instruction.}* Heb. *and;* or, *and though* (the copulative in a twofold notion; as chap. 13.12.) *teaching* I taught them, (that is, I constantly taught them: the verb is an infinitive; and of such forms, see Esai 59.11, 13.) *rising up early and teaching;* (sedulously taking pains with them, and using all diligence about them, by my Prophets, Chap. 7.13. and 25.3. and 26.3. and 29.19. See 2 Chr. 36.15.) *and,* or, *yet* (as chap. 27.15.) *are they not hearing,* or, *hearkning* (as Chap. 44.16. they continue still heedless and regardless of ought, refusing) *to receive instruction.* Chap. 2.30. and 5.3. and 7.24. See 2 Chr. 36.16. Esai 65.3.

**V. 34.** *{But they set their abominations in the house which is called by my name, to defile it}* Heb. *And they set,* or, *They set also,* as chap. 29.20. for he proceeds here to a further degree of their impiety) *their abominations,* see chap. 66.17.) *in the house which my name is called upon it,* (as chap. 2.10, 11, 14.) *to defile it,* 2 Chr. 36.14.

**V. 35.** *{And they built the high places of Baal, which are in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to cause their sons and their daughters to passe through the fire unto Moloch, which I commanded them not, neither came it into my mind, that they should do this abomination, to cause Judah to sin,}* See chap. 7.31. and 19.5. but *Molec* (as Lev. 18.21. and 20.2.) here, instead of Baal there: whereby it appears that *Molec* and *Baal* are used promiscuously, and in a kind of generality, the one containing the notion of *a King,* whence the ambiguity, Zeph. 1.5. the other of *an Owner, Lord, Master,* or *Husband.* See chap. 2.23. *to passe,* as Lev. 18.21. to wit, *thorow the fire:* a defective speech, supplied, 2 King. 16.3. *to cause to passe thorow the fire,* for, *to burn;* as it is Chap. 19.5.

**V. 36.** *{And now therefore thus saith the LORD the God of Israel concerning this city, whereof ye say it shall be delivered into the hand of the King of Babylon by the sword, and by the famine, and by the pestilence.}* This version rendering the particle here used as an illative, makes no very good coherence, as if it were said, Because this people have dealt thus wickedly with me, I will therefore deal graciously with them. But to make the connection suitable to the subject matter, it would be rendered as a discretive; (whereof see on chap. 30.16.) *Yet now notwithstanding* all this their extreme impiety & pertinacy in evil, *thus saith the Lord the God of Israel,* he that yet owns this people, having a poor remnant among them, *concerning this city,* which yourselves have given for lost now, having no hope to hold it out, being in such condition as it is; See ver. 24, 28, 29. For God proceeds here to acquaint them with what after-good he intended to them, though they deserved nothing less; and so withal to satisfy Jeremy concerning the purchase that he had caused him to make, ver. 43, 44.

**V. 37.** *{Behold, I gather them out of all countries whither I have driven them in mine anger, and in my fury, and in great wrath:}* Heb. *Behold, I am gathering* (as Esai 56.8.) *them;* to wit, those of *Israel* and of *this city,* ver. 36.) I have a full purpose to recollect them *out of all those countries, whither I shall have driven them;* for he speaks of those that were yet abiding in the land and in the city. See Chap. 16.15. and 23.3. and 29.14. Ezek. 11.17.

*{and I will bring them again unto this place, and I will cause them to dwell safely.}* Heb. *in,* or, *unto confidence;* securely, confidently, without fear; as Esai 14.30. and 47.8. So Chap. 23.6. and 33.16. Ezek. 34.28.

**V. 38.** *{And they shall be my people, and I will be their God.}* See Ezek. 36.28. Chap. 24.7. and 30.22. and 31.33.

**V. 39.** *{And I will give them one heart,}* Ezek. 11.19. I will make them of one mind, Act. 4.32. Eph. 4.3——6. Phil. 2.1. or all in regard of newness of heart alike, Ezek. 11.19. and 36.26, 27.

*{and one way}* Both of worship and of life, Ezek. 11.19. and 36.27.

*{that they may fear me for ever,}* That is, serve me for ever: religious fear and reverence being the ground and qualification of all sincere service, and duty acceptable to God, Deut. 5.29. Psal. 2.8. Eccl. 12.13. Heb. 12.28. Heb. *all the dayes,* or, *all their dayes;* as Deut. 6.24. and 11.1.

*{for the good of them, and of their children after them.}* So Deut. 4.44. and 5.29. the surest way of laying a foundation of welfare for posterity, Psal. 37.26. and 115.13, 14.

**V. 40.** *{And I will make an everlasting covenant with them,}* Heb. *I will cut out with them a covenant of perpetuity.* See Esai 61.8. chap. 31.31. Ezek. 39.29.

*{that I will not turn away from them to do them good}* Heb. *that I will not turn from after them that I do them good.* I will never surcease to pursue and follow them with favors incessantly, Zach. 8.15. So, *to turn from after God,* Zach. 1.6.

*{but I will put my fear in their hearts,}* Heb. *and* (which would do better than the discretive here) *my fear;* that is, *the fear of me:* as, *thy fear,* for, *the fear of thee,* Psalm 5.7.) *will I give into their hearts;* as Ezek. 36.26, 27.

*{that they shall not depart from me}* That they may continue constant with me, and not constrain me by their apostasy to break again with them. I will so deeply rivet a reverent dread of me into their souls, as shall cause them to cling and cleave fast unto me, and to keep close with me for ever. See Psalm 80.18. and 86.11. Esai 59.21. ver. 39. chap. 50.5. whence may well be gathered, that when this people shall be brought home unto Christ, they shall never fall off from him again, Esai 59.20, 21.

**V. 41.** *{Yea, I will rejoice over them to do them good,}* Or, *And I will rejoice over them,* (as Esai 62.5. Zeph. 3.17.) *in doing them good;* as Deut. 28.63.

*{and I will plant them in their land assuredly with my whole heart, and with my whole soul.}* Heb. *in truth,* or *stability,* (as Hos. 2.20.) *with all my heart, and with all my soul:* as Deut. 6.5. and 10.12. I will settle them firmly in their land again, Chap. 24.6. & 31.28. and what I do for them, I will do it entirely and affectionately; as they also in like manner shall seek to and serve me, Chap. 24.7. Psal. 119.2, 10.

**V. 42.** *{For thus saith the LORD, Like as I have brought all this great evil upon this people,}* Which is in part already befallen them, and is ready further to seize upon them. See chap. 44.2.

*{so I will bring upon them all the good that I have promised them.}* So Zach. 8.14, 15. Chap. 29.10. and 31.28.

**V. 43.** *{And fields shall be bought in this land, whereof ye say, It is desolate, without man, or beast, it is given into the hand of the Chaldeans.}* Heb. *And,* or, *Then* (as Chap. 29.12.) *shall be the field be bought* (either *this field* in particular, which you now deal for, vers. 9. or *fields,* in general, vers. 44. the word *field* taken collectively; as chap. 7.20. and 9.21.) *in this land, of which ye say, desolation it is,* or *it will be* (as chap. 4.27.) *without man and beast;* as chap. 33.10, 12. which you make no other account of, but that being overrun with the Chaldeans, it will become such a waste. See ver. 36.

**V. 44.** *{Men shall buy fields for money}* Or, *Fields,* I say, *shall be bought.* Heb. *they shall buy* (the verb taken indefinitely, as chap. 31.23.) *for silver,* (as ver. 9, 25.) land shall again be bought and sold, as in times past, ver. 15.

*{and subscribe evidences and seal them, and take witnesses,}* Heb. *and* (or, *both;* as chap. 5.24.) *writing in books, and sealing, and causing witnesses to witnesse:* or, *and writing* they shall write, *and sealing* they shall seal, *and taking witnesses* they shall take witnesses; as Chap. 7.9. bargains of sale shall be made, with all usual solemnities and means of assurance. See ver. 10.

*{in the land of Benjamin,}* Where Anathoth was situate. See chap. 1.1. and which had continued one with Judah, 2 Chr. 11.12. See chap. 17.26. and 33.13.

*{and in the places about Jerusalem}* Where this sale is now made, and which is ready to be surprised, ver. 8, 9.

*{and in the cities of Judah}* That are most of them taken already, chap. 34.7.

*{and in the cities of the mountains, and in the cities of the valley, and in the cities of the South:}* Or, *both* (as before, and Psal. 76.6. chap. 31.13.) *in the cities of the mountains, and in the cities of the lowland, and in the cities of the upland;* in all the cities of both these tribes, whether situate above on the hills, or below in the vale, or in a middle posture between those two: of which division, see on chap. 17.26.

*{for I will cause their captivity to return}* Though I suffer them to be carried away captive from their land for a time; yet will I bring them back from captivity again. See ver. 3. chap. 30.3.

## CHAPTER 33

**Verse 1.** *{Moreover the word of the LORD came unto Jeremiah the second time, while he was yet shut up in the Court of the Prison, saying,}* This prophecy, as it is very near of the same date with the next foregoing; so is it much of the same subject matter with it, and with that before it, contained in Chapter 30. and 31. all three penned principally for the comfort and support of the faithful, against that long and tedious captivity ready now to surprise them, and amidst those grievous pressures that during it they were to endure, with many gracious promises of preservation and restitution, together with a constant continuance of a settled estate under the Messias to abide unto the world's end. Heb. *And the word of God was unto Jeremiah;* as chap. 1.11.

*{the second time}* As chap. 1.13. this being either the second revelation that he had during his restraint; or the second, as some, of the same subject with the former.

*{while he was yet shut up}* Heb. *and he was yet shut up;* as, *and he reigned,* for, *while he reigned,* 1 King. 11.25.

*{in the Court of the Prison}* See chap. 32.2.

**V. 2.** *{Thus saith the LORD the maker thereof, the LORD that formed it to establish it,}* That is, as some of the Jewish commenters, and some that follow them, he that made Jerusalem, (before mentioned, chap. 32.44.) and formed it, and made it not to be ruined, but to stand and continue, at least not to let it lie always ruined. See Esai 22.11. and 37.26. But others rather of either rank understand it of the promise of restitution, rendering the words, *the Lord that doth, the Lord that formeth,* (or contrives it, with a purpose) *to establish it,* to perform and make good that his gracious promise of restauration before propounded, chap. 31.37, 44. and now again here reiterated with further assurance given of it, verse 6, 7. See Esai 46.11.

*{the LORD is his name}* Or, *whose name is Jehovah,* Psal. 83.18. Esai 42.8. one able to give being to whatsoever he does promise, or purpose, Esai 14.24. and 44.26——28. and 46.10. the demonstrative for the relative; as verse 3.

**V. 3.** *{Call unto me, and I will answer thee;}* This some conceive spoken, as to God's people, to encourage them to seek unto God, with assurance of success in their suits; fetching in hither those places, Esai 42.9. and 46.10. and 48.3——7. But the most take the words rather as spoken to the Prophet, encouraging him to seek for further revelations from God, concerning those favors, which in future times he purposed to confer upon his people. Howbeit, I conceive not, with the Jewish doctor, that they contain any revocation of the former inhibition of prayer and intercession in the people's behalf, chap. 7.16. and 11.14. and 14.11. for that concerned only their present deliverance; this their future re-establishment.

*{answer thee}* According to your desire.

*{and shew thee great and mighty things, which thou knowest not}* Or, *great and hidden,* or, *abstruse and reserved things:* as, *there is nothing reserved,* or, *restrained from thee,* Job 42.2. See Esai 48.6.

*{which thou knowest not.}* Heb. *thou knowest them not:* the demonstrative for the relative; as ver. 2. So also Esai 48.6. or, as some, *which thou acknowledgest not;* which in regard of your weakness you are not able to conceive, as having some glance at his former debate with God, chap. 32.25. But the plainer notion seems here the better.

**V. 4.** *{For thus saith the LORD the God of Israel, concerning the houses of this city, and concerning the houses of the Kings of Judah, which are thrown down by the mounts, and by the sword.}* Before God comes to impart unto the Prophet his gracious purposes concerning the deliverance of this people in future times, he first acquainted him with those calamities that were suddenly to befall them, and which they should not by any means be able to avoid or escape: as before the like, Chap. 32.28, 29.

*{concerning the houses}* As, *concerning Judah and Jerusalem,* Esay 1.1. & 2.1.

*{of the Kings of Judah}* Wherein their kings have successively dwelt: or, *Kings,* for, *Princes.* See chap. 17.19. and 19.13.

*{are thrown down}* As some, by themselves, to raise fortifications, and make places of defense against the enemy; as Esay 22.10. or, that are to be thrown down, as sure to be demolished, as if already they were, by the enemies' assault, or upon their surprisal of them: as, *destroyed,* for, ready to be *destroyed,* Psal. 137.8. *perished,* for, ready to perish, Esay 27.13. *slain,* for, out of hand to be slain, Chap. 9.1. this rather; because that for which the cure and recovery was promised, verse 6.

*{by the mounts}* Heb. *to the mounts,* or *engines,* which some therefore render *for;* as Ezek. 6.9, 11. & 21.12. & 27.31. understanding it of fortifications raised for defense: but others rather, as our version yields it, *by the mounts,* raised by the enemy against the city, or the *engines,* wherewith they batter the walls and shoot into it, Chap. 32.24. so the particle seems also taken in the next member, by, or with the sword, or what is thereby specified.

*{by the sword}* That is, by the hostile force and violence of the enemy; as the word, *sword,* is commonly used, Josh. 10.28, 30. Howbeit, the word may here be as well rendered, *with hammers,* or, *with mattocks;* or; *with axes;* (the word, though singular, being taken collectively) for with this variety of notion is the term sometime expressed. Exod. 20.15, *if thou lift up thy tool,* or, *hammer;* (as the Latin renders it) *upon it, thou hast polluted it:* there it seems indeed to be used for some polishing tool employed about building, but elsewhere for such instruments as are used about battering and beating down of buildings; as 2 Chron. 34.6. where it is said of Josias that he caused the monuments of idolatry to be beaten down, and *broken with mattocks.* So is the word there rendered, and Ezek. 26.9. of Nebuchadnezzar, that he should *set engines of battery against the walls* of Tyre, *and with axes* (the same word with this here, but plural there) *break down her towers:* by the former were they battered in likelihood during the siege, with these latter after the surprisal of the city: Nor do I mislike that exposition of a learned man, who conceives a complexive form of speech in the word of *throwing down,* rendering it, *to be demolished* being exposed to *shot and sword:* though instead of the latter word, I should rather substitute some other instrument of demolition: Of such forms, see on Esay 14.12. & 38.17, 21. So the preposition might retain its ordinary use.

**V. 5.** *{They come to fight with the Chaldeans, but it is to fill them with the dead bodies of men,}* How these words come in here, or how they cohere with the former, is not easy to determine. Some suppose them to be added, as rendering a reason, why the houses came thus to be demolished by the enemy; to wit because the inhabitants stood it out against them, and refused to open to them, that which exasperated the Chaldeans against them. Others, as giving assurance of the surprisal and destruction of the city, notwithstanding all their power and industry that should or could be used by them for the saving thereof: And the most read them as an entire sentence by themselves; which if we admit, I should include this whole verse in a parenthesis, as if it were said, (they come indeed to fight *with the Chaldeans,* but all to no purpose; for I fight myself against them, and have turned my face away from them for their sins) and so the file of the discourse may be carried on from ver. 4. to ver. 6. Yet some hang these words upon the former: and that divers diversely. Some, by repeating of the foregoing particle, *Thus saith the Lord,* concerning the house of Jerusalem, and concerning them also *that come to fight with the Chaldeans.* But this seems to leave the sentence in an abrupt kind of suspense. Others therefore rather by knitting them to the last words of the verse, concerning *the demolishing of the houses* by *those that come* (to wit, from other places) *to fight with the Chaldeans,* (and to defend this city against them) but indeed *to fill them with the carcasses of men:* as God will dispose the issue and event of it: or, concerning the engines and instruments, wherewith they would be demolished, as others, on this wise; *by the shot and sword* (the destroying instruments) *of those that come to fight with the Chaldeans, and to fill them with the carcasses of men:* and these understand the place of those associates and confederates of the Chaldeans that assisted them at the siege of Jerusalem: and this I should readily incline unto (for there is no more than *coming to fight* in the text) if I could find the particle here used in this notion of assistance anywhere joined with the term of *fighting,* or *warring;* but so I never yet met with it, but in the contrary notion of opposing and fighting against, as elsewhere, so Chap. 21.5. & 37.10. Others again, by insertion of a copulative, and supply of the word *houses* render it, *concerning the houses of the King of Judah,* and of those (that is, and concerning the houses of those) *that go* out *to fight with the Chaldeans,* &c. that which yet seems not to go so smoothly away. Nor can I rest satisfied with that of another learned late writer, who renders the words, *The Chaldeans come to fight.* The particle being (says he) oft-times a note of a noun nominative preceding a verb, whether transitive, or intransitive; as Neh. 9.32, 34. 1 Sam. 17.34. 2 Kings 6.5. Chap. 38.16. Ezek. 39.14. & 43.7. I shall leave it to the consideration of others. I incline rather to put the whole verse into a parenthesis, (*Going* they are *to fight with the Chaldeans* (very busy they are about it) *but* (Heb. *and;* as Chap. 12.2.) *to fill them with mens corpses* &c.) that will be the issue of it, though not their aim: to fill them, that is, *the houses,* mentioned ver. 4. as the most: though a learned scholiast understands it of *filling,* that is, *satiating* the bloodthirsty minds and desires of the Chaldeans, that were eagerly set upon slaughter: but the word that peculiarly imports *satiety* is not here: *with the carcasses of men.* Heb. *Adam,* taken collectively; as Chap. 9.22.

*{whom I have slain in mine anger and in my fury}* Or, *whom I will slay,* Heb. *have smitten,* or, *will smite* (as Josh. 11.14.) to wit, by the sword of the Chaldeans: whom not so much the Chaldeans slay, as I slay by them. See Chapter 25.33. & 32, 31, 37, 42.

*{and for all whose wickedness I have hid my face from this city}* In displeasure, Psal. 27.9. Esay 57.17. the ground of all misery and calamity; as his favorable aspect the source and fountain of all true felicity, Psal. 30.5, 7.

**V. 6.** *{Behold I will bring it health and cure,}* This is that which by the Prophet God is reported to have said concerning this city of Jerusalem, and the stately structures of it that are shortly to be demolished and laid level with the ground, ver. 4. I will cause them to be re-edified and raised up again. Heb. *I am making cure, and healing to go up,* or *to come, unto her,* or, *unto it;* to wit, the city. Of the terms here used, and the application thereof unto buildings, see on chap. 30.17.

*{and I will cure them,}* I will restore the people unto their former state again, Esay 57.18. Chap. 3.22.

*{and I will reveal unto them abundance of peace and truth.}* I will show, that is, exhibit, and impart unto them, confer and bestow upon them (as Psal. 85.7. Rom. 8.18, so Psal. 4.6. abundance of firm and sure prosperity. See Esay 39.8. Chap. 14.13. & 32.41.

**V. 7.** *{And I will cause the captivity of Judah, and the captivity of Israel to return:}* As Chapter 24.5. & 30.3. & 32.44.

*{and I will build them as at first.}* Settle them again, and cause them to thrive and prosper, as formerly. See chap. 12.16. & 18.9. ver. 11. Esay 1.26.

**V. 8.** *{And I will cleanse them from all their iniquity, whereby they have sinned against me;}* Heb. *I will purifie them,* an allusion to the ritual purifications and lotions prescribed in the law for the cleansing of polluted persons; before which performed, they might not be admitted into the camp or congregation, Lev. 13.46. & 14.3, 7, 8. Numb. 5.2, 4. & 12.15. & 19.11——20. So Ezek. 36.25. & 37.23.

*{and I will pardon all their iniquities whereby they have sinned, and whereby they have transgressed against me.}* For till these be purged and pardoned, there can be no peace between God and man; nor can there be true joy or sound comfort of ought to man, until his peace be made with God, Psal. 32.1——5. See chap. 31.34. Mic. 7.18.

**V. 9.** *{And it shall be to me a name of joy, a praise and an honour before all the nations of the earth, which shall hear all the good that I do unto them:}* This restitution of God's Church and people shall procure much honor and glory to God among other people abroad, chap. 13.11. Esay 63.14. and, *a name of joy* for such as men are wont to rejoice in.

*{and they shall fear and tremble for all the goodness, and for all the prosperity that I procure unto it.}* Heb. *peace;* as ver. 6. The apprehension of God's favor to his people manifested by his admirable workings for them, shall strike a reverent awe and dread of them into other people round about them. See Exod. 15.14——16. 1 Chron. 13.17. 2 Chron. 20.29. Esth. 8.17.

**V. 10.** *{Thus saith the LORD; Again there shall be heard in this place (which ye say shall be desolate without man and without beast, even in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, that are desolate without man, and without inhabitant, and without beast)}* See on chap. 42.43. and the like descriptions of desolation, chap. 4.35. & 12.4. & 50.3. & 51.62.

*{which ye say shall be desolate}* Heb. *which ye are saying* (that is, of which you say, and whereto you make no other account) *waste,* or, *desolate it is:* the pronoun demonstrative, for the verb substantive, as Hagg. 1.9.
