**V. 11.** *{The voice of joy, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride,}* See chapter 7.34. & 16.9.

*{the voice of them that shall say, praise the LORD of hosts, for he is good, for his mercy endureth for ever.}* The solemn form of praising God, prescribed to the Levites, 1 Chr. 16.41. Psal. 106.1. & 107. & 118.1. & 136.1. Esay 12.4. See this fulfilled after their return from captivity, Ezr. 3.11.

*{and of them that shall bring the sacrifice of praise into the house of the LORD.}* See chap. 17.26.

*{for I will cause to return the captivity of the land, as at the first, saith the LORD.}* Or, *when* (as chap. 11.23. & 13.21.) *I shall have brought back the captivity* (that is, the captives) *of the land,* (as the *captivity of Sion,* Psal. 126.1.) *and* shall have settled them (a complexive form, as ver. 4.) *as at the first,* ver. 7.7. Chapter 30.20. Lam. 5.21.

**V. 12.** *{Thus saith the LORD of hosts, Again in this place, which is desolate without man, and without beast, and in all the cities thereof shall be an habitation of shepherds causing their flocks to lie down.}* In *this place,* the land of Judah which is to be laid waste, and is in part so already, the enemy having overrun most of the country (See Chap. 23.43.) and in the cities thereof; the lands and pastures lying round about them (as Ps. 134.13. See Chap. 34.1.) shall be sheep-cotes, and sheds or cottages for shepherds that shall tend them and feed them quietly without disturbance; so that they shall have their due times both of feeding, and for rest: an argument of times of settled peace in those parts. So Chap. 31.24.

**V. 13.** *{In the cities of the mountains, in the cities of the vale, and in the cities of the South, and in the land of benjamin, and in the places about Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah,}* Or, *in the up-land cities, both in the land of Benjamin,* &c. See on chap. 32.44.

*{shall the flocks passe again under the hands of him, that telleth them, saith the LORD.}* Or, *shall the lesser-cattel* (sheep and goats: for the word includes both, Exod. 12.5. and so verse 12.) pass under the rod to be tithed or told, as they go quietly in and out. See Lev. 26.32. Ezek. 27.32. Joh. 10.3, 10, 12.

**V. 14.** *{Behold the days come, saith the LORD, that I will perform that good thing that I have promised, unto the house of Israel, and to the house of Judah;}* Heb. *Behold the dayes coming* (as Chap. 31.27, 31.) *and* (as Chap. 27.8.) *I will establish* (as 1 Kings 6.12.) *that good word* (as 1 Kings 2.3, 8. & 18.24.) *that I have spoken* (as Josh. 1.3.) *unto* (or, *concerning;* as chap. 27.19.) *the house of Israel,* and *concerning* (as Esay 1.1.) *the house of Judah.* Chap. 30.3, 4. & 31.27.

**V. 15.** *{In those days, and at that time, will I cause the branch of righteousness to grow up unto David; and he shall execute judgment in the land:}* See the same promise concerning the Messias, Chap. 23.5. only what was said, *I will raise,* or, *settle,* there; is said here, *I will make to bud,* or, *sprout;* as Psal. 132.17. Ezek. 29.21. the rather, because he speaks as a plant, word for word, *I will make a sprout to sprout out:* and, *a sprout of righteousnesse,* here; as, *a righteous sprout,* there.

**V. 16.** *{In those days shall Judah be saved,}* So chap. 23.6. *In his dayes shall Judah be saved.*

*{and Jerusalem shall dwell safely}* Or, *shall be inhabited* (for the word is sometime used in a passive notion. See Esay 13.20. chap. 17.6.) *in safety.* See chap. 23.6. See also chap. 30.18. & 46.27.

*{and this is the name wherewith she shall be called, The LORD is our Righteousness.}* Heb. *and this it is that he shall call her,* or, *call to her,* (that is, says the Rabbine, the name by which the Messias shall call her: but rather, *wherewith she shall be called;* as Esay 63.4. for the verb is indefinite) *Jehovah Tsidkenu.* That which was said to be the name of Christ the Messias, chap. 23.6. is here said to be the name of Jerusalem, the city of the Messias, the Church of Christ; given to him as the party, who imparts righteousness to her 1 Cor. 1.30. 2 Cor. 5.21. to her, that by bearing that name she may profess to have her whole righteousness, not from herself, but from him, Esay 45.24, 25. Phil. 3.9. that which, says the Rabbine here, the inhabitants of Jerusalem should have continually in their mouths, and shall no doubt when they come unto Christ, 2 Cor. 3.16. Some interpreters of prime note render the text, *and he that shall call her,* shall be *Jehovah our Righteousnesse;* but the words seem clearly to import the imposition of some name: which the learned scholiast observing, and yet loath to have this name given unto any other beside Christ, thus exhibits the Prophet's words, *and this,* is the name, *wherewith* every one *shall call him, Jehovah our Righteousnesse:* but this is a manifest corrupting of the text, which expressly holds out, not *him,* but *her.* See more hereof on chap. 23.6.

*{The LORD is our Righteousness}* *Jehovah Tsidkenu:* as *Jehovah Shammah, The Lord is there;* the name of the same city, Ezek. 48.35.

**V. 17.** *{For thus saith the LORD; David shall never want a man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel:}* A further confirmation, not of the restitution of the Church only, but of the continuation of it in a settled condition of constant government under Christ's royal regiment, and the ministry of his sacred ordinances, exercised and executed by persons specially designed thereunto. The Hebrew, *shall not be cut off unto David a man* (that is, some *man of David,* as, *to David a Psalm,* for. *a Psalm of David,* Psal. 14.1. some one of his seed) *sitting upon the throne of the house of Israel;* as chap. 35.19. See 2 Chron. 6.16. fulfilled principally in Christ, one of David's seed, unto whom God promises to give *the throne of his father David to reign over the house of Jacob for ever,* Luke 1.32, 33.

**V. 18.** *{Neither shall the Priests, the Levites, want a man before me, to offer burnt offerings, and to kindle meat offerings, and to do sacrifice continually.}* Heb. *Neither to,* or, *of the Priests the Levites there shall not be a man cut off from before me;* that is, from attendance upon me: as Deut. 10.8. A promise of the continuance of an evangelical ministry in the Church of God to the world's end, Mat. 28.20. Eph. 4.11——13. the ministers and offices of themselves described by those that then were in place, as Esay 66.21. and their employments and services by those that then were in use; as Esay 56.7. Mal. 1.11. Rom. 15.16.

*{to offer burnt offerings,}* Heb. *making an ascension,* or, *offering up,* to ascend; to wit; upon the altar. See Esay 56.7.

*{to kindle meat offerings,}* Heb. *burning* (as 2 Chron. 13.11.) *an oblation;* for of such oblations was a memorial made also by fire upon the altar, Lev. 2.2. & 6.15. and of them, see on Esay 1.13. & 56.7. *kindling* does not here so well; because the fire upon the altar was kindled and maintained principally for the burnt-sacrifices consisting of the bodies of beasts, but being so kindled and kept in for them, was used also for the meat and drink-offerings; nor does the word itself so signify.

*{to sacrifice continually.}* Heb. *doing;* or, *dressing,* (as Gen. 18.8. Exod. 10.25.) *sacrifice all dayes;* as chap. 32.29. but here alluding to the daily sacrifice, Numb. 28.3.

**V. 19.** *{And the word of the LORD came unto Jeremiah, saying,}* *Moreover,* or, *Furthermore,* as verse 1. chap. 1.11.

**V. 20.** *{Thus saith the LORD, If ye can break my covenant of the day, and my covenant of the night, and that there shall not be day and night in their season:}* Or, *if ye can annull* (Heb. *shall make void,* as Judg. 2.1. but herein a potential notion, as Esay 14.27.) *my constitution,* (for so the word *covenant,* here imports, Gen. 8.22.) *concerning the day; and concerning the night, so as that* (as Chap. 29.6.) *there should not be day and night* in their due, or, set time. It it be possible for any created power to break off the intercourse of night and day. See the like expressions, Esay 54.9. chap. 31.35, 36. verse 25.

**V. 21.** *{Then may also my covenant be broken with David my servant; that he should not have a son to reign upon his Throne, and with the Levites the Priests my ministers.}* Heb. *my covenant,* my promise or engagement (*also shall be made void* (but potentially taken, as verse 20.) *with David* (2 Sam. 7.16. Psal. 132.11.) *my servant* (the style commonly in way of eminency given him, Psal. 78.70. & 89.20. & 132.10.) *from being to him* (as 1 Sam. 15.2. Hos. 4.6.) *a son reigning upon his Throne,* &c. as the like, ver. 18. As soon shall the one fail, as either of the other, the princely, or priestly succession, the same with that before, verse 17, 18.

**V. 22.** *{As the host of heaven cannot be numbered: neither the sand of the sea measured: so will I multiply the seed of David my servant, and the Levites that minister unto me.}* A promise not of the continuation only of a state and Church, but of a large increase of issue in the kingdom of Christ (the honor of a King consisting in the multitude of his people, Prov. 14.18.) and a correspondent number of ministers and officers for the ordering and managing of them. See the like promises to Abraham, Gen. 13.15. & 15.5. & 22.17. Heb. *Which* (for, *Like as;* as Exod. 34.18. Lev. 7.26. 2 Sam. 14.19. chap. 48.8. But found here also above those places, that the Jewish critics restrain it to) *the host of heaven,* (*the stars,* Gen. 22.) *shall not be numbred,* (for *cannot;* as Gen. 16.10. & 32.12.) *and the sand of the sea shall not be measured;* (for *cannot;* as Hos. 1.10.) See the like potential notions, verse 20, 21. See of the like promise, Esay 53.8, 10. and performance: Rev. 7.9.

**V. 23.** *{Moreover, the word of the LORD came unto Jeremiah, saying,}* Or, *Again.* Heb. *And.* as chap. 24.4.

**V. 24.** *{Considerest thou not what this people have spoken?}* Heb. *Seest thou not* (as Psal. 119.159. chap. 2.31.) *what this people* (either the unfaithful party among God's own people, wholly despairing of any possibility of being ever raised up and restored again, Esay 40.27. & 49.14. Ezek. 33.10. & 37.11. or, the Chaldeans and other enemies of God's people, chap. 50.7.) *have spoken,* or, *do speak;* what they have commonly in their mouths.

*{The two families}* Or, as some render it, *As for the two families;* put absolutely: as Psal. 104.17. *the two families;* to wit, of David and Aaron, as some, the princely, and the priestly, verse 17, 18, 22. or, of *Judah and Benjamin,* as others, chap. 32.44. or, of *Judah,* and *Israel,* as the most, verse 14.

*{which the LORD hath chosen,}* Or, *did choose,* or, *had chosen,* as Psal. 105.26.

*{he hath even cast them off,}* Heb. *and;* as chap. 23.33, 34. where the copulative has an emphasis in it; *he hath utterly cast them off:* and does not at all now regard them, or mind them any more. So rather, than, as some, *he doth now reject them.* See chap. 30.17.

*{Thus have they despised my people, that they should be no more a nation before them.}* Or, *Thus despise they my people.* See Esay 54.6. Heb. *and;* as chap. 25.14. they set light by them, as never like to come to be a nation again, in their account. Heb. *from being any more a nation before them;* as chap. 48.2.

**V. 25.** *{Thus saith the LORD,}* God's firm resolution opposed to this their vain imagination.

*{If my covenant be not with day and night, and if I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth:}* Or, as some, *If my covenant abide not day and night,* (that is, constantly and perpetually; as 1 Chr. 9.33. Psalm 19.2. chap. 9.1.) or, (as others) concerning *day and night,* (the constant intercourse of either, verse 20.) *and the Ordinances concerning heaven and earth* (for the course of the one to do service to the other, chap. 31.35, 36. (which *I have settled* be *not;* that is, do not, continue or abide, Psalm 119.91. See c. 17.8. But this syntax the last clause will hardly admit: or, as others rather therefore, *If I have not* settled, or *If I shall not dispose* (so that it cannot, or shall not be altered, vers. 20. (my constitution of day and night, Genesis 8.22.) *and if I have not settled,* or *shall not dispose, the Ordinances of heaven and earth* in a certain and constant course; for the office of the one, Genesis 1.14, 16. and the safety and benefit of the other, Genesis 1.9. chapter 5.22, 24. & 31.35. or more particularly, those courses that I have set for such distinction of times to be continued by the motion of the celestial bodies for the use and benefit of the creatures below upon earth, Psalm 74.16, 17. and 104.19, 23. the supply only is in the former branch, from the latter; the like whereunto; See Esay 30.17.

**V. 26.** *{Then will I cast away the seed of Jacob, and David my Servant; so that I will not take any of his seed to be Rulers over the seed of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob:}* Heb. *I will also refuse the seed of Jacob* (to own them at all for my people; or to keep them in being, as a nation, chapter 31.35, 36. verse 24.) *and David my servant* (verse 21, 22.) *from taking of his seed* (as 1 Kings 22.3. 2 Kings 5.20.) *rulers* (verse 21.) *over the seed of Abraham; Isaac and Jacob;* unto whom the promises were specially made for continuance of their seed, Psalm 105.9, 10. this for *rulers,* fulfilled partly in Zerubbabel, and his successors, Ezra 2.1. Zach. 2.4. but principally in Christ, Luke 1.33. verse 15. and the seed of these here mentioned are the body of the faithful, whom he rules by his Word, and Spirit, Psalm 105.1, 6. Romans 9.6——8. Gal. 3.16, 17. & 6.16.

*{for I will cause their captivity to return; and will have mercy on them.}* Or, as some, *when I shall bring back their captivity;* as Chapter 31.34. but that though not amiss there, does not so well here: rather, *but* (here, as Chapter 14.12.) *I will bring back their captivity:* and thereby make it to appear that I have not utterly rejected them, as their enemies imagine. See Esay 14.1. Chapter 32.4. Verse 11.

## CHAPTER 34

**Verse 1.** *{The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD,}* This Chapter contains two several prophecies at two several times delivered. The former is related from verse 1——7. together with the time when it was delivered, both prefixed and subjoined. The inscription here the same with Chapter 18.1.

*{(when Nebuchadnezzar King of Babylon, and all his Army, and all the Kingdoms of the earth of his Dominion, and all the people fought against Jerusalem, and against all the Cities thereof) saying,}* In the time of the siege, whereof 2 Kings 25.1. Chapter 52.1.

*{when}* Heb. *and* c. 14.15. & 163.

*{Nebuchadnezzar}* Elsewhere in this prophecy called *Nebuchadretsar,* 21.2. & 25.1, 9.

*{of his Dominion}* Heb. *of the Dominion of his hand:* See Psalm 89.25.

*{all the Cities thereof}* Either of Judah, verse 7. or of Jerusalem, Chapter 19.15. that being the mother-city, Chapter 15.8. and the rest as daughters to her, Lamentations 3.51. so are inferior towns and cities commonly styled, Joshua 15.32, 36, 41, 43, &c.

**V. 2.** *{Thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel}* As Chapter 30.2.

*{Go, and speak unto Zedekiah King of Judah, and tell him; Thus saith the LORD,}* This prophecy seems to have been delivered to Jeremy while he was yet at liberty; and the message sent from God to Zedekiah by him to have occasioned his restraint. See Chap. 32.2, 3. The message consists partly of an heavy denunciation of the surprisal of the city, and the King together with it, and the deportation of him to Babylon, verse, 2, 3. partly, of some mitigation of this sad sentence, assuring him from God, that he yet should die a natural death, and have an honorable sepulture, verse 4, 5.

*{Go}* Heb. *Going;* as chap. 22. & 3.12.

*{Behold, I will give this City into the hand of the King of Babylon; and he shall burn it with fire}* See Chapter 32.3. and 21.10. Verse 32.

**V. 3.** *{And thou shalt not escape out of his hand, but shalt surely be taken,}* Heb. *shalt taking be taken;* as Chapter 26.15. and 38.4.

*{and thine eyes shall behold the eyes of the king of Babylon, and he shall speak with thee mouth to mouth,}* So c. 32.4.

*{and thou shalt go to Babylon,}* c. 32.5.

**V. 4.** *{Yet hear the word of the LORD, O Zedekiah king of Judah; Thus saith the LORD concerning thee, Thou shalt not die by the sword:}* You shall not die a violent, but a natural death, by God's ordinary visitation, chap. 32.5.

**V. 5.** *{But thou shalt die in peace;}* Not in war or fight.

*{and with the burnings of thy fathers the former kings, which were before thee, so shall they burn them for thee:}* The King of Babylon shall afford him that, which he had denied unto Jehoiakim, chap. 22.19. & 36.30. he shall give his people leave to bury him in an honorable manner, and with their solemnities the burning of sweet odors amongst the rest, at his exequies, as they were wont to use at the funerals of their kings in their own country, such of them at least, as had lived beloved, and died desired. See 2 Chr. 16.14. & 21.19.

*{and they will lament thee, saying, Ah LORD,}* Or, *they shall lament thee;* that it may run in the same tenor with the former. There shall solemn lamentation be made for you, as for your father Josias 2 Chronicles, 35.24, 25. denied to Jehoiakim his brother, Chapter 22.18.

*{for I have pronounced the Word, saith the LORD}* Heb. *I have spoken the word;* or *spoken it.* (*word,* for *thing;* as c. 32.27.) both the one and the other, as v. 3, 4.

**V. 6.** *{Then Jeremiah spake all these words unto Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem:}* Then, or so, as chap. 13.2, 5. The Prophet forbore not to go to the King and deliver God's message to him in his royal city, though the doing of it was like to cost him dear. See chap. 32.3.

**V. 7.** *{When the king of Babylons army fought against Jerusalem, and against all the cities of Judah that were left}* Heb. *And;* and as verse 1. See there.

*{against Lachish, and against Azekah}* Of these cities, see Joshua 10.10, 31. and of the former also, Esay 36.2. & 37.8.

*{for these defenced cities remained in the Cities of Judah:}* Heb. *Cities of defence,* or *fortification:* as c. 4.5. & 8.14. those two only (besides Jerusalem) yet hold out against the Chaldean forces, *of the Cities of Judah,* that were of any considerable strength: as *mountain in Gilboa,* for *mountains of Gilbon,* 2 Samuel 1.21. or *among the Cities of Judah:* as *in the thousands,* for *among the thousands,* Mic. 5.2.

**V. 8.** *{This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD}* Heb. *The word that was to Jeremiah from the Lord;* as verse 1. and as that there, so this here, seems to be the inscription or title of a new prophecy, somewhat later than the former, delivered, as appears, upon a more special occasion, related from verse 8——11. for from thence the word or message here mentioned, itself begins, continued unto the end of the Chapter: the former was delivered when the Chaldean forces were set down before the city, and eager in the siege of it, and the city by reason thereof in distress, v. 1, 7. this latter when there were some relaxation of their former straits; the Chaldeans being for some space of time risen from before the city, upon the approach of some Egyptian aids, verse 21. chap. 37.5.

*{after that the king Zedekiah had made a Covenant with all the people to proclaim liberty unto them}* Heb. *had cut a Covenant:* of which form of speech, see on Esay 28.15. and hereafter, verse 18. for when the enemy pressed hard upon them, and they seemed to be in some distress, they made some show of remorse and repentance for their sinful courses, and renewed their covenants with God, and made some kind of reformation: as the like, Judges 10.15, 16. Psalm 78.34, 35. Hosea, 6.1. and among other enormities, which God's Prophets it seems had admonished them of, verse 10. they had agreed to break off that injurious course, whereby many of them kept their brethren still in servitude, after the expiration of that term of years, which was for their service by God's appointment prefixed; (see verse 14.) and liberty was thereupon proclaimed *unto them,* that is, in behalf of all those that were so wrongfully detained.

**V. 9.** *{That every man should let his manservant, and every man his maidservant, being an Hebrew, or an Hebrewess, go free,}* Having served them the time limited by the law, Exods 21.2. Heb. *to dismisse free* (as Deut. 15.18. & ver. 11.) *a man,* for *every one;* as chap. 32.19.

*{that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his Brother.}* Keep them in service. See the phrase, chapter 27.7. and 30.8.

**V. 10.** *{Now when all the Princes, and all the people, which had entered into the Covenant, had heard that every one should let his manservant, and every one his maidservant, go free, that none should serve themselves of them any more, then they obeyed, and let them go.}* Being by God's Prophets informed of their duty herein, they condescended thereunto; as verse 9. Heb. *And they heard* &c.——*and they heard* (for, *when they heard——* as c. 26.10. *then they obeyed,* as c. 35.8.) *and dismissed;* a defect of the pronoun, as chap. 31.5.

**V. 11.** *{But afterwards they turned, and caused the servants, and the handmaids, whom they had let go free, to return, and brought them into subjection for servants, and for handmaids.}* Heb. *And* (as Chapter 12.2.) *after so* (as Chapter 16.16.) After they had thus done in the time of their straits; when the straitness of the siege was for sometime intermitted, the Chaldeans, rising in likelihood to meet the Egyptian army, that came to raise the siege, and to relieve the city, supposing themselves now to be safe enough, and imagining that the Chaldeans would not return to the siege again, they repented them of what they had formerly well done; as Pharaoh did of dismissing the Israelites, Exod. 14.5. and brought them back into bondage again, v. 16. See the term here used, Neh. 5.5. 2 Chronicles 28.10.

**V. 12.** *{Therefore the Word of the LORD came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,}* Or, *Then;* as chap. 43.8. that word whereof before verse 8. which now here follows: and it contains, 1 A relation of a Law enacted by God, concerning the dismission of their servants after a certain term of years, verse 13, 14. 2 A narration of the violation of this Law, together with a reformation of the offense therein committed, verse 14, 15. 3 A revolt from this their temporary reformation, verse 16. and 4 A denunciation of dreadful judgments to be inflicted upon them for this their relapse and breach of covenant with God, verse 17–22.

**V. 13.** *{Thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel,}* As v. 2.

*{I made a covenant with your fathers in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondmen, saying;}* Heb. *I cut a covenant* (as verse 8.) *with your fathers* (and you in them, Deuteronomy 5.2,3. & 29.10–15.) *in the day* (about the time; as Chap. 7.22.) *of my bringing them forth out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of Servants:* as Exod. 20.2. where you were no better than as bondmen and servants, Exodus 1.11–14. and he seems the rather to mention this their service and bondage here, thereby to imply the equity of the Law here subjoined, that since God has freed them from the condition of bondmen, it was not meet for them to make bondmen of their brethren, Deuteronomy 15.15. nor to make slaves of those, whom God had set free, Lev. 25.39,42.

**V. 14.** *{At the end of seven years let ye go every man his brother an Hebrew, which hath been sold unto thee;}* Or: *that hath sold himself unto thee,* Lev. 25.29. Deut. 15.12. for these passives have oft-times a reciprocal notion; as chap. 23.24.

*{At the end of seven years}* That is, six years being fully complete, (as it is in the next words) at the beginning of the seventh, Exod. 21.2. Deut. 15.12. and the Jewish Doctors well observe, that the word here used, includes either term, or utmost limit of ought, whether that whence it begins, as that wherewith it is closed up, and concluded, 2 Kings 19.23. & 50.26.

*{let ye go}* Heb. *ye shall dismiss.* See on v. 14. and *a man for every one;* as there.

*{and when he hath served thee six years thou shalt let him go free from thee:}* Heb. *and he hath served thee, — and thou shalt dismiss him,* for *when he hath served thee, thou shalt dismiss him:* as before, v. 10.

*{but your fathers hearkened not unto me, neither inclined their ear.}* So c. 7.24.

**V. 15.** *{And you were now turned,}* Heb. *Ye had turned to day:* as *Ye have rebelled to day.* Josh. 22.18.

*{and hath done right in my sight}* Or *that which is right in my sight;* which I approve of: as Deut. 13.18. & 21.9.

*{in proclaiming liberty every one to his neighbour,}* Or *one to another;* as Gen. 11.3. See v. 8.

*{and ye had made a Covenant before me}* Heb. *cut a covenant to my face.* You had by a solemn Covenant in my presence (Psal. 42.2.) engaged yourselves to persist in the observation of what you had done. See v. 8.

*{in the house which is called by my Name}* Heb. *whereupon my Name is called:* in the Temple that bears my Name, chap. 7.10. and 32.34.

**V. 16.** *{But ye turned}* Or *But ye have turned back;* or *are revolted;* as c. 8.5. Heb. *And.* as v. 11.

*{and polluted my name}* Or *have polluted my name;* have grievously wronged and abused me, by breach of your covenant so solemnly plighted in my presence. So Lev. 19.12. Exod. 20.39. and 22.26. Mal. 1.7,12.

*{and caused every man his servant, and every man his hand-maid, whom he had set at liberty at their pleasure to return; and brought them into subjection, to be unto you, for servants, and for handmaids.}* Or *and have caused each one his servant, and his hand-maid, whom ye had let go free* (as v. 10.) *according to their desire,* (Deut. 21.14.) to return (unto service) *and have brought them into subjection to become your servants and hand-maids again.* See v. 11.

**V. 17.** *{Therefore thus saith the LORD, ye have not hearkened unto me in proclaiming liberty every one to his brother, and every man to his neighbour:}* That is, *one to another;* as ch. 23.35. You have not done it, because you have not persisted in it, but have wickedly undone again, what you had done: whereby it appears, that you did it not in sincerity. So Psal. 78.8,34–37. Hos. 6.1,4. So reconcile, 1 Samuel 28.6. with 1 Chron. 10.14. and 2 Kings 17. verse 33. with verse 34.

*{behold, I proclaim a liberty for you to the sword, and to the pestilence, and to the famine,}* I will give the sword, famine and pestilence, (Chapter 15.2.) free liberty to seize upon you, to subdue you, to over-master you; thus is God wont to execute judgment by a kind of retaliation. See Esay, 66.5. Chapter, 14.16.

*{and I will make you to be removed into all the Kingdoms of the Earth.}* Heb. *I will give you for a removal unto all the Kingdoms of the Earth,* Deuteronomy 28.64. Ch. 15.1. and 24.9. and 29.18.

**V. 18.** *{And I will give the men that have transgressed my Covenant, which have not performed the words of my Covenant, which they had made before me, when they cut the Calf in twain, and passed between the parts thereof,}* Heb. *the Covenant which they cut before me;* as vers. 8,15. So that by these and the like religious rites of divine institution, God and man do interchangeably seal either to other; and man covenants with God, as well as God with man, Exodus 24.8. Psalm 50.5. John 3.33. Rom. 4.11. And we see the ground of that phrase of *cutting out a Covenant;* alluding to that solemn rite of dividing the body of some slain beast for sacrifice, and passing through the sides of it lying apart, as confessing themselves worthy, and in way of execration (whence *the oath and the curse,* Neh. 10.29.) thereunto, devoting themselves to be so cut in twain, (Matt. 24.51.) and destroyed, as that creature was, if they should violate the Covenant that then they made. See somewhat the like ceremony in Gods covenanting with Abraham, Gen. 15.10,17. and the like also among the Heathen, in making of solemn leagues and agreements. See in Homers *Iliads,* l. 3. Virgils *Eneides* l. 8. Tully of *invention,* l. 2. Livy, *his History,* l. 1. Some read the words, *I will make the men that have transgressed my Covenant* (which they made one with another, but before me, and concerning a branch of my Covenant with them, verse 8.13,15.) — *as the calf* (the note of similitude inserted, as Chapter 26.18.) *which they cut in twain;* and a learned late Interpreter thus digests them, *I will give the men that transgressed my Covenant, and that have not performed the words, or contents,* (as Est. 9.31.) *of the Covenant, and of the Calf which they cut in two;* and therewith obliged the same: and the tenor of the Context inclines much this way.

**V. 19.** *{The Princes of Judah, and the Princes of Jerusalem, the Eunuchs, and the Priests, and all the people of the land, that passed between the parts of the Calf,}* All sorts reckoned up, that none may hope to escape, having dealt all alike perfidiously in their Covenant.

**V. 20.** *{I will even give them into the hands of their enemies, and into the hand of them that seek their Life}* So Chapter 21.7. and 22.25.

*{and their dead bodies shall be for meat unto the Fowles of the Heaven, and unto the Beasts of the Earth.}* Chapter 7.33. and 16.4.

**V. 21.** *{And Zedekiah King of Judah and his Princes will I give into the hand of their enemies, and into the hand of them that seek their life, and into the hand of the King of Babylons Army, which are gone up from you.}* Or, *departed from you.* as Exodus 12.38. Chapter 37.5. having upon the coming of some Egyptian aids raised their siege for a short time, Chapter 37.5.11. but not long after returned again, as the Prophet also foretold, that they should, Chap. 37.8. vers. 22. and left not the City until they surprised it.

**V. 22.** *{Behold, I will command, saith the LORD, and cause them to return to this city, and they shall fight against it and take it, and burn it with fire.}* I will by a secret and hidden, but efficacious providence and disposal, cause them to come back and do all this; as if I had given them an express charge and command so to do. See 2 Sam. 16.10. 2 Kings 24.2. 2 Chron. 36.17. Chap. 49.14. & 50.21. See the like threatened Chap. 21.10. & 32.28,29. executed, 2 Kings 25.4,9. Chap. 52.7,13.

*{and I will make the Cities of Judah a desolation without inhabitant.}* See Chapter 26.15.

## CHAPTER 35

**Verse 1.** *{The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, in the days of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah King of Judah, saying;}* See the like Inscriptions, Chap. 11. and 18. and 21. This Chapter contains a Narration of the Rechabites precise abstinence from wine, in obedience to the charge given them by their fore-father Rechab, ver. 1–12. here related to control and aggravate the disobedience of Gods people to his commands, verse 12–15. together with a denunciation of evil to the one, v. 16,17. and a promise of blessing to the other, v. 18,19.

**V.** *{Go unto the house of the Rechabites;}* Those of the family of Rechab, which were by original Kenites, descended from Jethro, or Hobab, Moses his father in Law, Judges 1.16. and 4.11. they were called Rechabites from one Rechab, a man, it seems, of special note among them in his times, 1 Chr. 2.55. 2 Kings 10.15. being foreigners they had no possession among Gods people, but lived upon their employments, v. 7.

*{and speak unto them, and bring them into the house of the LORD, into one of the chambers, and give them wine to drink,}* Under the name *the Lords house,* are comprehended all the buildings that were about the Temple, among which were *chambers,* wherein the Priests lodged, and wherein were bestowed the holy vestments, the oblations, and other the like necessaries, 1 Chron. 28.11,12. 1 King 6.5,6,10. 2 Chr. 3.11. Ezek. 4.17,44,46. & 41.6. & 42.13. hither would God have them brought, rather than unto some more obscure and private place, that the more notice might be taken of it.

*{Go}* Heb. *Going Go.* See chap. 2.2. & 34.2.

*{give them wine to drink,}* Heb. *thou shalt make,* or *do thou make them drink wine;* that is, offer them wine, tender it to them; and that is all he did, v. 5.

**V. 3.** *{Then I took Jaazaniah the son of Jeremiah, the son of Habaziniah, and his brethren, and all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites;}* Or, *So I took;* as Chapter 13.2,5. Heb. *And.*

**V. 4.** *{And I brought them into the House of the LORD, into the chamber of the sons of Hanan, the son of Igdaliah a man of God,}* This Hanan some suppose to be that Hanani mentioned, 2 Chron. 16.7. but that is uncertain, and not very probable; for, whether the title of *a man of God* (given usually to Prophets and Teachers of Gods people, Deut. 33.1. Psalm 90.1. 1 Tim. 6.11.) belong here unto Hanan, or unto Igdaliah, is somewhat doubtful. Whoever he was, these his sons it seems were of the course of those that waited and served that week. See 1 Chr. 24.5,6. & 25.1,2, &c. 2 Chron. 23.4,8.

*{which was by the chamber of the Princes}* That is, say some, where the rich gifts were disposed; or their treasure for safety kept, 2 Kings 18.15. or, rather where they used to meet, to consult together of public affairs. See chap. 26.10,17. though others understand it of the chief of the Priests of the course that then ministered, or those that were next under the high Priest: See 2 Chron. 23.4. c. 20.1.

*{which was above the chamber of Maaseiah the son of Shallum}* For the chambers were built with divers Stories one over another, Ezek. 41.5,6. See on Esay 6.1.

*{the keeper of the door}* Heb. *threshold;* as Ezekiel 43.8. and the title of *Keepers of,* or *attendants at the threshold,* is commonly given to *porters,* or *door-keepers,* 1 Chronicles 9.19. 2 Chronicles 34.9. Howbeit, the Jewish Commenters here render it, *the Keeper of the Vessel:* in likelihood, because the word is sometime used for *Vessels, cups, basins,* or *bowls,* Exodus 12.22. 2 Kings 12.14. See 1 Chron. 9.28,29. and the Chaldee both here, and 2 Kings 12.10. & 22.4 *the Treasurer,* as being one of these seven Chamberlains, or Treasurers, that kept the keys of the sacred Treasure; the word being used as for *a threshold,* or *transom,* first then for *a door,* and after for *a chamber;* and thence the Kings *Chamberlains* so termed, Esther 2.21. & 6.2. See on Esay 6.4.

**V. 5.** *{And I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites pots full of wine and cups, and said unto them, Drink ye wine}* He invites them to drink it, to try what they would do: Yet says not to them, *Thus saith the Lord, Drink wine:* for then they ought not to have refused it; but the end of the tender was by their refusal out of obedience to their ancestors charge, to convince and condemn the Jewish people for their disobedience to Gods commands, v. 16.

*{pots full of wine, and cups}* Pots containing some large quantity of wine; for it has affinity with a term that signifies *an hill,* or *hillock:* and cups to pour it out into, and so drink it: but because the former word is used for a drinking *cup* as well as the latter, Gen. 44.2 I suppose there is a trajection in the words, and it is all one, as if he had said, *bowls and cups full of wine.* See the like hereunto before, c. 32.9,11.

**V. 6.** *{But they said, we will drink no wine:}* Heb. *And* (as Chapter 30.9.) *they said, we will not drink wine,* or *we may not;* as, *that shall be done,* for *that ought not to be done,* Genesis 20.9.

*{for Jonadab the son of Rechab our father commanded us, saying.}* *Our father,* that is our Ancestor, or progenitor; for this Jonadab lived in Jehu's time, 2 Kings 10.15. between two and three hundred years before Jeremies days: Nor is that learned mans Argument convincing with me, who would hence evince, that this Jonadab should be one that lived in or about Jeremies time, because they call him their *father,* and say, *Our father commanded us: your father Abraham,* says our Savior to the Jews, John 8.56. and, *what did Moses command you?* to those that then lived, Mark 10.3. and how the one *Pashur,* is called *the son of Immer,* and the other of *Melchiah,* see on Chapter 20.1. and 21.1.

*{Ye shall drink no wine, neither ye nor your sons for ever;}* Why Jonadab enjoined his issue this strict course of life, is questionable. Some suppose, to keep them in that course, that they had followed, while they lived in the land of Midian, where they gave themselves to a shepherds life, living in tents, and tending their flocks, not planting of vines, nor drinking wine, which the Country yielded not; but contenting themselves with such sustenance as their flocks afforded, Exod. 2.16. & 3.1 Judges 4.17,19. Others, because having no inheritance in the land, being but strangers therein, they were to live upon their employments, and should not therefore look to live in so free and plentiful a manner, as those that had lands and revenues yearly coming in. Others, that he would thereby enure them to hardship, as by a prophetical spirit foreseeing those calamities, that should in process of time befall those among whom they lived. But these things being but mere conjectures, it is not safe certainly hereof to define ought.

*{neither ye, nor your sons}* Heb. *ye, and your sonnes;* as *ye and your fathers,* chapter 16.13. and, *the King and his servants,* chapter 36.24.

**V. 7.** *{Neither shall ye build house, nor sow seed, nor plant vineyard, nor have any; but all your days, ye shall dwell in tents;}* The words of the charge may well all be rendered in the imperative, for which the future is frequently used, *Drink not wine, nor build house,* &c. *but dwell in Tents all your days;* all your life long; as Deut. 11.1. & 12.1.

*{that ye may live many days in the land where ye be strangers}* Heb. *on the face of the land* (as Gen. 6.1.) *which ye are sojourning there,* or *wherein ye sojourn:* as 2 Samuel 4.3. for they were by original Kenites, or Midianites, not of the line or lineage of Israel. This promise of lengthening their days subjoined, some refer to that blessing annexed by God to the precept of obedience to parents, Exod. 20.12. Ephes. 6.2. Others rather suppose herein to be intended that by retaining such a course of life they were like to live the longer in a strange country peaceably and quietly, free from envy and grudge of the natives of the land, who are not wont so well to brook the growth and greatness of strangers among them, but are thence moved many times to seek the rooting of them out, Exod. 1.9,10. But whatsoever the ground of the injunction was, or whatsoever the end aimed at in it, they had been and still were very careful to observe it.

**V. 8.** *{Thus have we obeyed the voice of Jonadab the son of Rechab our father,}* Heb. *And* (which would rather be here retained) *hearkened to the voice;* as c. 7.23.

*{in all that he charged us, to drink no wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons, and our daughters:}* Or *in not drinking wine:* So this is the particle with the Verb infinitive frequently used: as Gen. 3.22. c. 28.6. and 19.9. and 36.8.

**V. 9.** *{Nor to build houses for us to dwell in}* Or *And in not building:* as before v. 8.

*{neither have we vineyard, nor field, nor seed:}* We neither till nor plant.

**V. 10.** *{But we have dwelt in Tents}* As he willed us, verse 7. ordinarily, save when necessity enforces us to do otherwise verse 11.

*{and have obeyed, and done according to all that Jonadab, our father commanded us}* Heb *we have heard;* as c. 34.10. Exodus 20.19. ver. 8. And this seems to have been inviolably observed by them from the time of Jehu, unto the reign of Jehojakim, for about three hundred years. See on v. 6.

**V. 11.** *{But it came to passe}* Heb. *And it was:* As chapter 41.11,13.

*{when Nebuchadrezzar came up into the land}* In a warlike hostile manner, see on Esay 7.1.

*{that we said}* Heb. *And we said;* *and* for *that:* As chapter, 31.14.

*{come and let us go to Jerusalem for fear of the Army of the Chaldeans,}* Heb. *from the face of;* as Esay 21.15. & 31.8. and so in the next clause.

*{and for fear of the Army of the Syrians,}* Heb. *Aramites;* that assisted the Chaldeans, and served under them, in their expedition against Judea, 2 Kings 24.2.

*{so we dwell at Jerusalem}* Or *abide;* as chapter 40.5. verse 15. It seems that they held not themselves so strictly tied to these observances, but that in case of necessity they did and might dispense with them.

**V. 12.** *{Then came the Word of the LORD unto Jeremiah saying}* Heb. *And the word was to him;* as c. 32.26.

**V. 13.** *{Thus saith the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel,}* as chapter 17.4.

*{Go and tell the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem,}* Heb. *Going* (as v. 2.) *and thou shalt say* (or *say thou,* as chap. 16.11.) *to the man of Judah,* (as chap. 3.3.) and the inhabitants of *Jerusalem;* as Esay 5.5.

*{will ye not receive instruction to hearken to my word? says the LORD.}* Or *in hearkning to my words:* as v. 8,9. See Chap. 2.30. & 5.3. & 7.28.

**V. 14.** *{The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab, that he commanded his sons, not to drink wine are performed;}* Or *the things* (as Deuteronomy 30.10.) *that he enjoined his sons, are* each of them (for the Verb is singular, the Noun plural, as Proverbs 14.1. Joel 1.20.) *inviolably kept,* Heb. *are established:* as chapter 33.14.

*{for unto this day they drink none.}* For so many descents, verse 8.

*{but obey their Fathers commandment}* Heb. *hear:* As verse 10.

*{notwithstanding I have spoken unto you}* Or *yet.* Heb. *and;* as chap. 27.15.

*{rising early and speaking}* I have from time to time sedulously and assiduously by my ministers and messengers minded you of my charge, and called upon you for obedience thereunto, chap. 7.13. & 11.7.

*{but ye hearkened not unto me.}* Or *but* Heb. *and* as v. 11. *ye have not hearkned to me;* as c. 26.5,7. v. 15.

**V. 15.** *{I have sent unto you all my servants the Prophets, rising early, and sending them,}* Heb. *And I have sent;* as Chapter 1.2. or *I have even sent;* as Chapter 30.7. or, *For I have sent;* as Esay 65.5. See Chapter 7.25. & 25.4. & 26.5. & 29.19. & 44.4. 2 Chron. 36.15.

*{saying, Return ye now every man from his evil way, and amend your doings,}* See c. 18.11. & 25.5.

*{and go not after other gods to serve them,}* c. 25.6.

*{and ye shall dwell in the land which I have given to you, and to your fathers,}* Heb. *and sit* or, *dwell;* as Psalm 37.27. or, *remain abide;* as verse 11. Chapter 40.5,10. See Chapter 7.3. and 25.5.

*{but ye have not inclined your ear, nor hearkened unto me.}* See c. 7.24,26. & 11.8. & 17.23. & 34.14.

**V. 16.** *{Because the sons of Jonadab the son of Rechab have performed the commandment of their father, which he commanded them; but this people have not hearkened unto me.}* As v. 14,15. Their obedience to him shall rise in judgment against you to condemn you for your disobedience to me. See Matt. 12.41,42.

**V. 17.** *{Therefore thus saith the LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel;}* as ver. 13. c. 5.14.

*{Behold I will bring upon Judah, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, all the evil that I have pronounced against them:}* Or *denounced,* Heb. *spoken;* as Chap. 18.8. Heb. *I am bringing.* See c. 6.19. & 11.11. & 19.3.

*{because I have spoken unto them, but they have not heard; I have called unto them, but they have not answered.}* Or, *Because when I spake to them they would not hear; when I called unto them, they would not answer,* Prov. 1.24. Esay 50.2. Psalm 81.11. Chapter, 7.13. It is God that speaks, and that calls, whether immediately by himself, or by the ministry of his messengers, Esay 1.2,20. Chapter 15.19. Luke 10.16. 2 Cor. 5.20. & 13.3. Eph. 2.17. 1 Pet. 3.9.

**V. 18.** *{And Jeremiah said to the house of the Rechabites,}* Or, *Moreover,* as c. 33.1.

*{Thus saith the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel;}* As before, v. 13. so vers. 19.

*{Because ye have obeyed the commandment of Jonadab your father, and kept all his precepts, and done according to all that he hath commanded you}* Or, *that he commanded you.* Heb. *have heard,* for, *obeyed,* as v. 8.

**V. 19.** *{Therefore thus saith the LORD of Hosts the God of Israel, Jonadab, the son of Rechab shall not want a man to stand before me for ever.}* Heb. *There shall not be cut off a man of,* or, *unto Jonadab the son of Rechab standing before me all the days.* See the like forms of speech, chap. 33.17,18. intimating, that either his posterity should not be utterly rooted out, but continue in being, and consequently in Gods sight, as are all things that have any existence, Psalm 89.36. & 139.7. Prov. 15.3. see chap. 31.36. for to expound it, as some, of continuance in Gods favor; as Genesis 17.18. there is no necessity: or that they should not fail of some constant employment about the sacred Offices concerning the Law, as the phrase sometimes imports a special attendance, Deut. 10.8. 1 Kings 10.8. & 17.1.) which as some have not improbably supposed that they might have because it is reported of them that they were *Scribes,* and given to the study of *literature,* 1 Chr. 2.55. so long as that State, either civil or sacred should stand: for with restriction and relation to the continuance of those things, whereupon the matter mentioned depends, are the like forms of perpetuity commonly conceived, and so to be understood See Genesis 17.13. Exodus 21.6. Numbers 18.8. But what some others add out of *Eusebius* his *Ecclesiastical History,* l. 2. c. 22. from Hegesippus, that these Rechabites should be Priests, and that one of them, a Priest, being present at the murder of James the Just, should reprove them for so doing, is of no probability, but seems a frivolous supposition and groundless relation: for what part or portion could strangers, as they were, have in the Priesthood, Numbers 3.10. Nor seems that surmise of one of the Rabbines probable, that some of the Priests or Levites marrying of their daughters, some of their issue in process of time might come to be Priests: for the words seem to imply continuance in some present employment (if to such a notion they be restrained) and to a constant succession therein. And as unlikely is that which a learned Writer suggests, that these Rechabites in Jeremies days, should begin a new course of combining themselves into a body, and engaging themselves to a constant attendance on the Temple-service in such manner, as did *Anna* the Prophetess. Luke 2.37. and to a free contributing thereunto; and that therefore it was, that they did forbear the use of Wine, because they were daily to frequent the Temple; for that Law concerned the Priests only, and then only when they went in to do service Lev. 10.9. Ezekiel 4.21. Nor is there any ground, or probability of such their perpetual and general resort to the Temple service, living ordinarily in Tents abroad out of the City, v. 7,10.

## CHAPTER 36

**Verse 1.** *{And it came to passe in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah King of Judah, that this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying,}* The charge mentioned here to Jeremiah, seems to have been given him toward the latter end of this fourth year of *Jehoiakim* (see verse 9.) and in likelihood consequently to have been later than those here related. chap. 25. and 35. Heb. *it was that this word was;* as chapter 1.2. & 31.28. The Chapter contains first, a charge given by God unto Jeremy to gather together, and engross in one volume, the sum of all the Sermons, that he had delivered from his first entrance upon his prophetical function unto the time present, verse 2,3. 2 Jeremies performance of it by the help of Baruc his Scribe, v. 4. 3 Baruc's publishing of it by the Prophets appointment in the Temple upon a solemn fast day, v. 5–10. and after again upon occasion, at the Court in the Scribes chamber before the Princes, v. 11–15: 4 The effect it had upon those that there heard it, and their acquainting the King with it, verse 6–20. 5 The Kings hearing some part of it read and thereupon cutting it in pieces, and burning it in the fire, and giving order to apprehend Baruc and Jeremy, v. 21–26. 6 A second charge given the Prophet to write a new roll with further additionals to the former verse 27,28,32. together with a dreadful denunciation against Jehojakim for his burning of the other, ver. 29–31.

**V. 2.** *{Take thee}* An elegant redundancy; as Esay 8.1. & 10 v. 28.

*{a roll of a book}* That is, *a book* made up in *a roll,* or *a volume,* Esay 8.1. not stitched up, as ours usually are; but rolled up, as our records, and drafts of deeds, and instruments are ordinarily wont to be. Yet herein, as is supposed, differing from these, in that not fastened all the sheets together, as they, at the head; but either glued or sewed up sheet after sheet, the head of the sheet following to the tail of the foregoing, as our long Inventories oft are and so rolled up the whole body of it from the head of the first sheet to the end of the last. See Esay 34.4.

*{and write therein}* Heb. *and thou shalt write* (as Deut. 37.3. or cause to be written, as chap. 32.10. & Deut. 17.18. for the Rabbines conceit, as if the King were there enjoined to write out the book of the Law with his own hand, is frivolous) *on it;* as chap. 51.6. *on a book.*

*{all the words that I have spoken unto thee,}* Or, *all those things;* as Chapter 11.12. and 16.10. the sum and substance of the Sermons that have been preached by you hitherto: for the Rabbines dote, that would have by this roll meant the Book of the *Lamentations;* though that be one of the five which the Jews call *rolls,* or *volumes.*

*{against Israel, and against Judah, and against all the Nations}* Or *concerning;* as Esay 1.1. See chap. 1.10. & 25.11.

*{from the day that I spake unto thee:}* Or *from the day wherein I spake unto thee:* a defect of the Relative, as Ezekiel 28.15.

*{from the days of Josiah even unto this day.}* From the thirteenth year of Josiah, at what time he was called to his Prophetical office, c. 1.2. unto the fourth of *Jehoiakim,* by the space of three and twenty years, c. 25.3.

**V. 3.** *{It may be that the house of Judah will hear all the evil which I purpose to do unto them, that they may return every man from his evil way.}* Or *It may be that when the house of Judah shall hear all the evil that I intend* (Heb am *intending* or *thinking;* as c. 29.11.) *to do unto them* (unless they prevent it by timely repentance, c. 18.8.) *they will turn each one* (H. *a man;* as c. 34.9.) *from his evil way.* c. 36.3.

*{that I may forgive their iniquity, and their sin}* Heb. *and I will forgive;* as the like c. 46.3. Gods end in menacing evil being, that he may not inflict it; in threatening destruction, that he may not destroy Ezek. 3.18.

**V. 4.** *{Then Jeremiah called Baruch the son of Neriah; and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the LORD, which he had spoken unto him upon a roll of a Book.}* *Then:* Heb. *And* as Chapter 29.12. *upon* (as Joshua 10.13. so verse 18.) *a roll of a Book.* See on v. 2. Jeremy made that use of Baruc, as Paul did of Tertius, Rom. 16.22.

**V. 5.** *{And Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, I am shut up, I cannot go into the house of the LORD:}* Or, *I am detained* or *restrained,* (as 1 Samuel 21.5. 2 Chron. 20.37.) so that *I cannot go into the house of the Lord:* a defect of the particle; as Chapter 18.16. Esay 62.13. what the occasion of Jeremies restraint was at present, is not certainly known. One of the Rabbines says, he was shut up in prison; but that seems otherwise: for what needed the King then to give order for the apprehension of him? verse 26. Others say he was commended by the King to keep his house. But neither does this seem to sort well with the advice given by the princes for Baruch and him to hide themselves, verse 19. Others, that he dared not go abroad, or be seen in public for fear of the King, whose cruel disposition he was well acquainted with Chapter 26.20–23. But this Story in that Chapter related, sufficiently refutes. Others suppose that by some Ecclesiastical censure he might be restrained; and others again, by some Legal pollution: and others, Lastly, by some special inhibition from God, or secret intimation from his Spirit, as was Paul, Acts 16.6,7. But sufficient light of information herein failing us, there can be no certain determination of ought.

**V. 6.** *{Therefore go thou and read in the roll}* Heb. *And* (as Chapter, 29.27.) *thou shalt goe, and shalt reade;* as *thou shalt write,* verse 2.

*{which thou hast written from my mouth}* As I endited or dictated to you, verse 4,18.

*{the words of the LORD in the ears of the people}* In their hearing; as chap. 29.29 and so verse 14,15.

*{in the Lords house}* A defect of the preposition; as Chapter 29.25.

*{upon the fasting day:}* Heb. *on the day of fast:* on which, concourse of people would be out of all parts. See on vers. 9.

*{and also thou shalt read them}* Or; *and read them also;* as before.

*{in the ears of all Judah that come out of their cities.}* In the hearing, not of the inhabitants of Jerusalem only, but of all the people also, that from the several cities of Judah, repair hither, to seek God by supplication and prayer, as on such occasions they used to do, 2 Chron. 20.3,4.

**V. 7.** *{It may be they will present their supplication before the LORD,}* Heb. *their supplication will fall to the face* (or, *in the presence*) *of the Lord:* an allusion to the dejected gesture of persons that come to seek for mercy, Deut. 9.25. Matth. 26.39.

*{and will turn every one from his evil way.}* As verse 3. all prayer and supplication, humiliation and fasting, being without reformation and amendment unavailable, Esay 58.3,5. Chapter 12.12. Zach. 7.5,7. being no other than a bare bodily exercise, 1 Tim. 4.8.

*{for great is the anger and fury that God hath pronounced against this people.}* Or, *denounced.* Heb. *spoken;* as chap. 35.17. See chap. 32.37. Zach. 7.12.

**V. 8.** *{And Baruch the son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the Prophet commanded him: reading in the books the words of the LORD, in the Lords house.}* Heb. *in read;* as chap. 35.8. *to drink.* See before, on verse 6.

**V. 9.** *{And it came to passe in the fifth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah King of Judah, in the ninth month, that they proclaimed a fast before the LORD to all the people in Jerusalem, and to all the people that came from the cities of Judah unto Jerusalem.}* Or, *For,* (as chap. 23.22.) *so it was* (verse 1.) *in the fifth year of Jehoiakim* (in the beginning of that year of his reign, the year after that, wherein this charge was given Jeremy, verse 1,2. the length of the matter to be written in the roll, requiring some time for the engrossing of it, or it being on purpose reserved till then) *in the ninth month* (not of that year of his reign, but from the ordinary beginning of the year then current) that (a defect of the particle, as verse 1. (*a fast was proclaimed* (for the verb is indefinite; as chap. 6.30.) *to be held before the Lord* in his Temple at Jerusalem; as *they sold Joseph* to be carried into *Egypt,* Acts 7.9. as well for other the people of Judah, as for those that dwelt there, See on verse 6. This was not the ordinary yearly fast enjoined in the Law, Lev. 23.27. for that was kept on *the tenth day of the seventh month,* answering to part of our September, and part of our October, whereas this was held *in the ninth month,* which comprehended part of our November, and part of our December, called *Chisleu,* Zach. 7.1. two months later than that; and was therefore proclaimed upon some extraordinary occasion, whether of that long and great drought and dearth, thence proceeding, mentioned, Chap. 14.1,2. whereof some intimation seems there, verse 12. or upon some fear of a new invasion by foreign forces, Jehoiakim having been sometime before compelled to submit unto the King of Babylon, and to hold from him, Dan. 1.1. 2 Kings 24.1. from whom yet not long after he began to revolt, and thereby incensed him against him, 2 Kings 24.1. For that seems to me nothing probable, which yet some suggest, that the fast should be to bewail the calamities that had formerly befallen them, in the siege, and surprisal of the city, in the latter part of Jehojakims third year, and entrance of his fourth, a twelve-month, or more it may be, before: Nor does that instance of those fasts, Zach. 7.3,5. come home here: for their captivity, and the state of their city, Temple and Land, did all that while still continue the same. But I incline rather to that first of famine by drought, which might be further also increased much by the spoil made in the late invasions.

**V. 10.** *{Then read Baruch in the book,}* Heb. *And* (which may well be here retained) *Baruch read in the book;* as verse 8.

*{the words of Jeremiah}* Which he had dictated to him, verse 4,18. called also *the words of the Lord,* verse 6. because they came to the Prophets from him. See chap. 1,12.

*{in the house of the LORD}* See chap. 35.4.

*{in the chamber of Gemariah the son of Shaphan the Scribe.}* Out of the window of his chamber, or some balcony (for such also there were about those buildings) adjoining thereunto, and looking into the Court, where the people were assembled: Nor can I accord with that learned man, who supposes, that it was read only in private within the chamber to some few that were met together in that room. See Jeremies Charge to Baruc, verse 6. and the words following, which expressly control it.

*{the Scribe}* An officer belonging to the Temple, as another to the Kings Court, verse 12.

*{in the higher Court,}* Or *upper court* the Priests court, 2 Chron. 4.2. termed usually, *the inner,* 1 Kings 6.36. Ezek. 10.3. & 40.32. here the *upper* court, in regard of the peoples court, called also *the great,* 2 Chron. 4.9. and *the utter* court, Ezek. 10.5. & 40.20. being lower by divers degrees than it Ezek 40.31. Howbeit, there want not those, who by the *upper court* here understand the peoples court; yet not simply or absolutely, but that part of it wherein the men or males met, so termed in relation to the other part of it wherein the women used to assemble, being lower much than the other: but whether any such distinct court were so ancient or no, is uncertain: these Authors themselves acknowledging, that this *lower court* for the women, was not at the first built by Solomon.

*{at the entry of the new gate of the Lords house}* Or, *by* (as chapter 13.5. & 32.7.) *the entry of the new gate;* the East-gate by Jotham re-edified, 2 Kings 15.35.

*{in the ears of all the people.}* Or, *hearing,* as verse 6.

**V. 11.** *{When Micajah the son of Gemariah the son of Shaphan had heard out of the book all the words of the LORD;}* Or, *Now when Micajah had heard* Heb. *and Micajahu* (as *Jirmiahu,* chap. 1.1.) *heard* (but the copulative has oft a double notion: as chap. 13.12. & 34.10 or in this syntax the one may be fetched hither from the head of the next branch, verse 12.) *from off the book all the words of the Lord;* as verse 6.

**V. 12.** *{Then he went down into the Kings house}* Or, *He went to the Kings house;* the copulative hence taken into the former for the clearer expression, in our language, *And he heard; — and he went,* for, *And,* or, *Now.* (as chap. 30.4.) *when he had heard, — he went;* as chap. 26.10. *Now when they heard, — they came.*

*{went down into the Kings house}* Or, *went* simply, (see on chap. 26.10.) *to the Kings house:* the particle is wanting; as chap. 22.1.

*{into the Scribes chamber:}* Heb. *up to,* the chamber of Elishama the Kings Secretary, Verse 20. See Esay 36.3.

*{and lo all the Princes sat there;}* Heb. *sitting,* as 2 Kings 6.32. even *Elishama the Scribe:* Whose chamber it was.

*{and Delaiah the son of Shemajah, and Elnathan the son of Achbor, and Gemariah the son of Shaphan, and Zedekiah the son of Hananiah, and all the Princes.}* That is, the rest of them, as chap. 39.13 and as, *all the houses;* chap. 52.13. of one of these, see chap. 26.22 of other of them, verse 25.

**V. 13.** *{Then Micajah declared unto them all the words that he had heard, when Baruch read the book in the ears of the people.}* Heb. *And* (which may well be retained) *and, words,* for *things;* as chap. 26.16. (for if he had related all the words that he spake they should not have needed to send for the roll; nor was his memory so good) and, *read in the book* as verse 10 and *ears,* for, *hearing,* as there. Now for what end Micajah did this is uncertain; whether out of a malicious disposition to cause the Prophet and his Scribe to be questioned as Shemajah, chap. 29.24,25. or out of a religious intention, to have some course taken, if it might be for the pacifying of Gods wrath, and preventing of the judgment denounced, is not certain: yet the latter seems the more probable.

**V. 14.** *{Therefore all the Princes sent Jehudi the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelamiah, the son of Cushi unto Baruch, saying;}* Of this *Jehudi,* see further on verse 21.

*{Take in thine hand the roll, wherein thou hast read in the ears of the people, and come,}* *Therefore,* or, *then;* Heb. *And* (as verse 4.) and, *which thou readest in it:* an elegant redundancy; as the like, chap. 7.14. and, *ears,* for, *hearing;* as verse 10,13.

*{So Baruch the son of Neriah took the book in his hand, and came unto them.}* Heb, *And.* as Chap. 28.7.

**V. 15.** *{And they said unto him, Sit down now, and read it in our ears:}* Heb. *Sit,* for, *sit down,* as Esay 47.1.

*{So Baruch read it in their ears.}* Heb. *and;* as verse 14. and *ears,* as before.

**Ver. 16.** *{Now it came to passe,}* Heb. *And it was,* as Verse 1.

*{when they had heard all the words,}* Or, *those words,* or, *those things:* as verse 13. and so after again.

*{they were afraid, both one and other;}* Or, that *they were afraid:* the particle supplied, as verse 1. *both one and other;* as well bad as good: all of both sorts were stricken alike with terror and dread: as Acts 5.11. or, *they were afraid,* and looked *one upon another:* as men astonished are wont to do, Esay 13.8. or, as some, they spake one to another; or, consulted one with another; they laid their heads together: but the parallel place seems to lead unto the former supply. Heb. *a man to,* or, *on his friend,* or, *neighbor;* as chap. 34.15. and it is, howsoever, a complexive form, such as v. 9.

*{and said to Baruch; we will surely tell the King all these words.}* Or, *things;* as before. Heb. *telling tell:* as 1 Sam. 22.24. Judg 14.12. to try whether any good might thereby be wrought upon him: for they seem to be better affected than either themselves, or other of them afterward in Zedekiahs time were. See on chap. 38.4.

**V. 27.** *{And they asked Baruch, saying, Tell us now how didst thou write all these words at his mouth?}* Or, *How couldst thou write* (in a potential notion; as Chap. 2.23.) *all these words,* or, *things* (as before) *from his mouth:* for so the Hebrew has it: as Job 22.22.

**V. 18.** *{And Baruch answered them, He pronounced all these words to me with his mouth,}* Heb. *from his mouth;* as verse 17. They seem to lay here too much weight upon the words of the text, who following the Latin rendering them, *He spake them as if he read,* would have Boruchs meaning to be, he uttered them as distinctly and readily all along, as if he had read them out of a book, whereby it might appear that they were by an immediate instinct of spirit suggested unto him. But the terms of the text imply no more, but that the Prophet dictated unto him, what he should write; in doing whereof, he might well for ought I see make use of such copies of his Sermons formerly delivered, as he had by him: as also he did sometime in likelihood, not of some of his own only, but of the Sermons of what Prophets also that had been before him. See Chap. 45.19,43,44. & 51.15–19.

*{and I wrote them with ink in the book}* Heb. *on the book;* as Josh. 10.13. and the Jewish Doctors criticism seems here over-nice, that would have it to be spoken in way of anticipation: for it is not a book, says he, until it be written in, and written out: as if *tables* to write on, were not tables, until such use had been made of them; a defect there is of the pronoun: as Chapter 34.10.

*{with ink}* The usual material to write with in those times; not added here as a learned Writer, to intimate, that he did not draw them on slate, or in lead; or, on waxed tables; for their own eyes to whom he spake showed them the contrary: but intimating only the ordinary manner of doing it.

**V. 19.** *{Then said the Princes unto Baruch, Go hide thee, thou and Jeremiah, and let no man know where ye be}* Heb. *And;* as verse 4. and, *be hid;* the passive in a reciprocal notion; as Chap. 23.24. & 34.14. They foresaw that the King might be enraged against them, and give order to apprehend them; as he had formerly for Uriah, Chap. 26.21. that which also he did verse 25. and they seem to have been desirous of and careful for their indemnity and safety: the one of them had been formerly employed by the King for the bringing back of Uriah, when he was fled into Egypt Chap. 26.22. but it may be had now some remorse for what then he had done. See verse 25. However, it appears that Jeremy was not at present in custody, as some have said. See verse 5.

**V. 20.** *{And they went in to the King into the Court,}* Into the Inner Court, where his personal residence usually was; for the Kings palace was divided into three Courts; the utter, next the ordinary way, the middle, and the inner. See 2 Kings 20.4. The Scribes Chamber, and of other principal officers was in likelihood in the middle court, the Kings peculiar lodgings in the innermost; for the word *court* here, as also verse 10. comprehends not the open *court-yard* only, as we call it, but the buildings also about it.

*{but they laid up the roll in the chamber of Elishama the Scribe,}* Because uncertain whether the King would desire to see it or no.

*{and told all the words in the ears of the King.}* Acquainted the King with the main sum and substance of the subject matter that it contained. See the like forms, Verse 31.

**V. 21.** *{So the King sent Jehudi to fetch the roll.}* Heb, *And,* as verse 14. and, *to take the roll,* for, to take and bring it: a complexive form; like that, Psal. 78.18. *thou hast taken,* or, *received gifts, to men;* that is, to give to, or, bestow upon, *men;* Eph. 4.8. & Prov. 25.22. *thou shalt rake coales upon his head,* that is, *take and heap* them, Rom. 12.22. So Gen. 27.9 *take me two kids,* for, *take* and bring me: and 1 Sam. 4.3. *let us take the Ark from Shilo;* that is, take and bring it: or, as we use to say, *fetch it:* and so we render it not amiss both here and there: for that word with us also includes a two-fold notion. See the like forms, Esay 38.17.21. This *Jehudi* seems to have been one that was usually employed as a messenger, both by the King and the Princes, See verse 14. what a learned Writer here says of him, that he was a man much of the Kings own disposition, and one that the King therefore had continually about him, I suppose is no more than his mere conjecture.

*{and he took it out of Elishama the Scribes chamber;}* Took and brought it, as before; for the word is the same.

*{and Jehudi read it}* Some part of the matter contained in it; not all, verse 13.

*{in the ears of the King}* In his hearing: as verse 6.14. and hereafter again.

*{and in the ears of all the Princes which stood by the King.}* Attending upon him. Heb, *from off;* as at some convenient distance: he *sate,* verse 22. they *stood:* as 1 Kings 10.8. See Esay 6.1,2.

**V. 22.** *{Now the King sat in the winterhouse,}* Heb. *And.* as Chap. 30.4. *house,* or, *room;* for the manner of Kings and and great men was to have houses or rooms fitted for, and suitable to the several seasons of the year; some wider, more open, and airy, to let the wind and fresh air in the more freely, which they made use of in the summer, Judg. 3.20. chap. 22.14. Others closer and warmer, which in winter time they more frequently used. See Amos 3.15.

*{in the ninth month}* Wherein the fast had been held; one of their winter months. See on ver. 9.

*{and there was a fire on the hearth burning before him.}* Heb. *only; and the hearth burning before him:* that is indeed, fire burning upon it, verse 22. but the particle here used has no such notion of *upon* here, but is a note only, as also in divers places elsewhere, of that which we call a nominative case. So Prov. 16.33. Ezek. 31.4.

**V. 23.** *{And it came to passe, that,}* Heb. *And it was,* as verse 9.

*{when Jehudi had read three or four leaves}* The word properly signifies *doors,* whence rendered in the dual form, *two-leaved doors,* Esay 45.1. and as we take the word from *a leaf* of paper, to design thereby *a board,* or *boards,* whereof such *doors* consist. So the Hebrews take from such *doors,* or, *boards,* whereof they are, made, the word to signify *leaves* of paper, parchment, or the like whereof rolls or books are made. So called, say some, because in figure and shape they resemble such tables or boards. Others, because they are shut and opened as doors are, Esay 29.11,12. & 34.4. chap, 32.11. Rev. 5.1,2. & 6.14. some learned Interpreters render it *leaves,* as ours does: that the Scoliast controls, because it was *a roll,* not *a book,* such as we commonly use: and he instead thereof substitutes *columns:* in my mind more unfitly, since the term of *columns* is used commonly for the two moieties, or counter-parts (if I may so call them) of a page. Another learned man renders it, *three or four titles* of the sections into which it was divided. I see not why we may not retain, either with ours and others, *leaves:* or with the old Latin, *pages:* seeing that either word may be used, as well of the parcel of a roll, as of a stitch book. Heb. *three leaves and four,* for, *three or four,* as Esay 17.6. *four, five,* by an ellipsis, for *four or five:* the copulative in a disjunctive notion: as, *father and mother.* for, *father or mother,* Exod. 21.15. So *two witnesses and three,* for *two or three witnesses* 2 Cor. 13.1. and a trajection withal, *three leaves or four,* for, *three or four leaves:* as, *seven shekels and ten,* for, *seventeen shekels* Chap. 32.9.

*{he cut it with the penknife}* *He.* to wit, *the King;* the pronoun for the noun: as, *he went,* for, the King *went;* 2 Kings 25.4. not Jehudi that read it, but Jehojakim to whom he read: taking it out of his hands, and not enduring to hear any more of it, verse 29. Heb, *he tore it with the Scribes knife,* or *razor,* as it is rendered, Psal. 52.2. Esay 7.20. such as the Scribes used to make or mend their pens with, and to raze out ought in any roll or writing, when occasion was so to do.

*{and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth, until all the roll was consumed in the fire that was on the hearth.}* A complexive form, as that before, verse 21. together with a trajection, as before: *he cast it into the fire,* and left it *on the fire,* (so is the Hebrew) *that was on the hearth untill the roll was consumed:* as Chap. 24.10.

**V. 24.** *{Yet they were not afraid, nor rent their garments,}* In token of grief, or fear; as the manner with them was. See Esay 36.22. & 37.1. See also on verse 27. The Princes feared, the King and his servants feared not. See ver. 16.

*{neither the King, nor any of his servants,}* Heb. *the King, and all* (for, *any,* as Chap. 40.5.) *his servants.* See Chap. 35.6, *ye and your sons;* neither *ye* nor *your sons.*

*{that heard all these words}* Or, *though they heard all these things;* as verse 2,13.

**V. 25.** *{Nevertheless Elnathan, and Delaiah, and Gemariah, had made intercession to the King that he would not burn the roll,}* Or, *And albeit,* or; *Notwithstanding that;* so is the particle used Neh. 6.1. Esay 49.15. And it may be observed, that this *Elnathan* who had before so far condescended to the Kings pleasure, to be used by him as an instrument for the apprehending of Uriah, Chap. 26.22. was one of those who now endeavored to dissuade and stay the King from the burning of Jeremies book. See ver. 12,19.

*{but he would not hear them}* Or; *Yet* (as Chap. 35.14.) *he would not hearken to them.* Heb. *and he hearkened not unto them:* being desperately bent to run on in a godless course to his own ruin: as Chap. 8.6.

**V. 26.** *{But the King commanded Jerahmeel the son of Hammelech, and Seraiah the son of Azriel, and Shelamiah the son of Abdiel to take Baruch the Scribe, and Jeremiah the Prophet}* Heb, *And* (which may well here be retained) *charged* (as Deut. 3.28.) *Jerahmeel,* or, *Jerachmeel, the son of Hammelech,* or, *the Kings Son:* but it seems rather to have been a proper name, as Chap. 38.6. for it is not likely that the King, though a wicked man, would use his own sons as pursuivants, or messengers.

*{but the LORD hid them}* Heb. *and;* as Chap. 35.6. God suffered them not to be found, having before withdrawn themselves, by the advice of the Princes, verse 19. God herein showing his care to protect and secure his Prophets, according to his promise, Chap. 1.19. & 15.21. Though we need not descend to such niceties, as the Jewish Doctors here do, affirming that God either cast a mist about them, or made their eye-sight fail the kings messengers, when they came into those places where they were: as was done with the men of Sodome, Gen, 19.11. and with those that came to seize on Eliseus, 2 Kings 6.18. God could many other ways secure them.

**V. 27.** *{Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah,}* Or, *Again the word of the Lord came,* Heb, *was,* as Chap. 1.2.) *unto Jeremiah,* as Chap. 24.4.

*{(after that the King had burnt the roll, and the words that Baruch wrote at the mouth of Jeremiah) saying}* Or, *with the words:* as Chap. 26.21. the roll wherein they were written: otherwise Gods Word cannot be burnt, no more than it can be bound, 2 Tim. 2.9. And the Jewish Doctors here dally, after their wonted manner, who because it is said, *burnt the roll, and the words,* hence gather, that there should have been a two-fold renting of their garments, verse 24. one for the burning of the parchment; and another for the burning of the writing in it: they might better have said, one for the cutting or rending of it, and another for the burning of it, but these are mere fancies.

*{at his mouth.}* Heb. *from his mouth;* as before, Verse 17,18.

**V. 28.** *{Take thee again another roll,}* Heb. *Return* (as Gen. 26.18.) *and take thee* (as verse 2.) *another roll.* See verse 18.

*{and write in it all the former words that were in the first roll, which Jehojakim the King of Judah hath burnt.}* Heb. *write on it.* as ver. 4. *all the former words,* or, *things* as verse 13. *that were in the first roll,* or, *former:* as Esay 48.3.

**V. 29.** *{And thou shalt say to Jehojakim King of Judah,}* Or, *And say* (as Chap 35.13.) *unto* (as verse 12 chap. 26.5.) or, *concerning* (as chap. 18.8,9.) *Jehojakim,* ver. 30. and thus rather, as the particle does with words of speech most frequently signify, as Esay 1.1. & 2.1, Chap. 16.3. & 49.1,7. for it is not likely that God would have him to present himself to Jehojakim, from whom he had taken a course to conceal him; but would have him to put these things into the new roll, verse 30.

*{Thus saith the LORD, Thou hast burnt this roll.}* Or, *Because thou hast burnt this roll.* See the like defect of this causal, Chap. 10.14. the rather to be supplied here, to make it cohere the more fitly with verse 30.

*{saying, why hast thou written therein, saying,}* Spoken as Jehojakims words, not unlike to those of Zedekiah, Chap 32.3. This, say some, he would have spoken to him, if he could have been found. But God is wont to attribute unto persons speeches correspondent to their inward thoughts and imaginations, which he sees and regards. See Esay 14.13. & 47.7. Chapter 2.25. & 6.16,17.

*{The King of Babylon shall certainly come and destroy this land}* Heb. *shall coming come;* as Habb 2.3.

*{and shall cause to cease from thence both man and beast?}* Chap. 32.10. that it may keep an exact Sabbath; for thereunto the word alludes, 2 Chr. 36.21.

**V. 30.** *{Therefore thus saith the LORD, of Jehojakim King of Judah, He shall have none to sit upon the Throne of David;}* None of his issue shall sit upon it, for any time worth speaking of: for his son Jehojacin; or Jeconiah, reigned but three months and ten days, 2 Kings 24.8. 2 Chron. 36.9. and Zedekiah his Uncle succeeded him, 2 Kings 24.17. See chap. 1.1,3 & 22.30. where the like is also denounced against his son Jeconiah Yet we need not strain the term of *sitting* here with a learned late Writer to have it signify *remaining; staying abiding;* as Psal. 9.7. the sense is proper and plain enough, as before: and it is like that, Chapter 37.9. *the Chaldeans shall not depart.* and yet they did depart, as is said there, verse 5. but not for any space of time, or to any purpose: not unlike to that of our Savior concerning Jairus his daughter, *the damsel is not dead,* Mat 9.24.

*{and his dead body shall be cast out in the day to the heat, and in the night to the frost.}* Or, *to the heat by day, and to the frost by night:* that being so exposed, it may the sooner putrefy and become the more vile and loathsome; not that his body could be sensible of such usage, or himself being deceased of ought that should befall his body; but that the sight of a Kings body in such a condition, should be an hideous spectacle, and horrid monument of Gods heavy wrath and indignation against him, unto all that should behold it, Esay 66.24. See the very same in effect denounced before against him, chap. 22.19.

**V. 31.** *{And I will punish him, and his seed, and his servants for their iniquity,}* Heb. *I will visit upon him, and his seed, and his servants, their iniquity.* So Chap. 23.34. See Chap 21.7.

*{and I will bring upon them, and the Inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the men of Judah, all the evil that I have pronounced against them:}* See Chap. 35.17.

*{but they hearkened not.}* Or, *because they would not hear.* Heb, *and they heard not;* but the copulative has sometime a causative notion: as Esay 64.5, *thou art wrath, and we have sinned,* for, *because we have sinned.*

**V. 32.** *{Then took Jeremiah another roll, and gave it to Baruch the Scribe the son of Neriah, who wrote therein from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the book which Jehojakim king of Judah had burnt in the fire; and there were added besides unto them many like words.}* Or, *So Jeremy took,* as verse 14. Heb. *And.* and, *wrote upon it;* as 18. and, *many words as they.* Thus dealt God with the roll that Jehojakim burnt; as before with the yoke that Hananiah broke, Chap. 28.13,14. and the King gained no more by burning the book, than wicked Princes and People by murdering of Gods Prophets, 2 Chron. 24.21,22,25. Zach. 1.5,6. an increase of guilt, Chap. 26.19. and an addition of wrath, Esay 28.14,22.
