Chapter 52.34. some understand it here of a continued allowance of diet by Nebuzaradan assigned him; but the entertaining of him with a meal's meat (though it is not probable that he would neglect so common a courtesy) was scarce worth the reciting: and for constant allowance for the future, it is most likely that he would leave that to Gedaliah, unto whom he was to commend him; the first therefore is here most probable: he would not dismiss the Prophet to travel in a land so wasted, and dispeopled, without competent provision and necessaries for his journey.

*{and a reward}* Or a present, rather; for it is used for a gift, either tendered in testification of due respect and honor, as Ezekiel 20.40. or exhibited in signification of grace and favor, Esther 2.18. which because it consisted sometime in messes of meat, Genesis 43.34. 2 Samuel 11.8. some of the Jewish doctors would make this and the former all one: but there is small reason for it.

*{and let him go.}* Or, *dismissed him*; as verse 1.

**Verse 6.** *{Then went Jeremiah unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah,}* A city in the land of Benjamin, Josh. 18.26. 1 Kings 15.22. Then Heb. *And* as c. 39.9.

*{and dwelt with him among the people that were left in the Land.}* Or, *abode with him*. Heb. *sat*; and, *in the midst*: as verse 5.

**Verse 7.** *{Now when all the Captains of the forces, which were in the fields,}* Having fled, and being scattered here and there, for fear of the Chaldeans. See 2 Kings 25.23.

*{even they and their men}* Their complices and their followers; as Gen. 14.24. & 24.59. 1 Sam. 23.8.

*{heard that the King of Babylon had made Gedaliah Governor in the land,}* Whom they conceived good hopes of, as knowing him to be a man of an ingenuous disposition.

*{and had committed unto him men, and women, and children, and of the poor of the land, of them that were not carried away captive to Babylon;}* Heb. *little one*; or *little child*; taken collectively; as Esther 3.13. and *poverty* for, *poor*; as also 2 Kings 24.14. and 25.12.

**Verse 28.** *{Then they came to Gedaliah to Mizpah}* Heb. *And they heard—and they came;* as c. 38.7,8.

*{even Ishmael}* One of the blood royal, c. 41.1. Heb. *and*, for *even*; to wit, as c. 42.1.

*{the son of Nethaniah,}* Heb. *Nethanijahu:* as *Jirmijahu* c. 1.1. and the like, Esay 1.1.

*{and Johanan, and Jonathan the sons of Kareah}* *Johanan,* or *John;* as Luke 1.14. for the name is the same; and so verse 13,15.

*{and Seriah the son of Tanhumeth}* Or, *Tanchumeth;* as *Achaz,* Mat. 1.9. See Esay 1.1.

*{and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite,}* The name of a family in the tribe of Judah, so called from the city, or seat of their abode, 1 Chr. 2.54. & 9.16. & 27.15.

*{and Jezaniah the son of a Maachathite,}* Another family so called from some principal man or woman of special note in it, 1 Chr. 2.48. & 9.15. & 27.16.

*{they and their men}* As before, v. 7.

**Verse 9.** *{And Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan, sware unto them, and to their men, saying, fear not to serve the Chaldeans:}* Heb. *to stand before them;* as Chapter 35.19. See 2 Kings 25.24.

*{dwell in the land}* As Psalm 37.3. or, abide; stay in it: leave it not: as v. 6.

*{and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you.}* As chap. 38.20.

**Verse 10.** *{As for me, Behold, I will dwell at Mizpah, to serve the Chaldeans, which will come unto us:}* Upon occasion of state from the king. Heb. *And* (as 1 Chr. 28.2. See v. 4.) *I will abide,* or *reside,* (Heb. *sit*; as verse 6.) at Mitspah, a frontier town; having its name from the garrison or sentinel, there wont to be kept: whence the diversity of versions, Hosea 5.2.

*{but ye}* Or, *as for you*; Heb. *and ye*: as Esay 65.11. So before; *And I*.

*{gather ye wine and summer fruits, and oil,}* For their harvest was past before the city was taken, being dispatched usually within compass of the three first months, or near thereabout: whereas the city was stormed in the fourth, Chapter 32.2. See Deuteronomy 16.1,9. Wine, for grapes, Esay 62.9. (as grapes, for wine, Hosea 3.1.) and oil, for olives, whereof oil is made as wine of grapes, Exodus 27.20. Judges 9.9,13. and, summer, for summer-fruits: as Esay 10.9. and with the Greeks the like. So verse 12.

*{and put them in your vessels}* Reserve them after your wonted manner for store, as in time of peace and safety people are wont to do, making account in due time to make use of, and enjoy them, not fearing to be by any stripped of them, as in times of hostility frequently falls out, c. 5.17.

*{and dwell in your cities that ye have taken}* Continue in those places that you have seized on, and seated yourselves in being left and abandoned. See c. 51.29,32.

**Verse 11.** *{Likewise when all the Jews that were in Moab, and among the Ammonites, and in Edom, and that were in all the Countries, heard that the King of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah; and that he had set over them Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan;}* That had fled into foreign parts for succor and safety upon the Chaldeans' invasion. See Esay 16.4. *in all countries,* for all other countries: as 2 Chronicles 32.22. Cant. 4.9. Esay 26.13. chapter 32.20.

**Verse 12.** *{Even all the Jews returned out of all places whither they were driven, and came to the land of Judah to Gedaliah unto Mizpah,}* Heb. *And also all the Jews—heard—and all the Jews returned;* as v. 7,8. into the land of Judah, and Benjamin: the whole bearing the name from the principal part.

*{and gathered wine, and summer fruits, very much.}* Heb. *in much abundance*: as 1 Kings 4.29. the land being of itself rich and fertile; and few left to perceive and enjoy its revenue. See verse 10.

**Verse 13.** *{Moreover, Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the Captains of the forces that were in the fields came to Gedaliah to Mizpah;}* Here begins a new narration of a conspiracy entered into by some of the forementioned parties, v. 8. against Gedaliah, which being discovered by some other of them, they acquaint Gedaliah with it, and offer him their service to prevent it, verse 13–15. whom he giving no credit to, as being confident of the others' fidelity, v. 14,16. is treacherously surprised and murdered by them, together with those as well Jews as Chaldeans about him, Chapter 41.1–3. whereupon mischiefs and miseries, afterward related, ensue.

*{Moreover}* Heb. *And;* as chap. 33.1.

*{all the Captains}* The rest of them: as, all the houses, for the rest of them, 2 King. 25.9. those of whom before, v. 7. See the like, chap. 39.13.

*{came to Gedaliah}* The second time to disclose to him the mischievous plot contrived against him.

**Verse 14.** *{And said unto him, Dost thou certainly know;}* Heb. *knowing know:* as chap. 13.12. but the negative, is wanting; as very frequent in interrogatives of this nature: for their meaning is apparently, *Dost thou not know?* undoubtedly it is so? and you must well be assured of it. So they to Eliseus, *Dost thou know?* 2 Kings 2.3. for *Dost thou not know?* as it is rendered Job 20.4. See the like before, c. 31.20.

*{that Baalis the King of the Ammonites hath sent Ismael the son of Nethaniah to slay thee?}* Heb. *to smite thee in soul,* or *to strike thy soul;* that is, to take away your life: as Numbers 35.11. Thus the king having, as by a lineal descent, a malignant affection unto God's people, puffs up this young gallant (who among others in likelihood had fled for shelter into those parts, ch. 40.11.) with hopes of raising himself by the ruin of Gedaliah, that he might be an instrument of this people's further calamity, whereby himself might have the more liberty to prey upon the country at pleasure, having none now to protect them. Because some of the Greek copies here render the words, the queen of the king of the sons of Ammon; (So the Hebrew commonly styles them, see chapter 49.1.) a learned late writer would have the word Baalis here used to be no proper name of any person, man or woman; but a title of dignity: for, says he, as the queen-mother was among the Jews called *Gebirah,* c. 13.18. So was the same among the Ammonites called *Baalia,* which by a various dialect is no other than *Baalith* in Hebrew: and adds withal, that this queen dowager being regent in her son's minority, mingled her own malignity with this prince's ambition, to work this mischief. But this I shall leave to the judgment of others.

*{But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam believed them not.}* An ingenuous disposition is seldom suspicious. chapter 11.18,19. Heb. *And:* as; verse 10.

**Verse 15.** *{Then Johanan the son of Kareah spake to Gedaliah in Mizpah secretly saying,}* When they could not prevail therein with him jointly, he attempts to effect it more privately; supposing that in private he might be persuaded to hearken to that, which he would not openly take notice of, or seem at least to be acknown of: withal tendering his service for the preventing of the stroke, that was likely to fall upon Gedaliah, by turning it upon the traitor himself.

*{Let me go, I pray thee, and I will slay Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and no man shall know it.}* Heb. *I will smite;* as 2 Kings 6.21. and *man,* for *any one: man shall not know;* as c. 38.24. and a defect of the pronoun *it;* as 1 King. 1.11. & 2.32. So also v. 3. *wherefore should he slay thee?* Heb. *smite* or *strike thy soul;* or *thee in soul:* as before, v. 14.

*{that all the Jews which are gathered unto thee, should be scattered, and the remnant in Judah perish?}* Being as sheep without a shepherd, Zacha. 13.7. See the like emphatical form in way of expostulation, chapter 37.13,17. Heb. *and,* for *that;* as chapter, 39.14.

**Verse 16.** *{But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam said unto Johanan the son of Kareah;}* Heb. *and,* as v. 14.

*{Thou shalt not do this thing:}* Heb. *word:* as Chapter 22. verse 4.

*{for thou speakest falsely of Ishmael}* Heb. *thou speakest falsehood,* or *a lye;* as chapter 29.9. & 43.2. Thus the well-minded intending no evil to others, and deeming others by themselves, are not easily induced to think evil of others, or that others intend evil to them; and by occasion thereof, are oft deceived and ensnared to their utter undoing: Yet it behooved a prudent man, in Gedaliah's place especially, upon such intimation to have been more cautelous than he, it seems, was.

## CHAPTER 41

**Verse 1.** *{Now it came to passe,}* Heb. *And it was:* as Esay 36.1.

In this chapter is related the barbarous murder executed upon Gedaliah, and others with him, with other villainies after committed, and further evils ensuing thereupon. See 2 King. 25.25.

*{in the seventh month}* The month Tisri, containing part of our September, and part of our October: hence the *fast of the seventh moneth,* for the murder of Gedaliah, Zach. 7.5. & 8.19.

*{that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah the son of Elishama,}* Whether this Elishama were the same with the scribe of that name, c. 37.12. is uncertain.

*{of the seed royal}* Heb. *of the seed of the kingdome;* as Ezek. 17.13. in regard whereof Ishmael might pretend to have more right to the rulership of the land than Gedaliah and was the fitter instrument for the Ammonite to make use of for his own ends, chapter 40.14.

*{and the Princes of the King}* Heb. *great ones;* as chapter 39.15. Such of the princes as had formerly escaped by flight, either before the siege began, misdoubting the worst, when they saw the land invaded, and harassed, by so potent an army; or when it was for a time intermitted, by occasion of the Egyptian forces, that came to relieve the city, Chapter, 37.5. or after the surprisal of it, when they stole away by night 2 Kings, 25.4.

*{even ten men with him.}* Heb. *and ten men with him:* which *ten* some understand of the princes before mentioned; and so the copulative should have only an explicative notion; as chap. 39.4. and so our version takes it. But then there is a doubt how ten or eleven men should be able to make such massacre, as was by these there made. To which some answer that these great men came not without their followers: and others add, that these ten are especially mentioned, as ten persons expert and skillful to do mischief (Ezek. 21.31.) inured unto, and exercised in shedding of blood, such as Abimelech hired to assist him in the murder of his brethren, Judges 9.4,5. which Ishmael, for that end, brought along with him, and are said therefore to come not with them, but *with him.* See verse 7.

*{came unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah}* The place of his residence, Chapter, 40.6. as to give him a kind visit.

*{and there they did eat bread together in Mizpah}* Being entertained by him and as familiar friends admitted to his board. See the same form Psalm 41.9. Luke 14.1.

**Verse 2.** *{Then arose Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and the ten men that were with him}* Men fit for such a villainous and barbarous employment. *Then.* Heb. *And;* as c. 40. v. 15.

*{and smote Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan with the sword, and slew him, whom the King of Babylon had made Governor over the land.}* There seems to be a trajection in the words, as if it were said; *They smote with the sword, and slew Gedaliah the sonne of Ahikam the sonne of Shaphan, whom the King had made governour in the land:* but there may well be more than so in it: the words may be divided into two distinct sentences; *they smote with the sword* (which is in effect as much, as *they slew:* so chapter, 26.23.) *Gedaliah, &c. and they slew him,* or, *so* (as, Chapter, 40.5.) or, *thus* (as Chapter, 10.26. *they slew him, whom the King had made Governour in the land:* the vile fact repeated with this addition to aggravate the crime: the welfare of the whole land and people left in it, depending mainly upon this one man's safety. See c. 40.15.

**Verse 3.** *{Ishmael also slew}* Heb. *And* (as c. 1.3.) *Ismael smote;* as c. 40.14. See Acts 7.23.

*{all the Jews that were with him, even with Gedaliah at Mizpah,}* Having any relation to him, or in any place about him, or that offered to oppose his violence, and to hinder the execution of his murderous design: for he slew not the main body of the people: but carried them away with him, v. 9,10.

*{and the Chaldeans that were found there}* That is, *were;* as Est. 1.15. c. 52.25. So v. 8.

*{and the men of war.}* Or, being *men of war;* as spoken, not of the Jews, (of which 2 Kings 25.4.) but of the Chaldeans: for such in likelihood were all the Chaldeans, that stayed there with Gedaliah.

**Verse 4.** *{And it came to passe the second day after he had slain Gedaliah, and no man knew it:}* And it was not yet bruited abroad: for they had slain all sorts, that were about Gedaliah as well friends as foes, their own countrymen, as strangers, that none, as near as they could, might escape, to divulge what they had done. Heb. *a man knew not:* as c. 39.15.

**Verse 5.** *{That there came certain from Shechem, and from Shilo, and Samaria, even fourscore men,}* Whose way to Jerusalem lay by Mizpah, or near at least to it: Or, they might make it in their way, to visit Gedaliah, and those with him there. Heb. *And* (as Chapter 39.4.) *there came men,* for *certain men,* as chapter 26.22.

*{having their beards shaven, and their clothes rent, and having cut themselves,}* In the manner and habit of mourners; such, in part, as being heathenish, was disallowed among God's people, and inhibited in the Law, Leviticus 19.27. Deuteronomy 14.1. 1 King. 18.28. chap. 47.5. But hereof see on c. 16.6. Heb. *shaven of beard;* and *torn of garments:* as Esay 36.22.

*{with offerings and incense in their hand}* Having such things with them; as 2 King 5.5. c. 38.10,11.

*{to bring them to the house of the LORD.}* But here question is moved, to what purpose these folk should travel with such presents to Jerusalem, when as both city and temple were now razed and ruined. To this the Jewish doctors answer, some of them, that they had not yet heard of the taking of the city, when they set out, but heard of it on the way, and thereupon put themselves into that mournful habit. But against this may be objected, that though they had not heard of the storming and sacking of the city; yet they could not but hear of the strait siege that was about it: and could have little hope therefore of any free access to the temple. Other of them therefore say, that they had heard indeed of the taking of the city, and the deportation of the people: but not of the demolition of the temple: which afterward hearing of, when they were on their way, they turned in unto Mizpah, where they heard that Gedaliah the new ruler resided: for as for that which some add, that they might hope to find an altar built at Mizpah, instead of that at Jerusalem, such as Samuel sometime erected there, 1 Samuel 7.5—9. is nothing probable. It is more likely that, albeit they had heard both of the destruction of the city, and demolition of the temple, which could not but be known in places no farther remote before that time, and was the occasion of putting them into that mournful habit; yet they were traveling toward Jerusalem, to mourn over the sad condition of the place, and in hope to find some of the priests there, and an altar at least erected in the room of the former, to receive such oblations as they carried along with them: and *to the House of the Lord,* may be here well put, for to the place where it sometime stood: As, *Houses,* and *Palaces,* and *Forts,* and *Towers,* for places, where which sometimes were situated, Esay 33.22. and 31.14.

**Verse 6.** *{And Ishmael came forth from Mizpah to meet them,}* Or, *went out,* &c.

*{weeping all along as he went;}* Heb. *in going, and weeping:* as Chapter 50.4. Making show of the like mournful disposition with them, that they might not mistrust him.

*{and it came to passe as he met them, that he said unto them, Come to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam.}* As feigning himself to be one of his followers. Howbeit, I conceive that to be groundless, which a learned writer hence gathers, that these persons intended not at all to take Mizpah in their way, had they not been ticed in thither by this train of Ishmael's.

**Verse 7.** *{And so it was when they came into the middest of the City}* Or, *into the City;* as 1 Samuel 9.14. and so afterward, *into the midst of the pit,* for *into the pit:* as, *in the midst of a pit,* for, *in a pit,* 2 Samuel, 23.30.

*{that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah slew them, and cast them into the middest of the pit,}* Heb. *slew them into the middest of the pit:* A defective or complexive speech. The like whereunto: See Psalm, 89,39,44. Esay, 14.12. and 38.14,17,21. Chapter, 30.10,11. and the like is observed, 1 Maccabees, 7.19.

*{he, and the men that were with him.}* For he alone could not do it: but such murderous varlets, as he made use of, assisted him in it, and did the work for him. See v. 2.

**Verse 8.** *{But ten men were found among them}* Heb. *And,* as c. 10.16. and, *were found,* for *were,* as v. 3.

*{that said unto Ishmael, slay us not}* Heb. *And said:* the copulative for the relative; as c. 17.6. & 23.4.

*{for we have treasures in the field, of wheat and of barley, and of oil, and of honey.}* Or, *stores,* or *store-houses:* as the like word for notion is used, Chapter 38.7. See there, and 1 Chron. 27.25. a place herein parallel to this: for we are not to conceive that they had any grain at all at that time abroad in the fields their harvest being some months past over: See Chapter 40.10. But their meaning must be, that such commodities they had in their country farms and storehouses: which they were willing to part with for the saving of their lives, Prov. 13.8. Howbeit, I cannot assent to that learned interpreter, who renders the words, *we have treasures hidden in a certain field:* as if it were a speech parallel to that of our Savior, Matth. 13.44. for however the term here used spring from a root that signifies *to hide,* and *treasures* are said sometime *to be hidden,* Esay 45.3. yet the word in general signifies *treasures,* or *stores,* whether hidden or other, Gen. 43.23. nor is it probable that such stores as these of so many sorts, should be hidden under ground in some one part of a field; and much less that all ten should so bestow their stores in any one place.

*{So he forbare}* Heb. *and;* as c. 39.13.

*{and slew them not among their brethren}* Or, *with.* Heb. *in the midst of* (as chap. 39.14. verse 3.) *their brethren,* or *country men;* as Deut. 17.15.

**Verse 9.** *{Now the pit}* Heb. *And;* as Chapter 40.5,7. and so verse 13.

*{wherein Ishmael had cast all the dead bodies of the men, whom he had slain because of Gedaliah}* To conceal his murders, both of Gedaliah, and those other, whom either together with him, ver. 3. or by this occasion afterward, he had dispatched and made away. Heb. *whom he smote* (as v. 3.) *at,* or, *by the hand:* which is variously expounded: for some of the Jewish masters expound it, as the word in its proper and most familiar notion is wont to import, *by the hand of Gedaliah:* as it is said, *they fell by the hand of David and his servants,* 2 Samuel 23.22. and they are said, say they, to be slain *by the hand of Gedaliah;* because he slighted the advice that Captain John gave him, whereby their death and his own also might have been prevented. But this seeming somewhat too far fetched, others of them give other interpretations: Either, *by occasion of Gedaliah;* for they came chiefly to kill him; and by occasion thereof did the like to them finding them with him: as, *thou hast consumed us by the hand* (that is, *by occasion,* or *because*) *of our iniquities,* Esay 64.7. or, *in Gedaliah,* that is, *in the place,* where Gedaliah was: to wit, at Mizpah: the word being used sometimes for *a place* or *quarter:* as Deut. 23.12. Esay 56.11. Chapter 6.3. See there. Others again render it, *in the hand of Gedaliah;* that is, *in his service: hand,* for *service* or *ministry:* as *by the hand of Moses;* that is, by his ministry, Numbers 4.37. Psalm 77.20. and so also, 2 Chron. 36.15. Mal. 1.1. Others, *by the side of Gedaliah;* as, *I will stand at the hand* (that is, *by the side*) *of my father,* 1 Samuel 19.3. and *by the hand of them;* that is, *beside them* Neh. 3.4,5. such as were about him, or attending upon him: as 1 Chron. 18.17. and others, *in the hand of Gedaliah;* that is, *under his charge:* as *all his masters goods were in his hand;* that is, *under his charge,* in his custody, Genesis 24.10. and *these were in the hand of Ithamar,* for, *under his charge,* Numbers 4.33. but the meaning of the form of speech, as it is here used, is plain enough, intending no more than simply, *with Gedaliah, the men that he slew with him:* Nor need we go far for the interpretation of it: we had it before twice, chapter 38.10. *take thirty men in thine hand:* and *he took thirty men in his hand;* that is, *take them with thee:* and *he tooke them with him;* as it is there well rendered: and why it should not be likewise here, I see not: for it was before said, *with him,* v. 3. yet so to be restrained, as was there observed.

*{was it, which Asa the King had made for fear of Baasha King of Israel}* Or *which Asa the King made because of Baasha:* for the term here used imports no more: and is well so rendered, verse 18. See on chapter 17.11. How Asa fortified Mizpah, being a frontier town between him and Baasha, with the stones and timber, that he fetched away from Ramah, we read, 1 Kings 15.22. but of the pit here mentioned, we find nothing elsewhere; some suppose it to have been a trench or ditch, dug without the walls of the city. But this seems rather to have been some pit delved within the city near to which he drew on those 80. the greatest part whereof he slew, before he massacred them, the pit being ready at hand to receive them: but for what end or use it was at first contrived, whether to receive and contain water for necessary uses, upon occasion of a siege Esay 22.9,11. or for what other employment does not appear, nor can easily be determined: *deep and large* it seems it was as the prophet says of Tophet, Esay 30.33. that could contain so many corpses.

*{and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah filled it with them that were slain.}* With the bodies of them; which were therefore no small number.

**Verse 10.** *{Then Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people that were in Mizpah,}* Having out of all parts resorted thither to Gedaliah, c. 40.11,12.

*{even the Kings daughters}* Whom the Chaldeans had left behind; either being not much regarded by them when they were possessed of his sons; or being by some means otherwise concealed, and so escaping at the surprisal of the city. See Chapter 38.23. and 39.6.

*{and all the people that remained in Mizpah, which Nebuzaradan the Captain of the Guard had committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam,}* 2 Kings 25.12,22. Chapter, 39.10. and 40.5.

*{and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah carried them away captive; and departed to go over to the Ammonites:}* By whose king he had been set on work to do what he did, Chapter, 40.14.

**Verse 11.** *{But when Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the Captains of the forces that were with him, heard of all the evil that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had done,}*

**Verse 12.** *{Then they took all the men, and went to fight with Ishmael the son of Nethaniah;}* Heb. *And they heard—and they took,* as c. 40.7,8. *all the men;* to wit, that were then with them, or that they could get together.

*{and they found them by the great waters that are in Gibeon.}* The great pool of Gibeon (whereof 2 Sam. 2.13.) lying in the way from Mizpah to the Ammonites' country.

**Verse 3.** *{Now it came to pass that when all the people which were with Ishmael, saw Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the Captains of the forces that were with him, then they were glad.}* Heb. *And it was;* as verse 1. and, *and they were glad,* for *that they were glad;* as verse 5.

**Verse 14.** *{So all the people that Ishmael had carried away captive from Mizpah, cast about, and returned, and went unto Johanan the son of Kareah}* Heb. *And.* as v. 8. *cast about,* or *came about:* or *wheeled about;* as Eccl. 1.6.

**Verse 15.** *{But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men, and went to the Ammonites.}* Heb. *the sons,* of *Ammon.* See Chapter 40.14. Some render it, *For Ishmael escaped:* to wit, by flight; not staying, or daring to make head against the party that pursued him, which gave the people opportunity to go unto John. So is the copulative used c. 38.23.

**Verse 16.** *{Then took Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the Captains of the forces that were with him, all the remnant of the people whom he had recovered from Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah, (after that he had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam) even the mighty men of war, and the women and the children, and the Eunuchs, whom he had brought again from Gibeon:}* *from Mizpah,* that is, carried away *from Mizpah;* to wit, formerly by Ishmael, vers. 10. Heb. *smote,* for *slain;* as vers. 2. and *men,* simply, not *mighty men,* distinguished only from *the women,* as chap. 43.6. and, *child,* for *children;* as chap. 40.7.

**Verse 17.** *{And they departed, and dwelt in the habitation of Chimham, which is by Bethlehem;}* Some portion of land, that either David out of his own patrimony, or Solomon his son after him, who upon his deathbed gave him a special charge concerning him, 1 Kings 2.7.) had in likelihood conferred upon Chimham the son of Barzillai; for the kindness showed him by his father, when he fled from Absolom, See 2 Samuel 19.38.) which though at the year of release, Ezek. 46.17. it returned again to the crown; yet may seem still from thence to have borne that name: places oftentimes retaining the names of those many ages after, who had formerly held and enjoyed them, Psal. 49.11.

*{to go to enter into Egypt}* Their wonted place of refuge, Esay 30.1. & 31.1.

**Verse 18.** *{Because of the Chaldeans:}* Heb. *From the face of the Chaldeans;* as verse 9. and these words would better have been joined to the last clause of the verse before-going; as some other in like manner, Chapter, 50.13. for there is not the same reason of disjoining these here as there might be, Psalm 96.12,13. and 98.8,9.

*{for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the King of Babylon made Governor in the land.}* They feared that the Chaldeans would send in some forces upon them, to revenge the murder of Gedaliah, and the Chaldeans, that were slain together with him. See verse 3.

## CHAPTER 42

**Verse 1.** *{Then all the Captains of the Forces,}* In this chapter is related a motion, by the captains, that had put Ishmael and his accomplices to flight, rescued the people from them, whom they were carrying away toward the Ammonites, and had a purpose to transport them another way into Egypt, c. 41.17. made unto Jeremy, requesting him from God to advise them concerning their journey, v. 1—6. together with the answer returned unto them from God by the prophet; withal taxing them for their deep hypocrisy, and dissembling both with God and him, verse 7—22.

*{and Johanan the son of Kareah,}* Or, *even John.* As Chapter, 40.18. He especially among the rest: As *the servants of David, and Asabel,* 2 Samuel, 2.30. and, *Say to his Disciples, and to Peter,* Mark 16.7. See *Judah and Jerusalem,* Esay 1.1.

*{and Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah,}* See Chap. 43.1.

*{and all the people from the least, even unto the greatest:}* Of this form of speech, see on c. 6.13. & 31.34.

*{drew near.}* A term commonly used of addresses unto any by way of suit for relief, or advice, Genesis, 43.19. Numbers 36.1.

**V. 2.** *{And said unto Jeremiah the Prophet, Let, we beseech thee, our supplication be accepted before thee,}* Heb. *fall before;* as chapter 37.20. See v. 9. A learned Writer renders it, *fall thou down in prayer before God for us:* but this is to confound it groundlessly with that which follows: this form intimates their submiss seeking to him; the next branch his seeking to God for them, the subject matter of their suit.

*{and pray for us unto the LORD thy God,}* Whom you have special relation unto, as his Prophet. So they to Samuel, 1 Samuel, 12.19.

*{even for all this remnant, (for we are left but a few of many, as thine eyes doe behold us.)}* That was fulfilled which had been long ago foretold and menaced, Leviticus 26.22. Deuteronomy 28.62.

**V. 3.** *{That the LORD thy God may shew us the way wherein we may walke, and the thing that we may do.}* Heb. *And the Lord;* as Mal. 1.9. and, *way that we shall walk,* or *go,* for *should go:* as Psalm 25.12. and 143.8. and, *the word,* (as chap. 40.16.) *that we shall do:* as 2 Chronicles 20.12. They would have the Prophet tell them from God what they should do; when as they (the leaders of them, at least) were resolved what they would do already, chapter 41.17.

**V. 4.** *{Then Jeremiah the Prophet said unto them, I have heard you;}* I am willing to grant your request; so hearing is commonly taken in Scripture, Psalm 6.9. & 20.1. a defect of the Pronoun; as Esay 1.15.

*{behold, I will pray unto the LORD your God,}* As well as mine; having taken you to be his people, 1 Sam. 12.22.

*{according to your words}* According to what you propounded to me. So Gen. 44.10. Josh. 2.21.

*{and it shall come to passe that whatsoever thing the LORD shall answer you, I will declare it unto you;}* Heb. *and it shall be;* as chap. 30.8. and, *every word,* for *every thing,* or *whatsoever;* as chap. 44.17. So verse 5.

*{I will keep nothing back from you.}* Heb. *not a word:* as c. 26.2. and 38.14. So Paul, Act 20.20.

**V. 5.** *{Then they said to Jeremiah,}* Heb. *And.* and so also verse 4,8.

*{The LORD be a true and faithful witness between us,}* Gods special attribute in an eminency, Rev. 3.14. Heb. *a witness of truth:* as Proverbs 14.5,25. Thus in deep hypocrisy abuse they Gods Name, and take it in vain, calling him for a true and faithful witness, when as mean while they intended nothing less, than what so solemnly they professed and pretended, v. 20.

*{if we doe not even according to all things, for the which the LORD thy God shall send thee to us.}* Heb. *according to every word;* as verse 4.

**V. 6.** *{Whether it be good, or whether it be evil,}* Seem it never so disadvantageous, or dangerous to us. See Micajahs sound and sincere resolution, 1 King. 22.8,18. not counterfeit, as these mens. Heb. *if good and if evil:* as Eccl. 11.3.

*{we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we send thee,}* Heb. *hearken unto:* as c. 38.20. and so after again. See the peoples like profession to Moses, Deut 5.27,29.

*{that it may be well with us, when we obey the voice of the LORD our God}* As Deut 6.3.

**V. 7.** *{And it came to pass after ten days, that the word of the LORD came unto Jeremiah.}* Here comes to be related at length (after all this long discourse, or narrative inserted, to make way thereunto) that Word of the Lord before pointed unto, and intended, Chapter 40.1. Heb. *and it was* (as chapter 36.1.) *from the end of ten days,* (as chap. 34.14.) *and* (as chap. 41.14.) *the Word of the Lord was to Jeremy:* as chap. 34.1. Because it is said, *after ten days,* some hence gather, that the Prophet spent all those ten days in Prayer: But that is not necessary. The Prophet having seriously and solemnly commended it by prayer to God, was to expect when God would please to return to him, and to them by him, an answer. The reason, why God thus delayed it, being not revealed, is not easily conjectured, much less, can it be certainly determined. Some say, to add the more weight to the Oracle, when it should be delivered: and to free the Prophet from suspicion, of speaking from himself, which might have been at least, if not misdeemed, yet amiss pretended, had he suddenly returned an answer. I conceive, it might rather be to punish their hypocrisy, by holding them in suspense, who were questionless impatient of delay, having beforehand resolved what they would do, whatsoever the answer should be.

**V. 8.** *{Then called he Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the Captains of the forces which were with him, and all the people, from the least, even to the greatest:}* No sooner had the Prophet his answer and errand from God, but he calls them all to come and hear it; because all had requested it, and all were concerned in it. See v. 1.

**V. 9.** *{And said unto them; Thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel, unto whom ye sent me to present your supplication before him;}* Heb. *to make your supplication fall before him,* or *in his presence;* as chap. 38.27. Dan. 9.18,20. See verse 2. the like style given to God: see ch. 37.7.

**V. 10.** *{If ye will stay in this land, then will I build you, and not pull you down; and I will plant you, and not pluck you up:}* Heb. *sitting, sit,* or *staying stay;* as 1 Samuel 20.5. So verse 13. I will settle you, and prosper you, As chapter, 24.6. See the contrary, Psalm 28.5.

*{for I repent me of the evil that I have done unto you.}* I will no longer deal roughly and harshly with you, as of late I have done. Of this *repentance* in God: See Chapter 18.8. So Psalm 106.45.

**V. 11.** *{Be not afraid of the King of Babylon, of whom ye are afraid: be not afraid of him, saith the LORD:}* See the like encouragements, Esay 43.13. and 44.2. an emphatical ingemination; not unlike that, Esay, 8.12,13. and Luk 12.4,5.

*{for I am with you, to save you, and to deliver you from his hand.}* Gods assistance, a shelter all-sufficient, Esay 41.10,13,14. & 43.2,5. c. 1.19 & 15.20.

**V. 12.** *{And I will shew mercies unto you, that he may have mercy upon you,}* Heb. *I will give you mercies,* or, *tender compassions:* As Genesis, 43.14. Deuteronomy 13.17. I will cause you to find favor in the sight of Nubuchadnezzar, as Psalm 106.46. and the hearts of all men, as well Kings, as other inferior ones, being in his hand to wind and turn which way he pleases Prov. 21.1. they needed not to fear man, if they were careful to please him, Prov. 16.7. Heb. *and he shall,* for, *that he may;* as Mal. 1.9. v. 3.

*{and cause you to return to your own land.}* To the several places of your former abode, from which you had formerly either fled, or been forced, c. 41.11,12.

**V. 13.** *{But if ye say, We will not dwell in this land, neither obey the voice of the LORD your God,}* Or, *and I will not obey;* for it has reference to, *if ye say.* Heb. *And.* As c. 41.15. and *sit,* or *stay,* as v. 10 and *hearken to,* as v. 6.

**V. 14.** *{Saying, No, but we will go into the land of Egypt wherein we shall see no wars,}* As v. 13. *see no war,* for, sustain it, suffer it: As c. 14.13.

*{nor hear the sound of the Trumpet,}* Either of the enemy joining battle, or of their own summoning and calling people together to prepare thereunto, c. 4.19,21.

*{nor have famine of bread;}* Which Egypt, watered yearly by Nilus, had usually good store of, and was wont from Alexandria to furnish with bread-corn divers parts of the Roman State. See Esay 23.

*{and there will we dwell}* Or, *stay,* or, *abide;* As verse 10.13. that is, says a learned Annotator, there shall we have a settled and fixed abode, and not be compelled to remove from place to place, at the pleasure of our Lords and Masters the Chaldeans; but the simple sense I conceive here to be the right,

**V. 15.** *{(And now therefore hear the Word of the LORD, ye remnant of Judah;)}* As chap. 10.1. but here prefixed, with repetition, by the way inserted, to give the stronger assurance, and make the deeper impression of what was to ensue, and was like to relish ill with them.

*{Thus saith the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel,}* As Chapter 35.13.

*{if ye wholly set your faces}* Or, if you set yourselves obstinately Heb. *setting set your faces:* to *set the face toward a place,* is sometime used for to look wistly towards it; as Ezekiel 20.46. & 21.2. sometime for to bend, resolve and prepare for a journey that way, as Dan. 11.17,18. Luke 9.51.

*{to enter into Egypt, and go to sojourn there:)}* Which yet is by some here deemed to have been offensive, not so much in regard of that general prohibition in the Law, Deut. 17.15. as in regard of Gods special Will at present made known unto them, and a particular injunction to the contrary now given them, to stay in the land, v. 10. and so continue under the Babylonian government, unto which God would have them to be subject, Chapter 25.6,11,12.

**V. 16.** *{Then shall it come to pass, that the sword which ye feared shall overtake you there in the land of Egypt; and the famine whereof ye were afraid shall follow close after you in Egypt, and there ye shall die}* Heb. *And it shall be;* as v. 4. and *cleave after you,* for, *follow you closely;* as Psal. 63.8. Thus what the wicked fear, and by indirect courses seek to shun, by those means befalls them, by which they think to shift off and escape it, Prov. 10.24. Esay 66.4. c. 38.19,22 Ezek. 11.8. For fear of the Chaldeans they would needs go into Egypt, c. 41.21,22. making full account that they should be safe enough from them, were they but once there; and thither God sends after them the Chaldean sword, that destroys both the Egyptians and them, c. 43.11. and 44.27,30. & 46.13,25.

**V. 17.** *{So it shall be with all the men that set their faces to go into Egypt to sojourn there,}* Heb. *And* (for, *So* as Proverbs 17.3.) *all the men shall be that set their faces;* as verse 15 chap. 44.12. that voluntarily and obstinately, contrary to Gods command, bend themselves that way; not those that with the rest are carried away by constraint, as was the Prophet himself among others, and Baruc his scribe. c. 43.5,6.

*{they shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence}* As chap. 21.7. & 24.10. & 28.8. See c. 44.12.

*{and none of them shall escape or remain from the evil that I will bring upon them.}* See c. 44.14.

**Verse 18.** *{For thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel,}* As before, verse 9.

*{As mine anger and my fury hath been poured forth upon the Inhabitants of Jerusalem; so shall my fury be poured forth upon you, when ye enter into Egypt:}* Or, *when ye are come into Egypt:* As Numbers 15.18. the place where you think yourselves secure, were you once got thither. See Chapter 43.7. and 44.6. and of the form of speech, concerning wrath poured out, Chapter 10.24.

*{and ye shall be an execration, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach;}* As c. 24.9. See c. 44.12.

*{and ye shall see this place no more.}* There shall none of you return, as those shall that were carried hence unto Babylon, chapter 24.6. and 31.17.

**Verse 19.** *{The LORD hath said concerning you}* Or, *Thus;* or, *These things the Lord hath said.*

*{O ye remnant of Judah,}* As v. 15. c. 43.5.

*{Go ye not into Egypt;}* Or, as some render it, Therefore go not into Egypt.

*{know certainly that I have admonished you this day.}* Heb. *knowing know* (as Gen. 11.13.) *that I have,* or *that I do, this day testifie against you;* as Deut. 4.20.

**Verse 20.** *{For ye dissembled in your hearts,}* Or, *That* (as chap. 4.18.) *ye dissembled;* as knitting this unto that which went before, *I testifie against you;* or, *Certainly ye dissembled;* for so is the particle also used; as chap. 22.22. and 24.8. Heb. *ye seduced in your souls,* or *in your minds;* as Gen. 23.8. Prov. 23.7. or, as others, *against your souls;* as 1 King. 2.23. Proverbs 7.23. you sought to beguile God, or to deceive me, speaking one thing with your mouths, and minding inwardly another: for you have dealt thus deceitfully to your own evil and mischief. A learned scholar renders it, *Ye have seduced yourselves;* or *made an error in your souls.* And the old Latin much to the same effect, *you deceived your souls:* somewhat the like form of speech, is found in a term used, James 1.26. but the former seems somewhat harsh here: the latter takes no notice of the particle, which seems not here vacant. I should rather render it, with a late learned annotator, *Surely ye deceived me against your own souls,* or *yourselves,* me, wanting, as Esay 29.6. chapter 15.16.

*{when ye sent mee unto the LORD your God, saying, Pray for us unto the LORD our God, and according unto all that the LORD our God shall say, so declare unto us, and wee will do it.}* As v. 2,3,5,6.

**Verse 21.** *{And now I have this day declared it to you; but ye have not obeyed the voice of the LORD your God, nor any thing for the which he sent mee unto you.}* Or, *And when I have this day declared it to you, ye do not hearken to the voyce of the Lord your God* (as ver. 13.) *or unto ought* (*and,* as ver. 6. *to all;* as chap. 32.23.) *with which he sent me to you.* Yet had they not returned any answer to the Prophet's speech: but the Prophet knew well enough how it was with them, either having discovered it by their carriage during the ten days intervenient between their motion and God's answer vers. 7. or by their demeanor while he was delivering God's message: or (which is most probable) he might have it by revelation from God: as some other particulars concerning himself, c. 11.18,19. The like syntax, see c. 40.7,8.

**Verse 22.** *{Now therefore know certainly,}* Heb. *And* (as chap. 36.6.) *knowing, know;* as v. 19.

*{that ye shall die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence in that place whither ye desire to go, and to sojourn.}* Or, *to go to sojourn;* As Genesis 12.10. verse 15.7. In Egypt where you least expect it. See verse 16,17,18.

## CHAPTER 43

**Verse 1.** *{And it came to passe, that when Jeremiah had made an end of speaking unto all the people, all the words of the LORD their God, for which the LORD their God had sent him to them, even all these words;}* Or, *things:* as chap. 36.13,32. In this chapter is recorded what effect the message from God before related, had with those men it was sent to; to wit, their refusal to obey it, persistence in their former resolution for Egypt, and accomplishment thereof, v. 1–7. together with a new prophecy delivered by Jeremy in Egypt, after they were come thither, v. 8–13.

**Verse 2.** *{then spake Azariah the son of Hoshaiah,}* This is deemed by most to have been no other than that Jezaniah, mentioned c. 42.1. Yet it might be another, and a brother of his, because the father seems the same; and some suppose him the first mover of the journey into Egypt.

*{and Johanan the son of Kareah,}* Or, *John;* As Chapter 40.8. and 42.1.

*{and all the proud men}* Among whom, those were the chief ones, and it might well therefore be rendered, *and the rest of the proud men;* as chap. 40.13. So v. 14. chap. 52.18. Pride being the ordinary and most common cause of disobedience and rebellion against God; and of the contempt of his messengers, and messages see Exod. 5.2.

*{saying unto Jeremiah, thou speakest falsely,}* Heb. *falshood,* or *a lye:* as c. 40.16.

*{The LORD our God hath not sent thee to say, Go not into Egypt to sojourn there.}* Thus discovered hypocrisy turns into outrage and fury. So they, c. 5.13. *The Word of God is not in them.*

**Verse 3.** *{But Baruch the son of Neriah setteth thee on against us,}* They are not content to traduce and slander the Prophet, but Baruc also for him. The reason that a learned man renders, why they should cast this aspersion upon Baruc, to wit, because he being a younger man, should be more hot and eager than the Prophet in the delivery of these things, is groundless; nor seems probable: nor could he be lightly more eager than Jeremy himself was in the delivery of it, had he been to do it; nor is it likely that Jeremy made any use of him therein.

*{for to deliver us into the hand of the Chaldeans, that they might put us to death, and carry us away captive into Babylon.}* To slay some of us, and to transport the rest. See the like, Esay 10.4. and v. 12. and what should Baruc gain by this? But any pretense is colorable enough, where men are maliciously minded. Heb. *to give us into the hand,* or *power:* as c. 34.20.

**Verse 4.** *{So Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the Captains of the forces, and all the people obeyed not the voice of the LORD, to dwell in the land of Judah.}* Heb. *And Johanan:* as c. 41.14. and, *all the captains* (or *the rest of them;* as v. 2.) *hearkned not:* as c. 42.14. and, to sit, or, abide: as c. 42.10,13.

**Verse 5.** *{But Johanan the son of Kareah, and the Captains of the forces, took all the remnant of Judah, that were returned from all nations, whither they had been driven to dwell in the land of Judah,}* Heb. *And,* as c. 42.1. and, *all,* for the rest: and *to sit,* for to abide; as v. 4. See c. 40.11.

**Verse 6.** *{Even the men, and women, and children, and the Kings daughters, and every person that Nebuzaradan the Captain of the guard had left with Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan,}* See chap. 40.7. & 41.10,16. Heb. *every soul*; as chap. 52.10. Romans 13.1.

*{and Jeremiah the Prophet, and Baruc the son of Neriah.}* Whom by force they led away with them; and some other also in likelihood beside them.

**Verse 7.** *{So they came into the land of Egypt;}* Heb. *And:* as verse 4. See c. 42.18.

*{for they obeyed not the voice of the LORD:}* As Chapter 42.21. verse 4.

*{thus came they even to Taphpanhes.}* Heb. *and they came unto Tahphanhes,* or *Tachpanches.* An ancient city of Egypt, so called from a queen of that name, 1 Kings 11.19. The ancient Greek version terms it *Taphna.* Whence the later Greeks, corrupting the term, and framing it nearer to their own language, as if it had its original with them from a word that signifies a laurel, or bay-tree, call it commonly *Daphna,* and *Daphnæ Pelusiacæ,* to distinguish it from another *Daphnæ* in Syria. See Esay 30.4. where it is termed in a more contracted form *Hanes,* or *Chanes.*

**Verse 8.** *{Then came the Word of the LORD unto Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, saying,}* Heb. *And the word was;* as c. 36.27.

**Verse 9.** *{take great stones in thine hand, and hide them in the clay in the brickkiln, which is at the entry of Pharaoh's house in Tahpanhes, in the sight of the men of Judah:}* By this visible sign would God have confirmed, and as by an ocular demonstration set before the eyes of this refractory and rebellious people, the accomplishment of that judgment which before he had denounced against them, by the access of Nebuchadnezzar with his forces into Egypt, and by his pursuance of them among others there, from whose force they thither fled.

*{in the clay in the brickkiln}* By the former word here used, though nowhere else found, is by the Jewish doctors, and most others, agreed to be meant such material, as brick is wont to be made of; and that by the latter word is meant such a furnace, or place, as brick is wont to be framed and burnt in, is no less agreed on from 2 Samuel 12.31. Howbeit, because some Greek versions render the former word, an hidden place, and the old Latin, the former, *a Grot,* or, *Cave,* or, *Vault;* and the latter, a brick-wall: grounding in likelihood, on a place in Nah. 3.14. hence some make much ado to find out some trench or ditch near the king's palace, whereunto Jeremy should cast these stones; on which, as part of the foundation, Nebuchadnezzar, when he came into Egypt, should raise a brick wall, and build him a palace there. But little reason have we for such far-fetched fancies to recede from the received interpretation of the words: the main matter that some object is, that there is no likelihood, that a brick-kiln should be situate so near to the king's palace, which could not but be, by occasion of the noisome smoke thereof very offensive. To which may be answered: First, that the houses of these Egyptian kings were many of them of vast amplitude; and the brick-kilns therefore, though they were situate not far from some of these court gates, yet might be far enough distant from those parts of the palace, wherein the king and his great ones, did ordinarily keep. Secondly, that this place might be rather a work-house to frame some special kind of brick in for peculiar uses, than a furnace or kiln to burn them; and that such, as were either to be burnt elsewhere, or to be hardened only with the sun: and lastly, that the word rendered entry, does not always signify a door, or, a porch, but an opening, or, open way, that leads to a place, house, town, or city. So it is used, chap. 1.15. and so rendered, Gen. 38.14. and may well therefore also here so signify: as also that the particle here rendered, *in,* is used also for, *besides,* See Chap. 32.7. & 36.10. and the words may therefore be well here rendered, *beside the open way to Pharaoh's house.*

**Verse 10.** *{And say unto them, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel,}* As chap. 42.15.

*{Behold, I will send and take Nebuchadrezzar the King of Babylon my Servant,}* As he is also styled, chap. 25.9. Heb. *Lo I am sending.* So also chap. 25.9.

*{and will set his throne upon these stones that I have hid, and he shall spread his royal pavilion over them.}* Thereby implying that Nebuchadnezzar should proceed so far in the conquest of Egypt, as to pitch his pavilion in that very place, not far distant from the king's palace at *Tanes;* where his brick houses erected for his building then stood: the word rendered pavilion, so termed for the beautifulness of it, (for the term royal is not in the text) is nowhere else found.

**Verse 11.** *{And when he cometh he shall smite the land of Egypt: and deliver such as are for death to death, and such as are for captivity to captivity; and such as are for the sword to the sword}* Heb. *And he shall come, and he shall smite* (the like to that, chap. 42.21.) *the land of Egypt,* (that is, the inhabitants of the land; as Mal. 4.6.) *those that are for death, to death;* etc. to smite, for, to smite and give, or deliver up, or by giving and delivering up, to death. A complexive form of speech, like those Esay 38.14,17,21. chap. 36.23. & 41.7. See of this distribution of judgments, compared with chap. 42.17. on chap. 15.2. See also Zach. 11.2.

**Verse 12.** *{And I will kindle a fire}* As chap. 17.27.

*{in the houses of the gods of Egypt}* I will cause him to set their idol-temples on fire, and burn them down; that I may execute judgment as well on their gods, as on themselves. So Exod. 12.12. Esay 19.1. Chap. 46.25. Ezek. 30.13.

*{and he shall burn them; and carry them away captive,}* Some of their idols, being of wood or other like combustible matter, he shall burn: others of them, being of more rich and sumptuous materials, he shall carry away among other spoils, to employ otherwise, or to reserve in token of conquest. See Esay 46.2. chap. 48.7. and of this form of speech, on verse 3.

*{and he shall array himself with the land of Egypt, as a shepherd putteth on his garment,}* The meaning in general of this passage is agreed on, to wit, that by *the land of Egypt* is here meant the spoils of that country, which the Chaldean should gather together, and go away enriched with them: but about application of it to a shepherd's wonted guise, there is some variety of opinion. One of the Jewish masters would by the garment here mentioned have understood the cloth, that the shepherd sets up for a tent, to shelter him, while he stays in some one place, but takes down again and carries away with him, leaving nothing behind him, when he removes to some other place; as they use oft to shift, Esay 13.20. and so should the king of Babylon go from place to place in Egypt; and sweep all away with him. But this conceit needlessly forces the term and so the text: and some of ours therefore instead of his tent substituting his coat, go the same way, but keep closer to the term in the text. Another will have it allude to a shepherd's wrapping himself up in his garment to keep himself warm, because in the wilderness he is to tend his flock as well by night as by day, Gen. 31.40. 1 Sam. 25.16. Luke 2.8. which some of ours also follow. But other of ours refer it to the shepherds going forth in the morning to lead his sheep out to their pasture. (see Esay 40.11. Chap. 31.9. Josh. 10.3,4.) who is not wont to spend much time in arraying and dressing himself up, before he go out but casts on his coat suddenly, and is by and by gone: and so should Nebuchadnezzar, without difficulty or long delay, as speedily and easily, seize on the wealth of Egypt, and go away with it. And others again, to his returning home at evening, when having sat all the heat of the day without his coat, or upper garment, (as the word seems properly to signify, Gen. 9.22.) while he tended his sheep in those hot regions, he casts it on about him at evening, at such time as he goes homeward. and in like manner should Nebuchadnezzar return at his leaving of Egypt, not naked or bare, (as men are said to be, when they want their upper garment. See Esay 20.1.) but well clad, as with his coat, or upper garment about him. And this seems best to agree both with the drift of the Prophet, and the terms of the text. For as for that of the ancient Greek interpreter, whom a learned writer supposes to have read *chatah,* for *atah:* and renders it, he shall purge Egypt as a shepherd purges his coat of lice. Which some expound, he shall at leisure ransack all Egypt, and seize on all her wealth and treasure; as shepherds are wont leisurely to look their clothes, and pick out their lice: it is but a lousy interpretation (howsoever some seem to be much taken with it) grounded upon a corruption of the text: and I therefore leave it.

*{and he shall go forth from thence in peace.}* Or; depart (as Chap. 29.2.) *from thence in peace;* that is, *in safety,* without hurt or loss. as 2 Sam. 3.22,23. 1 Kings 22.27,28. or, quietly; the Egyptians not daring nor being able to stir, or to impeach him in his passage. So Exod. 11.7. Psal. 78.53. See the like, Esay 10.14. or, securely, says a learned writer, as a shepherd that having cast on his coat, does not fear in his return to be robbed or stripped of it, before he get home. See the like prophecy of Nebuchadnezzar's conquest of Egypt, Ezek. 29.19,20. & 30.19.

**Verse 13.** *{He shall break also the images,}* Heb. *And* (as Chap. 1.3.) *he shall break* (to shivers; for thence seems our English word shiver to have come) *the statues,* or, standing images. So the word properly signifies, Mic. 5.13.

*{of Bethshemesh}* A prime city of Egypt, with them called anciently, *On,* Gen. 41.45. the word signifies *the house of the sun;* and it was famous for idolatry, in regard of a stately temple, wherein the sun was there worshipped, whereof Herodote, lib. 2. See Esay 19.18.

*{that is, in the land of Egypt:}* This is added to distinguish it from another city of the same name in Hebrew, situate in the land of Judah, Josh. 15.10. 1 Sam. 6.12.

*{and in the houses of the gods of the Egyptians shall he burn with fire.}* The same in effect that was said before, Verse 12. save that God is said to kindle this fire there, and Nebuchadnezzar is said to burn them with it here; who was therefore no other than God's instrument in this act; as Sennacherib before him in other the like, Esay 10.5,6,15. & 37.18,19.

## CHAPTER 44

**Verse 1.** *{The word that came to Jeremiah,}* In this chapter is contained, 1. A second sermon or message, brought from God by the Prophet, reproving and menacing the Jewish people in Egypt, not so much now for their disobedience in leaving their own land, and journeying into Egypt, contrary to God's express command; as for that gross and abominable idolatry that they committed, when they had seated themselves in several parts of that land, Verse 1–14. 2. The refractory carriage of the people upon the delivery of it, expressly refusing to give any heed unto it, and professing a stiff resolution to persist in their idolatrous practices, Verse 15–19. 3. The Prophet's reply upon this their peremptory answer, Verse 20–23. 4. A new message with the like menaces to the former, ratified by a solemn oath, with reserve of a few that should survive to see the accomplishment of it, Verse 24–28. and confirmed by a sign that should be made good upon the person of the king of Egypt, under whose protection they there were, verse 29,30.

*{The word that came,}* Heb. *that was:* as Chap. 1.2. to wit, *from the Lord;* as Chap. 40.1.

*{concerning all the Jews,}* Heb. *unto*. the same particle that was before: it came to him, to be delivered to them, as Rev. 1.1. *which God gave to him to shew to his Servants.* Howbeit, the word is sometime used for concerning; as Chap. 22.11,18. & 27.19. and so may not amiss be rendered also here.

*{which dwell in the land of Egypt.}* Or, *that were residing*. Heb. *sitting*: and so again in the next words. See Chapter 42.10,13.

*{which dwell at Migdol}* A strong city, or fort, situate in the territory of Bethshemesh, not far from the Red Sea, Exod. 14.2. Numb. 33.7,8. But no hold or fort so strong that can secure or shelter against God, Esay 31.9. & 37.37,38.

*{and at Tahpanhes}* Of this, see chap. 43.7.

*{and at Noph}* Otherwise Moph, Hos. 9.6. and thence with the Greeks and Latins Memphis. See Esay 19.13. Ezek. 30.13.

*{and in the country of Pathros, saying,}* Another region in Egypt, that had its name from one of Mitsraim's issue, Gen. 10.14. supposed by some learned to be that which is commonly termed, Thebais; which they conjecture, partly, from some terms, though corrupted, of places therein situate, as the Phaturite canton in Pliny, and Pathyris a town in Ptolemy; and partly, from the situation of it; which from hence they gather to have been higher, and farther up into the country than Noph, or, Memphis; as Noph, or Memphis than Migdol, or, Magdolus; as the Greeks and Latins term it. Of it, see also on Esay 11.11. It is mentioned also, Ezek. 29.14. & 30.14.

**Verse 2.** *{Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel,}* As Chap. 43.10.

*{ye have seen all the evils that I have brought upon Jerusalem, and upon the cities of Judah:}* That which might have served to warn you, and make you more wise and wary. So Deut. 4.3. See chap. 3.7,8,12. & 7.12. so Neh. 13.18. Dan. 5.22. Zach. 1.5,6.

*{and behold this day they are a desolation, and no man dwelleth therein.}* Desolation, for, extremely desolate; as Chap. 37.19. Ezek. 14.15. See chap. 47.7.9.

**Verse 3.** *{Because of their wickedness, which they have committed,}* Heb. *from before,* or; *from the face of,* So chap. 7.12. & 21.12. & 23.10.

*{to provoke me to anger}* See chap. 7.18.

*{in that they went to burn incense and to serve other gods, whom they knew not, neither they, you, nor your fathers.}* They went from me, and left me, to go after strange gods, and serve them, Chap. 19.4. neither *they, ye, nor your fathers.* Heb. *ye; and your fathers;* as chap. 35.6. neither *ye, nor your sons.* Heb. *ye and your sons.* See the like also. Chap. 36.24.

**Verse 4.** *{Howbeit, I sent unto you all my Servants the Prophets, rising early and sending them,}* So Chap. 7.25. & 25.3. & 26.5. & 29.19. & 32.33. Heb. *And I sent;* as chap. 35.14.

*{saying, oh do not this abominable thing that I hate.}* Heb. *this word of abomination: word,* for, *thing;* as chap. 40.3. and, *abomination,* for, *abominable,* as chap. 32.35.

**Verse 5.** *{But they hearkened not, nor inclined their ear to turn from their wickedness,}* See chap. 7.24,25. & 11.8. & 34.14.

*{to burn no incense unto other gods.}* Or, rather, *in burning;* as chap. 35.8,9. & 38.4. so it is well rendered, verse 8.

**Verse 6.** *{wherefore my fury, and mine anger was poured forth;}* Heb. *And.* as chap. 42.22. See chap. 42.18.

*{and was kindled in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem.}* Or, *and it burnt.* as Numb. 11.3.

*{and they are wasted and desolate,}* Or, *so that* (as Chap. 19.16.) *they are become waste and desolate.* Heb. *are unto wasteness and desolation.* as chap. 25.38.

*{as at this day.}* Or, *as this day* appears, as chap. 25.18.

**Verse 7.** *{Therefore now thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel;}* Heb. *And now.* as chap. 42.22. See chap. 35.17. & 42.15.

*{Wherefore commit ye this great evil against your souls?}* As Num. 16.38. Chap. 7.19.

*{to cut off from you man, and woman, child, and suckling out of Judah, to leave you none to remain.}* To urge the Lord in his fierce anger to make an utter riddance of yourselves, and all yours. See verse 11. Of the word rendered *child,* see chap. 6.11. & 9.21. Heb. *out of the midst of Judah;* as chap. 51.6. and, *to make no remnant to remain to you:* as Esay 1.9.

**Verse 8.** *{In that ye provoke me unto wrath with the works of your hands,}* Your idols, Chap. 25.6,7.

*{burning incense unto other gods}* Or, *in burning.* Heb. *to burn;* as verse 5. but see there.

*{in the land of Egypt, whither ye be gone to dwell}* Or, *whither ye are come* (as chap. 42.18. & 43.7. for there they now were) *to abide,* or, *reside.* Heb. *sit;* as chap. 42.10,13. verse 1.

*{that ye might cut yourselves off, and that ye might be a curse and reproach among all the nations of the earth.}* See chap. 42.18. See Esay 65.15.

**Verse 9.** *{Have ye forgotten the wickedness of your fathers, and the wickedness of the Kings of Judah, and the wickedness of their wives, and your own wickedness, and the wickedness of your wives, which they have committed in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?}* See the like expostulations, Neh. 13.18. Heb. *evils;* as verse 7. *evil.*

**Verse 10.** *{They are not humbled even unto this day, neither have they feared; nor walked in my Law, nor in my statutes that I set before you, and before your fathers.}* Or, *How they have not been humbled,* or, *Yet they have not been humbled.* Neither humbled by those afflictions, that for their sins have befallen them, nor been wrought thereby unto any sincere and serious compunctions of heart and contrition of spirit, for their sins the procuring causes thereof. 2 Chron. 36.12,13. Chap. 5.3. A change of the person, as if God disdaining to talk further with them, should turn his speech from them to the prophet, So chap. 7.26. Heb. *have been contrite;* as Esay 57.15. *and, that I gave before you;* as chap. 26.4.

**Verse 11.** *{Therefore thus saith the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel,}* As verse 2,

*{Behold, I will set my face against you, for evil, and to cut off all Judah}* God threatens to set his face against them purposely to do evil to them, Chap. 21.10, Amos 9.4. to cut them off, and destroy them, Lev. 20.5. Psal. 34.16. See verse 7. as they had obstinately set their faces to go into Egypt against his injunction to the contrary, chap. 42.15,19. verse 12. Thus God long beforehand menaced *to walk crosse,* or, *thwartingly* with them, when they should walk so with him, Lev. 26.27,28. See Esay 66.3,4.

**Verse 12.** *{And I will take the remnant of Judah that have set their faces to go into the land of Egypt to sojourn there,}* Or, *that did set their faces,* that fixed their resolution to go thither, or, *have set their faces to go;* that is, out of a fixed resolution did go, and are come thither. See Chap. 42.15. not those that were brought thither by constraint, as Jeremy and Baruc, Chap. 43.6.

*{and they shall all be consumed and fall, in the land of Egypt: they shall even be consumed by the sword, and by the famine: they shall die, from the least even unto the greatest, by the sword and by the famine:}* See chap. 42.17. but what was said, *shall die,* there, is said, *shall fall* here; because men fall to the ground, when they die. So chap. 6.15. & 8.12. *from the least to the greatest;* as Chap. 42.1,8.

*{and they shall be an execration, and an astonishment, and a curse, and a reproach;}* as verse 8. Chap. 24.9.

**Verse 13.** *{For I will punish them that dwell in the land of Egypt, as I have punished Jerusalem, by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence;}* Heb. *And* (as chap. 38.23.) *visit upon* (as chap. 11.22. & 12.21.) *those* (to wit, Jews) *that sit,* or reside in the land of Egypt; as verse 1. Of these judgments, see before chap. 14.22. & 15.2. & 38.2. & 42.17. See verse 6.

**Verse 14.** *{So that none of the remnant of Judah, which are gone into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, shall escape, or remain, that they should return into the land of Judah, to the which they have a desire to return to dwell there: for none shall return but such as shall escape.}* This passage is by divers diversely rendered. Some render it, *So that* (Heb. *And*) *there shall be none, that shall escape, and be left of the remnant of the Jewes that came into the land of Egypt to abide there;* besides *those that shall set their mind* (Heb. *lift up their soul;* as Hos. 4.8.) *to return into the land of Judah, to return,* I say, *to dwell there.* But how this version may be fitted to the words of the text, I conceive not: that, *besides,* is without ground forced into the text. Our former versions (save that of Geneva, which our last concurs with) *So that none of the remnant of Judah, which are gone to dwell in Egypt, shall be left to come again into the land of Judah, although they think to come thither again, and to dwell there.* But neither will the words of the text admit this; that *although,* finds no place in it. The ancient Greek goes much the same way that our last does. The old Latin a little otherwise; *And there shall be none, that shall escape, and be left of the residue of who went to sojourn in the land of the Jewes, Egypt, and to returne into the land of Judah, to which they lift up their souls* (that is, *hope,* or, *desire;* as chap. 22.27.) *to return to, and dwell there.* As if their going into Egypt, yet were joined, with a purpose not to abide forever there, but to sojourn there for a time, as Elimelec did in the land of Moab, Ruth 1.1,1. and the Shunamite with the Philistines, 2 Kings 8.2. and when opportunity should be, which they hoped after some space of time would be, to return back into their own country again: and this the words of the text may well bear. And these all agree in the version of the last clause, as ours here exhibits it: *for none shall returne, but such as shall escape,* or, *some that shall escape;* intimating, yet, that there should be a reserve of some, but very few. See verse 28. But a learned scholiast departing, in the connexion of this last clause, from all that went before him, thus exhibits it; *So that there shall none escape, or remain in the remnant of Judah, to those that came into Egypt to abide there, and to return into the land of Judah: for they lift up their minds* indeed *to return to dwell there; but they shall not return, save those that escape.* But how that *for* comes in here, I conceive not, and leave it therefore to the judgment of others. The old Latin seems to have kept closest to the terms of the text. Howbeit, I conceive that that which our version exhibits, may well stand, if one of the copulatives in the text, be deemed superfluous, as oft it is, Psal. 7.9. Job 23.21. Chap. 6.25. Jon. 1.1. so that, *and to return;* be rendered simply, *to return.* See chap. 22.27. That of some, *escaping,* some of the Jewish doctors expound of Jeremy and Baruch, whom out of their Talmudic chronicles they tell, that Nebuchadnezzar, at his conquest of Egypt, sent back again into Judea: but the words are indefinite; and whether they died or no, is uncertain.

**Verse 15.** *{Then all the men which knew that their wives had burnt incense unto other gods, and all the women that stood by, a great multitude, even all the people that dwelt in the land of Egypt in Pathros, answered Jeremiah, saying,}* Heb. *And all,* &c. as Chap. 43.8. The effect of the message delivered from God to them by the prophet here follows. And in this verse is a description of the parties that return a peremptory answer of refusal and disobedience to it; to wit, such as were themselves guilty of the crime charged upon them or that knew their wives so to be; by the great multitude of whom it appears how exceedingly this idolatrous practice had spread itself among them, as such evils are wont to do, 1 Cor. 5.6. 2 Tim. 2.17,18. Heb. 12.15. and the women seem to be the chief speakers in this peremptory answer. See verse 19.

**Verse 16.** *{As for the word which thou hast spoken unto us in the name of the LORD, we will not hearken unto thee}* Heb. *the word;* put absolutely: as the like, Esth. 6.7. Psal. 73.28. Luke 21.6. See the like peremptory answers, Chap. 6.16,17. and observe how they proceed from evil to worse, Chap. 9.3. At first, it was no word of God, that the prophet spoke, Chap. 43.2. Now though it be, yet they will not obey it: they were at defiance with God's messenger before; now, with God himself, and his message.

**Verse 17.** *{But we will certainly do whatsoever thing goeth forth out of our own mouth.}* Heb. *We will doing do* (as chap. 22.4.) *every word* (as chap. 43.4.) *hath gone forth from our mouth:* whatsoever we have resolved upon, and have spoken, or have by solemn vow engaged ourselves unto; as Judg. 11.36. Esth. 7.8. Lam. 3.38.

*{to burn incense}* Or, *in burning incense;* as the particle is frequently in this form used. See verse 5.

*{to the Queen of heaven,}* The sun, as some, much adored in Egypt, (see chap. 43.13. or, the moon, as others; or, *to the frame of heaven:* the stars in general. See chap. 7. verse 18.

*{or to pour out drink offerings unto her}* Or, *and in pouring out drink-offerings to it,* as before.

*{as we have done, we and our fathers, our Kings, and our Princes, in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem.}* Their first argument, or knot of arguments rather, why they would persist in their idolatrous services, taken from custom, and antiquity, the practice of their ancestors; authority, the usage of great ones, their rulers; and the generality, the exercise of it, in all places. See chap. 2.28. & 11.13. Just the Popish arguments for their superstitions at this day.

*{for then had we plenty of victuals and were well, and saw no evil.}* Heb. *and* (but the copulative is oft so used, as Esay 53.2. Chap. 38.23. verse 13.) *then* (to be supplied, that it may cohere with verse 18.) *we were satiated with bread* (we had our fill of it, as Prov. 20.13. & 28.19. & 30.22. Ezek. 16.49. *bread,* for, *victuals* in general; as 1 Kings 4.22. Neh. 5.18.) *and we were good* (that is, merry; we lived merrily: as, *good with wine,* that is, merry with it, 2 Sam. 13.28. Esth. 1.10. and, *a good heart,* for, *a merry,* or, *a cheerfull heart* Prov. 13.13,15. & 17.22.) *and we saw not evill;* felt none, suffered none, endured none, had no experience of any evil; as ch. 5.12. & 42.14. A second reason why they would not leave their wonted guises, from the plenty and prosperity they had enjoyed, while they used them, ascribing to their idols, and idolatrous services, the good things, that God bestowed upon them. See Acts 14.17. See of their proneness hereunto, Esay 48.5. and their practice herein Hos. 2.7,8. The usual argument of blind and sorry creatures, the ignorant Popish sort among us, What a merry time it was; and how cheap and plentiful all things were, before this new Gospel came in, when they had nothing but mass and matins.

**Verse 18.** *{But since we left off to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven, and poured out drink offerings unto her, we have wanted all things, and have been consumed by the sword, and by the famine.}* Heb. *And* (as verse 17.) *from then;* as Gen. 39.5. Ruth. 2.7. Thus profane and godless wretches measure religion by their belly; will serve God no longer than he feeds them to their fill; and satisfy their unlimited lusts: and prone to impute as their plenty when they enjoy it, to their idols, so their penury and scarcity when they are pinched with it, or any other calamity that befalls them, to their neglect, not of God, but of them.

**Verse 19.** *{And when we burnt incense to the Queen of Heaven; and poured out drink offerings unto her, did we make her cakes to worship her, and pour out drink offerings unto her without our men?}* Their *husbands,* they mean, as Gen. 3.16. whose approbation of what in this kind they did, it seems that they deemed warrant sufficient to bear them out in doing of it. And hence it appears, that the women here took upon them to answer the prophet, as well as the men, yea, may seem to have been the chief and forwardest in this bad business; as was Jezabel with Ahab; 1 Kings 21.25. See verse 24,26. Of the cakes here mentioned, see before, on chap. 7.18.

*{to worship her}* Or, *to worship,* simply: the termination of the verb here used, seeming rather to be a syllabical adjection, than a pronoun feminine affixed. Some render it, not amiss, *to idolize,* or, *make an idoll,* to wit, of her, or it; or, *to do idol-service* to her, or it: as framed for a term that is used for *an idoll,* Esay 48.5. for that which one of the Jewish doctors has, who expounds it, of *drawing figures of Idols* on the cakes they made for that superstitious service, seems not so probable: and that much less that another has, who interprets it, *to chear her,* or, *make her merry;* by an antiphrasis: for the word rather signifies *to grieve,* or, *put to pain;* whence *Jabets* had his name, 1 Chr. 4.9. and idols likewise justly theirs. See Psal. 16.4. A learned late writer, because in the Ethiopic tongue the like term signifies *to be precious,* Mar. 14.3. Luke 12.23, from thence deems that it may signify here *to make precious:* and knitting it to the next word, renders it, *in making precious, and pouring out liquors:* which he interprets, *in pouring out precious,* or, *costly liquors:* as, *he digged, and made deep,* for, *he digged deep,* Luke 6.48. That which I shall refer to the consideration of others.

**Verse 20.** *{Then Jeremiah said unto all the people, to the men, and to the women, and to all the people, which had given him that answer, saying,}* Jeremy's reply follows to this peremptory answer, acquainting them with the true cause of all the evils that had befallen them; to wit, not the neglect of their idol services, but their persisting so long in them: which though for a while sometime under some religious kings they intermitted, yet eftsoons they returned unto again, and that these their idolatrous practices, God, though he long forbore them, yet could not endure to bear ever: but at length for the same, inflicted those evils upon them, verse 21—23. Heb. *against,* upon, or, *concerning the men;* as Esay 1.1. but it is sometime used for *unto;* as chap. 26.5. and, *answered a word;* as Esay 26.36.21.

**Verse 21.** *{The incense that ye burnt in the cities of Judah, and in the streets of Jerusalem, ye and your fathers your Kings, and your Princes, and the people of the land?}* As verse 17.

*{did not the LORD remember them?}* Keep all of it in mind, to take vengeance for all together. See Esay 65.6,7. a passage from number to number; as Psal. 127.5. & 140.8. God remembered them, though they were past and gone, 2 Kings 23.26. when they thought that he had forgotten them, Hos. 7.2.

*{and came it not into his mind?}* Heb. *did it not ascend,* or, *come up, upon his heart?* as Chap. 19.5.

**Verse 22.** *{So that the LORD could no longer bear, because of the evil of your doings, and because of the abominations which ye have committed:}* Heb. *And* (as ver. 14.) *the Lord could not further bear,* (as Prov. 30.21. See Esay 1.13.) *from the face of;* as ver. 3. and so again; ver. 23. God forbore you so long, that he grew weary of bearing any longer with you, till he was weary of repenting. See ch. 15.6. and till he saw there was no remedy, 2 Chr. 36.16. See the like, Gen. 6.3,5,7.

*{therefore is your land a desolation, and an astonishment, and a curse without an inhabitant, as at this day.}* Heb. *and.* See verse 26. Chap. 26.6.

**Verse 23.** *{Because you have burnt incense, and because ye have sinned against the LORD, and have not obeyed the voice of the LORD, nor walked in his law, nor in his statutes, nor in his testimonies:}* See chap. 42.21. & 43.7. verse 3,5.

*{therefore this evil is happened unto you, as at this day.}* As verse 22. See verse 6.

**Verse 24.** *{Moreover}* Heb, *And,* as chap. 39.7. A further denunciation ratified with an oath, verse 26.28.

*{Jeremiah said unto all the people, and to all the women,}* Because the weaker sex seem to be as eager sticklers as any in this contestation with the prophet. See verse 15,19.

*{Hear the word of the LORD all Judah that are in the land of Egypt.}* As Chap. 42.15. and, *all Judah,* for, *all ye Jewes,* or, *men of Judah,* verse 27. and so verse 26.

**Verse 25.** *{Thus saith the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel:}* As verse 11.

*{saying, ye and your wives have both spoken with your mouths, and fulfilled with your hand, saying,}* You make yourselves guilty of grievous crimes, one on the neck of another, in making of wicked vows, and in making of them good, and in making account further so to do still. See chap. 3.5. Heb. *women;* as chap. 38.22,23. and *and,* for, *both;* as chap. 32.44.

*{We will surely perform our vows that we have vowed to burn incense to the Queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto her;}* Heb. *doing do;* as ver. 17. *to burn,* or, *in burning;* and so, *in pouring.* See also there.
